segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of ‘one who lives by the teaching’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhu dhammavihārī hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is a mendicant who lives by the teaching defined?”
“Mendicant, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ;
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.
But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu pariyattibahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
segs.e: That mendicant is called one who studies a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, bhikkhu yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ deseti, uttari cassa paññāya atthaṁ nappajānāti.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it. But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu paññattibahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
segs.e: That mendicant is called one who advocates a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, bhikkhu yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena sajjhāyaṁ karoti, uttari cassa paññāya atthaṁ nappajānāti.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant rehearses the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it. But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu sajjhāyabahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
segs.e: That mendicant is called one who rehearses a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, bhikkhu yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati, uttari cassa paññāya atthaṁ nappajānāti.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant thinks about and considers the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it. But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu vitakkabahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
segs.e: That mendicant is called one who thinks a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.
Take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ;
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.
And they do understand the higher meaning.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhu, bhikkhu dhammavihārī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is one who lives by the teaching.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhu, desito mayā pariyattibahulo, desito paññattibahulo, desito sajjhāyabahulo, desito vitakkabahulo, desito dhammavihārī.
segs.e: So, mendicant, I’ve taught you the one who studies a lot, the one who advocates a lot, the one who rehearses a lot, the one who thinks a lot, and the one who lives by the teaching.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, bhikkhu, satthārā karaṇīyaṁ sāvakānaṁ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṁ upādāya, kataṁ vo taṁ mayā.
segs.e: Out of sympathy, I’ve done what a teacher should do who wants what’s best for their disciples.

segs.p: Etāni, bhikkhu, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni. Jhāyatha bhikkhu, mā pamādattha, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha. Ayaṁ vo amhākaṁ anusāsanī”ti.
segs.e: Here are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, mendicant! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later! This is my instruction to you.”
Numbered Discourses 5.75
8. Warriors
Warriors (1st)
“Mendicants, these five warriors are found in the world.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco yodhājīvo rajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati na santhambhati na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ.
segs.e: Firstly, one warrior falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.
Some warriors are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the first warrior found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ;
segs.e: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust,

segs.p: api ca kho dhajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ.
segs.e: but he falters and founders at the mere sight of a banner’s crest. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.
Some warriors are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the second warrior found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ sahati dhajaggaṁ;
segs.e: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

segs.p: api ca kho ussāraṇaññeva sutvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ.
segs.e: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.
Some warriors are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the third warrior found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ;
segs.e: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil,

segs.p: api ca kho sampahāre haññati byāpajjati.
segs.e: but he’s killed or injured when blows are struck.
Some warriors are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the fourth warrior found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ, sahati sampahāraṁ.
segs.e: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil and being struck.

segs.p: So taṁ saṅgāmaṁ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṁ ajjhāvasati.
segs.e: He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.
Some warriors are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the fifth warrior found in the world.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca yodhājīvā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the five warriors found in the world.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcime yodhājīvūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā bhikkhūsu.
segs.e: In the same way, these five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
segs.e: Firstly, one monk falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.
Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.
What is his ‘cloud of dust’?
It’s when a monk hears:

segs.p: ‘amukasmiṁ nāma gāme vā nigame vā itthī vā kumārī vā abhirūpā dassanīyā pāsādikā paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā’ti.
segs.e: ‘In such-and-such village or town there’s a woman or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.’

segs.p: So taṁ sutvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
segs.e: Hearing this, he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.
Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.
This is his ‘cloud of dust’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo rajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ;
segs.e: I say that this individual is like the warrior who falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust.
Some individuals are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
segs.e: This is the first individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṁ;
segs.e: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust,

segs.p: api ca kho dhajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
segs.e: but at the mere sight of a banner’s crest he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.
Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.
What is his ‘banner’s crest’?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na heva kho suṇāti:
segs.e: It’s when a monk doesn’t hear:

segs.p: ‘amukasmiṁ nāma gāme vā nigame vā itthī vā kumārī vā abhirūpā dassanīyā pāsādikā paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā’ti;
segs.e: ‘In such-and-such village or town there’s a woman or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.’

segs.p: api ca kho sāmaṁ passati itthiṁ vā kumāriṁ vā abhirūpaṁ dassanīyaṁ pāsādikaṁ paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgataṁ.
segs.e: But he sees for himself a woman or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.

segs.p: So taṁ disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
segs.e: Seeing her, he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.
Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.
This is his ‘banner’s crest’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ;
segs.e: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust,

segs.p: api ca kho dhajaggaññeva disvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ;
segs.e: but he falters and founders at the mere sight of a banner’s crest.
Some individuals are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
segs.e: This is the second individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ;
segs.e: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

segs.p: api ca kho ussāraṇaññeva sutvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
segs.e: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.
Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.
What is his ‘turmoil’?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṁ araññagataṁ vā rukkhamūlagataṁ vā suññāgāragataṁ vā mātugāmo upasaṅkamitvā ūhasati ullapati ujjagghati uppaṇḍeti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She smiles, chats, laughs, and teases him.

segs.p: So mātugāmena ūhasiyamāno ullapiyamāno ujjagghiyamāno uppaṇḍiyamāno saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ.
segs.e: He falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.
Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.
This is his ‘turmoil’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ;
segs.e: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

segs.p: api ca kho ussāraṇaññeva sutvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ;
segs.e: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil.
Some individuals are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
segs.e: This is the third individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ;
segs.e: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil,

segs.p: api ca kho sampahāre haññati byāpajjati.
segs.e: but he’s killed or injured when blows are struck.
What is his ‘blows are struck’?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṁ araññagataṁ vā rukkhamūlagataṁ vā suññāgāragataṁ vā mātugāmo upasaṅkamitvā abhinisīdati abhinipajjati ajjhottharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She sits right by him, lies down, or embraces him.

segs.p: So mātugāmena abhinisīdiyamāno abhinipajjiyamāno ajjhotthariyamāno sikkhaṁ apaccakkhāya dubbalyaṁ anāvikatvā methunaṁ dhammaṁ paṭisevati.
segs.e: Without resigning the training and declaring his inability to continue, he indulges in sex.
This is his ‘blows are struck’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ, api ca kho sampahāre haññati byāpajjati;
segs.e: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil, but is killed or injured when blows are struck.
Some individuals are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
segs.e: This is the fourth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ, sahati sampahāraṁ, so taṁ saṅgāmaṁ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṁ ajjhāvasati.
segs.e: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil, and being struck. He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.
What is his ‘victory in battle’?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṁ araññagataṁ vā rukkhamūlagataṁ vā suññāgāragataṁ vā mātugāmo upasaṅkamitvā abhinisīdati abhinipajjati ajjhottharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She sits right by him, lies down, or embraces him.

segs.p: So mātugāmena abhinisīdiyamāno abhinipajjiyamāno ajjhotthariyamāno viniveṭhetvā vinimocetvā yena kāmaṁ pakkamati.
segs.e: But he disentangles and frees himself, and goes wherever he wants.

segs.p: So vivittaṁ senāsanaṁ bhajati araññaṁ rukkhamūlaṁ pabbataṁ kandaraṁ giriguhaṁ susānaṁ vanapatthaṁ abbhokāsaṁ palālapuñjaṁ.
segs.e: He frequents a secluded lodging—a wilderness, the root of a tree, a hill, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a forest, the open air, a heap of straw.

segs.p: So araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
segs.e: Gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, he sits down cross-legged, sets his body straight, and brings mindfulness to the present.

segs.p: So abhijjhaṁ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā viharati, abhijjhāya cittaṁ parisodheti;
segs.e: Giving up covetousness for the world, he meditates with a heart rid of covetousness, cleansing the mind of covetousness.

segs.p: byāpādapadosaṁ pahāya abyāpannacitto viharati, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī byāpādapadosā cittaṁ parisodheti;
segs.e: Giving up ill will and malevolence, he meditates with a mind rid of ill will, full of sympathy for all living beings, cleansing the mind of ill will.

segs.p: thinamiddhaṁ pahāya vigatathinamiddho viharati ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thinamiddhā cittaṁ parisodheti;
segs.e: Giving up dullness and drowsiness, he meditates with a mind rid of dullness and drowsiness, perceiving light, mindful and aware, cleansing the mind of dullness and drowsiness.

segs.p: uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahāya anuddhato viharati ajjhattaṁ vūpasantacitto, uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṁ parisodheti;
segs.e: Giving up restlessness and remorse, he meditates without restlessness, his mind settled internally, cleansing the mind of restlessness and remorse.

segs.p: vicikicchaṁ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho viharati akathaṅkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṁ parisodheti.
segs.e: Giving up doubt, he meditates having gone beyond doubt, not undecided about skillful qualities, cleansing the mind of doubt.

segs.p: So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe
segs.e: He gives up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.
Then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, he enters and remains in the first absorption …
second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.

segs.p: So evaṁ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṁ khayañāṇāya cittaṁ abhininnāmeti.
segs.e: When his mind has become immersed in samādhi like this—purified, bright, flawless, rid of corruptions, pliable, workable, steady, and imperturbable—he extends it toward knowledge of the ending of defilements.

segs.p: So ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti,
segs.e: He truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: ‘ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ āsavasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ āsavanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: He truly understands: ‘These are defilements’ … ‘This is the origin of defilements’ … ‘This is the cessation of defilements’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of defilements’.

segs.p: Tassa evaṁ jānato evaṁ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṁ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṁ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṁ vimuccati,
segs.e: Knowing and seeing like this, his mind is freed from the defilements of sensuality, desire to be reborn, and ignorance.
When he’s freed, he knows he’s freed.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.
segs.e: He understands: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’
This is his ‘victory in battle’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṁ, sahati dhajaggaṁ, sahati ussāraṇaṁ, sahati sampahāraṁ, so taṁ saṅgāmaṁ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṁ ajjhāvasati;
segs.e: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil and being struck. He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.
Some individuals are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
segs.e: This is the fifth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca yodhājīvūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā bhikkhūsū”ti.
segs.e: These five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.”
Numbered Discourses 5.76
8. Warriors
Warriors (2nd)
“Mendicants, these five warriors are found in the world.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco yodhājīvo asicammaṁ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṁ sannayhitvā viyūḷhaṁ saṅgāmaṁ otarati.
segs.e: Firstly, one warrior dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle.
He strives and struggles in the battle,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare hananti pariyāpādenti.
segs.e: but his foes kill him and finish him off.
Some warriors are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the first warrior found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo asicammaṁ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṁ sannayhitvā viyūḷhaṁ saṅgāmaṁ otarati.
segs.e: Furthermore, one warrior dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle.
He strives and struggles in the battle,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare upalikkhanti, tamenaṁ apanenti;
segs.e: but his foes wound him.
He’s carried off and taken to his relatives,

segs.p: So ñātakehi nīyamāno appatvāva ñātake antarāmagge kālaṁ karoti.
segs.e: but he dies on the road before he reaches them.
Some warriors are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the second warrior found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo asicammaṁ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṁ sannayhitvā viyūḷhaṁ saṅgāmaṁ otarati.
segs.e: Furthermore, one warrior dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle.
He strives and struggles in the battle,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare upalikkhanti, tamenaṁ apanenti;
segs.e: but his foes wound him.
He’s carried off and taken to his relatives,
who nurse him and care for him.

segs.p: So ñātakehi upaṭṭhahiyamāno paricariyamāno teneva ābādhena kālaṁ karoti.
segs.e: But he dies of his injuries while in their care.
Some warriors are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the third warrior found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo asicammaṁ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṁ sannayhitvā viyūḷhaṁ saṅgāmaṁ otarati.
segs.e: Furthermore, one warrior dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle.
He strives and struggles in the battle,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare upalikkhanti, tamenaṁ apanenti;
segs.e: but his foes wound him.
He’s carried off and taken to his relatives,
who nurse him and care for him.

segs.p: So ñātakehi upaṭṭhahiyamāno paricariyamāno vuṭṭhāti tamhā ābādhā.
segs.e: And while in their care, he recovers from his injuries.
Some warriors are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the fourth warrior found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo asicammaṁ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṁ sannayhitvā viyūḷhaṁ saṅgāmaṁ otarati.
segs.e: Furthermore, one warrior dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle.

segs.p: So taṁ saṅgāmaṁ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṁ ajjhāvasati.
segs.e: He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.
Some warriors are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo yodhājīvo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the fifth warrior found in the world.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca yodhājīvā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the five warriors found in the world.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcime yodhājīvūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā bhikkhūsu.
segs.e: In the same way, these five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā upanissāya viharati.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant lives supported by a town or village.

segs.p: So pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya tameva gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya pavisati arakkhiteneva kāyena arakkhitāya vācāya arakkhitena cittena anupaṭṭhitāya satiyā asaṁvutehi indriyehi.
segs.e: He robes up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, enters a village or town for alms without guarding body, speech, and mind, without establishing mindfulness, and without restraining the sense faculties.

segs.p: So tattha passati mātugāmaṁ dunnivatthaṁ vā duppārutaṁ vā.
segs.e: There he sees a lady scantily clad, with revealing clothes.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ mātugāmaṁ disvā dunnivatthaṁ vā duppārutaṁ vā rāgo cittaṁ anuddhaṁseti.
segs.e: Lust infects his mind,

segs.p: So rāgānuddhaṁsitena cittena sikkhaṁ apaccakkhāya dubbalyaṁ anāvikatvā methunaṁ dhammaṁ paṭisevati.
segs.e: and, without resigning the training and declaring his inability to continue, he indulges in sex.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo asicammaṁ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṁ sannayhitvā viyūḷhaṁ saṅgāmaṁ otarati, so tasmiṁ saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare hananti pariyāpādenti; tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi. Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo hoti.
segs.e: I say that this individual is like the warrior who is killed and finished off by his foes. Some individuals are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
segs.e: This is the first individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā upanissāya viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant lives supported by a town or village.

segs.p: So tattha passati mātugāmaṁ dunnivatthaṁ vā duppārutaṁ vā.

segs.e: Lust infects his mind,

segs.p: So rāgānuddhaṁsitena cittena pariḍayhateva kāyena pariḍayhati cetasā.
segs.e: and his body and mind burn with it.
He thinks:
‘Why don’t I visit the monastery and tell the monks:

segs.p: rāgapariyuṭṭhitomhi, āvuso, rāgapareto, na sakkomi brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ;
segs.e: “Reverends, I am overcome with lust, mired in lust. I am unable to keep up the spiritual life.
I declare my inability to continue training. I resign it and will return to a lesser life.”’

segs.p: So ārāmaṁ gacchanto appatvāva ārāmaṁ antarāmagge sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: But while traveling on the road, before he reaches the monastery he declares his inability to continue training. He resigns and returns to a lesser life.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo asicammaṁ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṁ sannayhitvā viyūḷhaṁ saṅgāmaṁ otarati, so tasmiṁ saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare upalikkhanti, tamenaṁ apanenti; apanetvā ñātakānaṁ nenti. So ñātakehi nīyamāno appatvāva ñātake antarāmagge kālaṁ karoti; tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi. Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo hoti.
segs.e: I say that they are like the warrior who is taken to his relatives for care, but he dies on the road before he reaches them. Some individuals are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
segs.e: This is the second individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā upanissāya viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant lives supported by a town or village.

segs.e: Lust infects his mind,

segs.p: So rāgānuddhaṁsitena cittena pariḍayhateva kāyena pariḍayhati cetasā.
segs.e: and his body and mind burn with it.
He thinks:
‘Why don’t I visit the monastery and tell the monks:

segs.p: rāgapariyuṭṭhitomhi, āvuso, rāgapareto, na sakkomi brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ;
segs.e: “Reverends, I am overcome with lust, mired in lust. I am unable to keep up the spiritual life.
I declare my inability to continue training. I resign and will return to a lesser life.”’
He goes to the monastery and tells the monks:

segs.p: ‘rāgapariyuṭṭhitomhi, āvuso, rāgapareto, na sakkomi brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ;
segs.e: ‘Reverends, I am overcome with lust, mired in lust. I am unable to keep up the spiritual life.
I declare my inability to continue training. I disavow it and will return to a lesser life.’
His spiritual companions advise and instruct him:

segs.p: ‘appassādā, āvuso, kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: ‘Reverend, the Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.

segs.p: Aṭṭhikaṅkalūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: With the similes of a skeleton …

segs.p: Maṁsapesūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: a scrap of meat …

segs.p: Tiṇukkūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: a grass torch …

segs.p: Aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: a pit of glowing coals …

segs.p: Supinakūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: a dream …

segs.p: Yācitakūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: borrowed goods …

segs.p: Rukkhaphalūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: fruit on a tree …

segs.p: Asisūnūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: a butcher’s knife and chopping board …

segs.p: Sattisūlūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: swords and spears …

segs.p: Sappasirūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: a cobra’s head, the Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.
Be happy with the spiritual life.

segs.p: māyasmā sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattī’ti.
segs.e: Venerable, please don’t declare your inability to continue training, resign it and return to a lesser life.’

segs.p: So sabrahmacārīhi evaṁ ovadiyamāno evaṁ anusāsiyamāno evamāha:
segs.e: When thus advised and instructed by his spiritual companions, he says:

segs.p: ‘kiñcāpi, āvuso, appassādā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo;
segs.e: ‘Reverends, even though the Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks,

segs.p: atha kho nevāhaṁ sakkomi brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ, sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmī’ti.
segs.e: I am unable to keep up the spiritual life. I declare my inability to continue training. I resign it and will return to a lesser life.’

segs.p: So sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: Declaring his inability to continue training, he resigns it and returns to a lesser life.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo asicammaṁ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṁ sannayhitvā viyūḷhaṁ saṅgāmaṁ otarati, so tasmiṁ saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare upalikkhanti, tamenaṁ apanenti; apanetvā ñātakānaṁ nenti, tamenaṁ ñātakā upaṭṭhahanti paricaranti. segs.e: This is the third individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā upanissāya viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant lives supported by a town or village.

segs.e: Lust infects his mind,

segs.p: So rāgānuddhaṁsitena cittena pariḍayhateva kāyena pariḍayhati cetasā.
segs.e: and his body and mind burn with it.
He thinks:
‘Why don’t I visit the monastery and tell the monks:

segs.p: rāgapariyuṭṭhitomhi, āvuso, rāgapareto, na sakkomi brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ;
segs.e: “Reverends, I am overcome with lust, mired in lust. I am unable to keep up the spiritual life.
I declare my inability to continue training. I resign it and will return to a lesser life.”’
He goes to the monastery and tells the monks:

segs.p: ‘rāgapariyuṭṭhitomhi, āvuso, rāgapareto, na sakkomi brahmacariyaṁ sandhāretuṁ;
segs.e: ‘Reverends, I am overcome with lust, mired in lust. I am unable to keep up the spiritual life.
I declare my inability to continue training. I resign it and will return to a lesser life.’
His spiritual companions advise and instruct him:

segs.p: ‘appassādā, āvuso, kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: ‘Reverend, the Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.

segs.p: Maṁsapesūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā …pe… tiṇukkūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā … aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā … supinakūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā … yācitakūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā … rukkhaphalūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā … asisūnūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā … sattisūlūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā … sappasirūpamā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo.
segs.e: a scrap of meat … a grass torch … a pit of glowing coals … a dream … borrowed goods … fruit on a tree … a butcher’s knife and chopping board … swords and spears … a cobra’s head, the Buddha says that sensual pleasures give little gratification and much suffering and distress, and they are all the more full of drawbacks.
Be happy with the spiritual life.

segs.p: māyasmā sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattī’ti.
segs.e: Venerable, please don’t declare your inability to continue training, resign it and return to a lesser life.’

segs.p: So sabrahmacārīhi evaṁ ovadiyamāno evaṁ anusāsiyamāno evamāha:
segs.e: When thus advised and instructed by his spiritual companions, he says:
‘I’ll make an attempt, reverends, I’ll struggle, I’ll be happy.

segs.p: Na dānāhaṁ, āvuso, sikkhādubbalyaṁ āvikatvā sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissāmī’ti.
segs.e: I won’t now declare my inability to continue training, resign it and return to a lesser life.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo asicammaṁ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṁ sannayhitvā viyūḷhaṁ saṅgāmaṁ otarati, so tasmiṁ saṅgāme ussahati vāyamati, tamenaṁ ussahantaṁ vāyamantaṁ pare upalikkhanti, tamenaṁ apanenti; apanetvā ñātakānaṁ nenti, tamenaṁ ñātakā upaṭṭhahanti paricaranti. Some individuals are like that.

segs.e: This is the fourth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

segs.p: So pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya tameva gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya pavisati rakkhiteneva kāyena rakkhitāya vācāya rakkhitena cittena upaṭṭhitāya satiyā saṁvutehi indriyehi.
segs.e: He robes up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, enters a village or town, guarding body, speech, and mind, establishing mindfulness, and restraining the sense faculties.

segs.p: So cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.
segs.e: Seeing a sight with his eyes, he doesn’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ cakkhundriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati; rakkhati cakkhundriyaṁ; cakkhundriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, he practices restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving its restraint.
Hearing a sound with his ears …
Smelling an odor with his nose …
Tasting a flavor with his tongue …
Encountering a touch with his body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.
segs.e: Knowing an idea with his mind, he doesn’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ manindriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati; rakkhati manindriyaṁ; manindriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, he practices restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.
Then after the meal, on his return from almsround,

segs.p: vivittaṁ senāsanaṁ bhajati araññaṁ rukkhamūlaṁ pabbataṁ kandaraṁ giriguhaṁ susānaṁ vanapatthaṁ abbhokāsaṁ palālapuñjaṁ.
segs.e: he frequents a secluded lodging—a wilderness, the root of a tree, a hill, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a forest, the open air, a heap of straw.

segs.p: So araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
segs.e: Gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, he sits down cross-legged, sets his body straight, and brings mindfulness to the present.

segs.p: So abhijjhaṁ loke pahāya …pe… so ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe
segs.e: He gives up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.

segs.p: vivicceva kāmehi …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, he enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.

segs.p: So evaṁ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṁ khayañāṇāya cittaṁ abhininnāmeti.
segs.e: When his mind has become immersed in samādhi like this—purified, bright, flawless, rid of corruptions, pliable, workable, steady, and imperturbable—he extends it toward knowledge of the ending of defilements.

He truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’. He truly understands: ‘These are defilements’ … ‘This is the origin of defilements’ … ‘This is the cessation of defilements’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of defilements’. Knowing and seeing like this, his mind is freed from the defilements of sensuality, desire to be reborn, and ignorance. When he’s freed, he knows he’s freed.
He understands: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo asicammaṁ gahetvā dhanukalāpaṁ sannayhitvā viyūḷhaṁ saṅgāmaṁ otarati, so taṁ saṅgāmaṁ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṁ ajjhāvasati; tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: I say that this individual is like the warrior who dons his sword and shield, fastens his bow and arrows, and plunges into the thick of battle. He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.
Some individuals are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṁvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
segs.e: This is the fifth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca yodhājīvūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā bhikkhūsū”ti.
segs.e: These five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.”
Numbered Discourses 5.77
8. Warriors
Future Perils (1st)

segs.p: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, anāgatabhayāni sampassamānena alameva āraññikena bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, seeing these five future perils is quite enough for a wilderness mendicant to meditate diligently, keenly, and resolutely for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, āraññiko bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Firstly, a wilderness mendicant reflects:
‘Currently I’m living alone in a wilderness.

segs.p: Ekakaṁ kho pana maṁ araññe viharantaṁ
segs.e: While living here alone

segs.p: ahi vā maṁ ḍaṁseyya, vicchiko vā maṁ ḍaṁseyya, satapadī vā maṁ ḍaṁseyya,
segs.e: I might get bitten by a snake, a scorpion, or a centipede.

segs.p: tena me assa kālaṅkiriyā, so mamassa antarāyo;
segs.e: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

segs.p: handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā’ti.
segs.e: I’d better rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ sampassamānena alameva āraññikena bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: This is the first future peril …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, āraññiko bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a wilderness mendicant reflects:
‘Currently I’m living alone in a wilderness.
While living here alone

segs.p: upakkhalitvā vā papateyyaṁ, bhattaṁ vā bhuttaṁ me byāpajjeyya, pittaṁ vā me kuppeyya, semhaṁ vā me kuppeyya, satthakā vā me vātā kuppeyyuṁ,
segs.e: I might stumble off a cliff, or get food poisoning, or suffer a disturbance of bile, phlegm, or piercing winds.

segs.p: tena me assa kālaṅkiriyā, so mamassa antarāyo;
segs.e: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

segs.p: handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā’ti.
segs.e: I’d better rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ sampassamānena alameva āraññikena bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: This is the second future peril …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, āraññiko bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a wilderness mendicant reflects:
‘Currently I’m living alone in a wilderness.
While living here alone

segs.p: vāḷehi samāgaccheyyaṁ, sīhena vā byagghena vā dīpinā vā acchena vā taracchena vā, te maṁ jīvitā voropeyyuṁ,
segs.e: I might encounter wild beasts—a lion, a tiger, a leopard, a bear, or a hyena—which might take my life.

segs.p: tena me assa kālaṅkiriyā, so mamassa antarāyo;
segs.e: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

segs.p: handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā’ti.
segs.e: I’d better rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ sampassamānena alameva āraññikena bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: This is the third future peril …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, āraññiko bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a wilderness mendicant reflects:
‘Currently I’m living alone in a wilderness.
While living here alone

segs.p: māṇavehi samāgaccheyyaṁ katakammehi vā akatakammehi vā, te maṁ jīvitā voropeyyuṁ,
segs.e: I might encounter youths escaping a crime or on their way to commit one, and they might take my life.

segs.p: tena me assa kālaṅkiriyā, so mamassa antarāyo;
segs.e: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

segs.p: handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā’ti.
segs.e: I’d better rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, catutthaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ sampassamānena alameva āraññikena bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: This is the fourth future peril …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, āraññiko bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a wilderness mendicant reflects:
‘Currently I’m living alone in a wilderness.

segs.p: Santi kho panāraññe vāḷā amanussā, te maṁ jīvitā voropeyyuṁ,
segs.e: But in a wilderness there are savage monsters who might take my life.

segs.p: tena me assa kālaṅkiriyā, so mamassa antarāyo;
segs.e: And if I died from that it would be an obstacle to my progress.

segs.p: handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā’ti.
segs.e: I’d better rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ sampassamānena alameva āraññikena bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: This is the fifth future peril …

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca anāgatabhayāni sampassamānena alameva āraññikena bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five future perils, seeing which is quite enough for a wilderness mendicant to meditate diligently, keenly, and resolutely for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.”
Numbered Discourses 5.78
8. Warriors
Future Perils (2nd)

segs.p: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, anāgatabhayāni sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, seeing these five future perils is quite enough for a mendicant to meditate diligently, keenly, and resolutely for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
What five?
A mendicant reflects:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho etarahi daharo yuvā susukāḷakeso bhadrena yobbanena samannāgato paṭhamena vayasā.
segs.e: ‘Currently I’m a youth, young, with pristine black hair, blessed with youth, in the prime of life.

segs.p: Hoti kho pana so samayo yaṁ imaṁ kāyaṁ jarā phusati.
segs.e: But there will come a time when this body is struck with old age.

segs.p: Jiṇṇena kho pana jarāya abhibhūtena na sukaraṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasi kātuṁ, na sukarāni araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevituṁ.
segs.e: When you’re old, overcome by old age, it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas, and it’s not easy to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: Purā maṁ so dhammo āgacchati aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo;
segs.e: Before that unlikable, undesirable, and disagreeable thing happens,

segs.p: handāhaṁ paṭikacceva vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya, yenāhaṁ dhammena samannāgato jiṇṇakopi phāsuṁ viharissāmī’ti.
segs.e: I’d better preempt it by rousing up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized. That way, when it happens, I’ll live comfortably even though I’m old.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: This is the first future peril …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant reflects:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho etarahi appābādho appātaṅko samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya majjhimāya padhānakkhamāya.
segs.e: ‘Currently, I’m rarely ill or unwell. My stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold, but just right, and fit for meditation.

segs.p: Hoti kho pana so samayo yaṁ imaṁ kāyaṁ byādhi phusati.
segs.e: But there will come a time when this body is struck with sickness.

segs.p: Byādhitena kho pana byādhinā abhibhūtena na sukaraṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasi kātuṁ, na sukarāni araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevituṁ.
segs.e: When you’re sick, overcome by sickness, it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas, and it’s not easy to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: Purā maṁ so dhammo āgacchati aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo;
segs.e: Before that unlikable, undesirable, and disagreeable thing happens,

segs.p: handāhaṁ paṭikacceva vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya, yenāhaṁ dhammena samannāgato byādhitopi phāsuṁ viharissāmī’ti.
segs.e: I’d better preempt it by rousing up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized. That way, when it happens, I’ll live comfortably even though I’m sick.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: This is the second future peril …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant reflects:

segs.p: ‘etarahi kho subhikkhaṁ susassaṁ sulabhapiṇḍaṁ, sukaraṁ uñchena paggahena yāpetuṁ.
segs.e: ‘Currently, there’s plenty of food, a good harvest, so it’s easy to get almsfood, and easy to keep going by collecting alms.

segs.p: Hoti kho pana so samayo yaṁ dubbhikkhaṁ hoti dussassaṁ dullabhapiṇḍaṁ, na sukaraṁ uñchena paggahena yāpetuṁ.
segs.e: But there will come a time of famine, a bad harvest, when it’s hard to get almsfood, and not easy to keep going by collecting alms.

segs.p: Dubbhikkhe kho pana manussā yena subhikkhaṁ tena saṅkamanti.
segs.e: In a time of famine, people move to where there’s plenty of food,
where they live crowded and cramped together.

segs.p: Saṅgaṇikavihāre kho pana sati ākiṇṇavihāre na sukaraṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasi kātuṁ, na sukarāni araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevituṁ.
segs.e: When you live crowded and cramped together, it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas, and it’s not easy to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: Purā maṁ so dhammo āgacchati aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo;
segs.e: Before that unlikable, undesirable, and disagreeable thing happens,

segs.p: handāhaṁ paṭikacceva vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya, yenāhaṁ dhammena samannāgato dubbhikkhepi phāsu viharissāmī’ti.
segs.e: I’d better preempt it by rousing up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized. That way, when it happens, I’ll live comfortably even though there’s a famine.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: This is the third future peril …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant reflects:

segs.p: ‘etarahi kho manussā samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṁ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharanti.
segs.e: ‘Currently, people live in harmony, appreciating each other, without dispute, blending like milk and water, and regarding each other with kindly eyes.

segs.p: Hoti kho pana so samayo yaṁ bhayaṁ hoti aṭavisaṅkopo, cakkasamārūḷhā jānapadā pariyāyanti.
segs.e: But there will come a time of peril due to turmoil in the wilds, so the countryfolk mount their vehicles and flee everywhere.

segs.p: Bhaye kho pana sati manussā yena khemaṁ tena saṅkamanti.
segs.e: In a time of peril, people move to where there’s sanctuary,
where they live crowded and cramped together.

segs.p: Saṅgaṇikavihāre kho pana sati ākiṇṇavihāre na sukaraṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasi kātuṁ, na sukarāni araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevituṁ.
segs.e: When you live crowded and cramped together, it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas, and it’s not easy to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: Purā maṁ so dhammo āgacchati aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo;
segs.e: Before that unlikable, undesirable, and disagreeable thing happens,

segs.p: handāhaṁ paṭikacceva vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya, yenāhaṁ dhammena samannāgato bhayepi phāsuṁ viharissāmī’ti.
segs.e: I’d better preempt it by rousing up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized. That way, when it happens, I’ll live comfortably even in a time of peril.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, catutthaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: This is the fourth future peril …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant reflects:

segs.p: ‘etarahi kho saṅgho samaggo sammodamāno avivadamāno ekuddeso phāsu viharati.
segs.e: ‘Currently, the Saṅgha lives comfortably, in harmony, appreciating each other, without dispute, with one recitation.

segs.p: Hoti kho pana so samayo yaṁ saṅgho bhijjati.
segs.e: But there will come a time of schism in the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Saṅghe kho pana bhinne na sukaraṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasi kātuṁ, na sukarāni araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevituṁ.
segs.e: When there is schism in the Saṅgha, it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas, and it’s not easy to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: Purā maṁ so dhammo āgacchati aniṭṭho akanto amanāpo;
segs.e: Before that unlikable, undesirable, and disagreeable thing happens,

segs.p: handāhaṁ paṭikacceva vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya, yenāhaṁ dhammena samannāgato bhinnepi saṅghe phāsuṁ viharissāmī’ti.
segs.e: I’d better preempt it by rousing up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized. That way, when it happens, I’ll live comfortably even though there’s schism in the Saṅgha.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: This is the fifth future peril …

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca anāgatabhayāni sampassamānena alameva bhikkhunā appamattena ātāpinā pahitattena viharituṁ appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five future perils, seeing which is quite enough for a mendicant to meditate diligently, keenly, and resolutely for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.”
Numbered Discourses 5.79
8. Warriors
Future Perils (3rd)

segs.p: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, anāgatabhayāni etarahi asamuppannāni āyatiṁ samuppajjissanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these five future perils have not currently arisen, but they will arise in the future.
You should look out for them
and try to give them up.
What five?

segs.p: Bhavissanti, bhikkhave, bhikkhū anāgatamaddhānaṁ abhāvitakāyā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā.
segs.e: In a future time there will be mendicants who have not developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Te abhāvitakāyā samānā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā aññe upasampādessanti.
segs.e: They will ordain others,

segs.p: Tepi na sakkhissanti vinetuṁ adhisīle adhicitte adhipaññāya.
segs.e: but be unable to guide them in the higher ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Tepi bhavissanti abhāvitakāyā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā.
segs.e: They too will not develop their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Te abhāvitakāyā samānā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā aññe upasampādessanti.
segs.e: They too will ordain others,

segs.p: Tepi na sakkhissanti vinetuṁ adhisīle adhicitte adhipaññāya.
segs.e: but be unable to guide them in the higher ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Tepi bhavissanti abhāvitakāyā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā.
segs.e: They too will not develop their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.
And that is how corrupt training comes from corrupt teachings,
and corrupt teachings come from corrupt training.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ etarahi asamuppannaṁ āyatiṁ samuppajjissati.
segs.e: This is the first future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhavissanti bhikkhū anāgatamaddhānaṁ abhāvitakāyā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā.
segs.e: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who have not developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Te abhāvitakāyā samānā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā aññesaṁ nissayaṁ dassanti.
segs.e: They will give dependence to others,

segs.p: Tepi na sakkhissanti vinetuṁ adhisīle adhicitte adhipaññāya.
segs.e: but be unable to guide them in the higher ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Tepi bhavissanti abhāvitakāyā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā.
segs.e: They too will not develop their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Te abhāvitakāyā samānā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā aññesaṁ nissayaṁ dassanti.
segs.e: They too will give dependence to others,

segs.p: Tepi na sakkhissanti vinetuṁ adhisīle adhicitte adhipaññāya.
segs.e: but be unable to guide them in the higher ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Tepi bhavissanti abhāvitakāyā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā.
segs.e: They too will not develop their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.
And that is how corrupt training comes from corrupt teachings,
and corrupt teachings come from corrupt training.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ etarahi asamuppannaṁ āyatiṁ samuppajjissati.
segs.e: This is the second future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhavissanti bhikkhū anāgatamaddhānaṁ abhāvitakāyā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā.
segs.e: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who have not developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Te abhāvitakāyā samānā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā abhidhammakathaṁ vedallakathaṁ kathentā kaṇhadhammaṁ okkamamānā na bujjhissanti.
segs.e: In discussion about the teachings and elaborations they’ll fall into dark ideas without realizing it.
And that is how corrupt training comes from corrupt teachings,
and corrupt teachings come from corrupt training.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ etarahi asamuppannaṁ āyatiṁ samuppajjissati.
segs.e: This is the third future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhavissanti bhikkhū anāgatamaddhānaṁ abhāvitakāyā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā.
segs.e: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who have not developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Te abhāvitakāyā samānā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā ye te suttantā tathāgatabhāsitā gambhīrā gambhīratthā lokuttarā suññatāppaṭisaṁyuttā, tesu bhaññamānesu na sussūsissanti, na sotaṁ odahissanti, na aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapessanti, na ca te dhamme uggahetabbaṁ pariyāpuṇitabbaṁ maññissanti.
segs.e: When discourses spoken by the Realized One—deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with emptiness—are being recited they won’t want to listen. They won’t actively listen or try to understand, nor will they think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing.

segs.p: Ye pana te suttantā kavitā kāveyyā cittakkharā cittabyañjanā bāhirakā sāvakabhāsitā, tesu bhaññamānesu sussūsissanti, sotaṁ odahissanti, aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapessanti, te ca dhamme uggahetabbaṁ pariyāpuṇitabbaṁ maññissanti.
segs.e: But when discourses composed by poets—poetry, with fancy words and phrases, composed by outsiders or spoken by disciples—are being recited they will want to listen. They’ll actively listen and try to understand, and they’ll think those teachings are worth learning and memorizing.
And that is how corrupt training comes from corrupt teachings,
and corrupt teachings come from corrupt training.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, catutthaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ etarahi asamuppannaṁ āyatiṁ samuppajjissati.
segs.e: This is the fourth future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhavissanti bhikkhū anāgatamaddhānaṁ abhāvitakāyā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā.
segs.e: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who have not developed their physical endurance, ethics, mind, and wisdom.

segs.p: Te abhāvitakāyā samānā abhāvitasīlā abhāvitacittā abhāvitapaññā therā bhikkhū bāhulikā bhavissanti sāthalikā okkamane pubbaṅgamā paviveke nikkhittadhurā, na vīriyaṁ ārabhissanti appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: The senior mendicants will be indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion, not rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
Those who come after them will follow their example.

segs.p: Sāpi bhavissati bāhulikā sāthalikā okkamane pubbaṅgamā paviveke nikkhittadhurā, na vīriyaṁ ārabhissati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: They too will become indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion, not rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
And that is how corrupt training comes from corrupt teachings,
and corrupt teachings come from corrupt training.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ etarahi asamuppannaṁ āyatiṁ samuppajjissati.
segs.e: This is the fifth future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca anāgatabhayāni etarahi asamuppannāni āyatiṁ samuppajjissanti.
segs.e: These are the five future perils that have not currently arisen, but will arise in the future.
You should look out for them,
and try to give them up.”
Numbered Discourses 5.80
8. Warriors
Future Perils (4th)

segs.p: “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, anāgatabhayāni etarahi asamuppannāni āyatiṁ samuppajjissanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these five future perils have not currently arisen, but they will arise in the future.
You should look out for them
and try to give them up.
What five?

segs.p: Bhavissanti, bhikkhave, bhikkhū anāgatamaddhānaṁ cīvare kalyāṇakāmā.
segs.e: In a future time there will be mendicants who like nice robes.

segs.p: Te cīvare kalyāṇakāmā samānā riñcissanti paṁsukūlikattaṁ, riñcissanti araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni;
segs.e: They will neglect the practice of wearing rag robes and the practice of frequenting remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: gāmanigamarājadhānīsu osaritvā vāsaṁ kappessanti, cīvarahetu ca anekavihitaṁ anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjissanti.
segs.e: They will come down to the villages, towns, and capital cities and make their homes there. And they will employ many kinds of improper solicitation for the sake of a robe.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ etarahi asamuppannaṁ āyatiṁ samuppajjissati.
segs.e: This is the first future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhavissanti bhikkhū anāgatamaddhānaṁ piṇḍapāte kalyāṇakāmā.
segs.e: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who like nice almsfood.

segs.p: Te piṇḍapāte kalyāṇakāmā samānā riñcissanti piṇḍapātikattaṁ, riñcissanti araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni;
segs.e: They will neglect the practice of walking for almsfood and the practice of frequenting remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: gāmanigamarājadhānīsu osaritvā vāsaṁ kappessanti jivhaggena rasaggāni pariyesamānā, piṇḍapātahetu ca anekavihitaṁ anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjissanti.
segs.e: They will come down to the villages, towns, and capital cities and make their home there. And they will employ many kinds of improper solicitation for the sake of almsfood.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ etarahi asamuppannaṁ āyatiṁ samuppajjissati.
segs.e: This is the second future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhavissanti bhikkhū anāgatamaddhānaṁ senāsane kalyāṇakāmā.
segs.e: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who like nice lodgings.

segs.p: Te senāsane kalyāṇakāmā samānā riñcissanti rukkhamūlikattaṁ, riñcissanti araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni;
segs.e: They will neglect the practice of staying at the root of a tree and the practice of frequenting remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: gāmanigamarājadhānīsu osaritvā vāsaṁ kappessanti, senāsanahetu ca anekavihitaṁ anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjissanti.
segs.e: They will come down to the villages, towns, and capital cities and make their home there. And they will employ many kinds of improper solicitation for the sake of lodgings.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ etarahi asamuppannaṁ āyatiṁ samuppajjissati.
segs.e: This is the third future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhavissanti bhikkhū anāgatamaddhānaṁ bhikkhunīsikkhamānāsamaṇuddesehi saṁsaṭṭhā viharissanti.
segs.e: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who mix closely with nuns, trainee nuns, and novice nuns.

segs.p: Bhikkhunīsikkhamānāsamaṇuddesehi saṁsagge kho pana, bhikkhave, sati etaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
segs.e: In such conditions, it can be expected that

segs.p: ‘anabhiratā vā brahmacariyaṁ carissanti, aññataraṁ vā saṅkiliṭṭhaṁ āpattiṁ āpajjissanti, sikkhaṁ vā paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissanti’.
segs.e: they will lead the spiritual life dissatisfied, or commit one of the corrupt offenses, or resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, catutthaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ etarahi asamuppannaṁ āyatiṁ samuppajjissati.
segs.e: This is the fourth future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhavissanti bhikkhū anāgatamaddhānaṁ ārāmikasamaṇuddesehi saṁsaṭṭhā viharissanti.
segs.e: Furthermore, in a future time there will be mendicants who mix closely with monastery attendants and novices.

segs.p: Ārāmikasamaṇuddesehi saṁsagge kho pana, bhikkhave, sati etaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
segs.e: In such conditions it can be expected that

segs.p: ‘anekavihitaṁ sannidhikāraparibhogaṁ anuyuttā viharissanti, oḷārikampi nimittaṁ karissanti, pathaviyāpi haritaggepi’.
segs.e: they will engage in storing up goods for their own use, and making obvious hints about digging the earth and cutting plants.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamaṁ anāgatabhayaṁ etarahi asamuppannaṁ āyatiṁ samuppajjissati.
segs.e: This is the fifth future peril that has not currently arisen, but will arise in the future …

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca anāgatabhayāni etarahi asamuppannāni āyatiṁ samuppajjissanti.
segs.e: These are the five future perils that have not currently arisen, but will arise in the future.
You should look out for them
and try to give them up.”
Numbered Discourses 5.81
9. Senior Mendicants
Desirable

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant with five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.
What five?

segs.p: Rajanīye rajjati, dussanīye dussati, mohanīye muyhati, kuppanīye kuppati, madanīye majjati—
segs.e: They desire the desirable, they hate the hateful, they’re deluded by the delusory, they’re annoyed by the annoying, and they’re intoxicated by the intoxicating.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is disliked and disagreeable by their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
What five?

segs.p: Rajanīye na rajjati, dussanīye na dussati, mohanīye na muyhati, kuppanīye na kuppati, madanīye na majjati—
segs.e: They don’t desire the desirable, they don’t hate the hateful, they’re not deluded by the delusory, they’re not annoyed by the annoying, and they’re not intoxicated by the intoxicating.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
Numbered Discourses 5.82
9. Senior Mendicants
Free of Greed

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant with five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.
What five?

segs.p: Avītarāgo hoti, avītadoso hoti, avītamoho hoti, makkhī ca, paḷāsī ca—
segs.e: They’re not free of greed, hate, and delusion; they are offensive and contemptuous.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
What five?

segs.p: Vītarāgo hoti, vītadoso hoti, vītamoho hoti, amakkhī ca, apaḷāsī ca—
segs.e: They’re free of greed, hate, and delusion; they’re not offensive and contemptuous.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
Numbered Discourses 5.83
9. Senior Mendicants
Deceiver

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant with five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.
What five?

segs.p: Kuhako ca hoti, lapako ca, nemittiko ca, nippesiko ca, lābhena ca lābhaṁ nijigīsitā—
segs.e: They use deceit, flattery, hinting, and belittling, and they use material things to chase after other material things.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
What five?

segs.p: Na ca kuhako hoti, na ca lapako, na ca nemittiko, na ca nippesiko, na ca lābhena lābhaṁ nijigīsitā—
segs.e: They don’t use deceit, flattery, hinting, or belittling, and they don’t use material things to chase after other material things.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
Numbered Discourses 5.84
9. Senior Mendicants
Faithless

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti, amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant with five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.
What five?

segs.p: Assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, kusīto hoti, duppañño hoti—
segs.e: They’re faithless, shameless, imprudent, lazy, and witless.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
What five?

segs.p: Saddho hoti, hirīmā hoti, ottappī hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, paññavā hoti—
segs.e: They’re faithful, conscientious, prudent, energetic, and wise.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
Numbered Discourses 5.85
9. Senior Mendicants
Cannot Endure

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant with five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.
What five?

segs.p: Akkhamo hoti rūpānaṁ, akkhamo saddānaṁ, akkhamo gandhānaṁ, akkhamo rasānaṁ, akkhamo phoṭṭhabbānaṁ—
segs.e: They can’t endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is disliked and disagreeable to their spiritual companions, not respected or admired.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
What five?

segs.p: Khamo hoti rūpānaṁ, khamo saddānaṁ, khamo gandhānaṁ, khamo rasānaṁ, khamo phoṭṭhabbānaṁ—
segs.e: They can endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
Numbered Discourses 5.86
9. Senior Mendicants
Attaining the Methods of Textual Analysis

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
What five?

segs.p: Atthapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, dhammapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, niruttipaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti,
segs.e: They have attained the textual analysis of meaning, text, definition, and eloquence.

segs.p: yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṁ uccāvacāni kiṅkaraṇīyāni tattha dakkho hoti analaso tatrupāyāya vīmaṁsāya samannāgato alaṁ kātuṁ alaṁ saṁvidhātuṁ—
segs.e: And they are deft and tireless in a diverse spectrum of duties for their spiritual companions, understanding how to go about things in order to complete and organize the work.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
Numbered Discourses 5.87
9. Senior Mendicants
Ethical

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “A senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
What five?

segs.p: Sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati. Ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu;
segs.e: They’re ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā;
segs.e: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segs.p: kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā;
segs.e: They’re a good speaker who enunciates well, with a polished, clear, and articulate voice that expresses the meaning.

segs.p: catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī;
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
Numbered Discourses 5.88
9. Senior Mendicants
Senior Mendicants

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu bahujanaahitāya paṭipanno hoti bahujanaasukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a senior mendicant who has five qualities is acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of of gods and humans.
What five?
They are long standing and have long gone forth.
They’re well-known, famous, with a large following that includes both laypeople and renunciates.
They receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā appaṭividdhā;
segs.e: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segs.p: micchādiṭṭhiko hoti viparītadassano, so bahujanaṁ saddhammā vuṭṭhāpetvā asaddhamme patiṭṭhāpeti.
segs.e: But they have wrong view and distorted perspective. They draw many people away from the true teaching and establish them in false teachings.

segs.p: Thero bhikkhu rattaññū cirapabbajito itipissa diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjanti, ñāto thero bhikkhu yasassī sagahaṭṭhapabbajitānaṁ bahujanaparivāro itipissa diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjanti, lābhī thero bhikkhu cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ itipissa diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjanti, bahussuto thero bhikkhu sutadharo sutasannicayo itipissa diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjanti.
segs.e: People follow their example, thinking that the senior mendicant is long standing and has long gone forth. Or that they’re well-known, famous, with a large following that includes both laypeople and renunciates. Or that they receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. Or that they’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned.
