segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu bahujanaahitāya paṭipanno hoti bahujanaasukhāya bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: A senior mendicant who possesses these five qualities is acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu bahujanahitāya paṭipanno hoti bahujanasukhāya bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: A senior mendicant who has five qualities is acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
What five?
They are long standing and have long gone forth.
They’re well-known, famous, with a large following, including both laypeople and renunciates.
They receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā;
segs.e: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhiko hoti aviparītadassano, so bahujanaṁ asaddhammā vuṭṭhāpetvā saddhamme patiṭṭhāpeti.
segs.e: And they have right view and an undistorted perspective. They draw many people away from false teachings and establish them in the true teaching.

segs.p: Thero bhikkhu rattaññū cirapabbajito itipissa diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjanti, ñāto thero bhikkhu yasassī sagahaṭṭhapabbajitānaṁ bahujanaparivāro itipissa diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjanti, lābhī thero bhikkhu cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ itipissa diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjanti, bahussuto thero bhikkhu sutadharo sutasannicayo itipissa diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjanti.
segs.e: People follow their example, thinking that the senior mendicant is long standing and has long gone forth. Or that they’re well-known, famous, with a large following that includes both laypeople and renunciates. Or that they receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. Or that they’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu bahujanahitāya paṭipanno hoti bahujanasukhāya bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānan”ti.
segs.e: A senior mendicant who possesses these five qualities is acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”
Numbered Discourses 5.89
9. Senior Mendicants
A Trainee (1st)

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “These five things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.
What five?

segs.p: Kammārāmatā, bhassārāmatā, niddārāmatā, saṅgaṇikārāmatā, yathāvimuttaṁ cittaṁ na paccavekkhati—
segs.e: They relish work, talk, sleep, and company. And they don’t review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.
What five?

segs.p: Na kammārāmatā, na bhassārāmatā, na niddārāmatā, na saṅgaṇikārāmatā, yathāvimuttaṁ cittaṁ paccavekkhati—
segs.e: They don’t relish work, talk, sleep, and company. And they review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.”
Numbered Discourses 5.90
9. Senior Mendicants
A Trainee (2nd)

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “These five things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu bahukicco hoti bahukaraṇīyo viyatto kiṅkaraṇīyesu;
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant trainee has many duties and responsibilities, and is competent in many tasks.
They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo dhammo sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the first thing that leads to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu appamattakena kammena divasaṁ atināmeti;
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee spends too much time doing trivial work.
They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo dhammo sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the second thing that leads to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu saṁsaṭṭho viharati gahaṭṭhapabbajitehi ananulomikena gihisaṁsaggena;
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee mixes closely with laypeople and renunciates, socializing inappropriately like a layperson.
They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo dhammo sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the third thing that leads to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu akālena gāmaṁ pavisati, atidivā paṭikkamati;
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee enters the town at the wrong time, and returns too late in the day.
They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho dhammo sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fourth thing that leads to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu yāyaṁ kathā ābhisallekhikā cetovivaraṇasappāyā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee doesn’t get to take part in talk about self-effacement that helps open the heart, when they want, without trouble or difficulty. That is,

segs.p: appicchakathā santuṭṭhikathā pavivekakathā asaṁsaggakathā vīriyārambhakathā sīlakathā samādhikathā paññākathā vimuttikathā vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā, evarūpiyā kathāya na nikāmalābhī hoti na akicchalābhī na akasiralābhī;
segs.e: talk about fewness of wishes, contentment, seclusion, aloofness, arousing energy, ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.
They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo dhammo sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fifth thing that leads to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu na bahukicco hoti na bahukaraṇīyo viyatto kiṅkaraṇīyesu;
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant trainee doesn’t have many duties and responsibilities, even though they are competent in many tasks.

segs.p: na riñcati paṭisallānaṁ, anuyuñjati ajjhattaṁ cetosamathaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t neglect retreat, and are committed to internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo dhammo sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the first thing that doesn’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu na appamattakena kammena divasaṁ atināmeti;
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee doesn’t waste their day doing trivial work.

segs.p: na riñcati paṭisallānaṁ, anuyuñjati ajjhattaṁ cetosamathaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t neglect retreat, and are committed to internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo dhammo sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the second thing that doesn’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu asaṁsaṭṭho viharati gahaṭṭhapabbajitehi ananulomikena gihisaṁsaggena;
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee doesn’t mix closely with laypeople and renunciates, socializing inappropriately like a layperson.

segs.p: na riñcati paṭisallānaṁ, anuyuñjati ajjhattaṁ cetosamathaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t neglect retreat, and are committed to internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo dhammo sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the third thing that doesn’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu na atikālena gāmaṁ pavisati, nātidivā paṭikkamati;
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee doesn’t enter the village too early or return too late in the day.

segs.p: na riñcati paṭisallānaṁ, anuyuñjati ajjhattaṁ cetosamathaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t neglect retreat, and are committed to internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho dhammo sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fourth thing that doesn’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu yāyaṁ kathā ābhisallekhikā cetovivaraṇasappāyā, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant trainee gets to take part in talk about self-effacement that helps open the heart, when they want, without trouble or difficulty. That is,

segs.p: appicchakathā santuṭṭhikathā pavivekakathā asaṁsaggakathā vīriyārambhakathā sīlakathā samādhikathā paññākathā vimuttikathā vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā, evarūpiyā kathāya nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī;
segs.e: talk about fewness of wishes, contentment, seclusion, aloofness, arousing energy, ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: na riñcati paṭisallānaṁ, anuyuñjati ajjhattaṁ cetosamathaṁ.
segs.e: They don’t neglect retreat, and are committed to internal serenity of heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo dhammo sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fifth thing that doesn’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā sekhassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant trainee.”
Numbered Discourses 5.91
10. With Kakudha
Accomplishments (1st)
“Mendicants, there are five accomplishments.
What five?
Accomplishment in faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.
These are the five accomplishments.”
Numbered Discourses 5.92
10. With Kakudha
Accomplishment (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are five accomplishments.
What five?
Accomplishment in ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.
These are the five accomplishments.”
Numbered Discourses 5.93
10. With Kakudha
Declarations
“Mendicants, there are five ways of declaring enlightenment.
What five?
One declares enlightenment out of stupidity and folly.
Or because of corrupt wishes, being of wishful temperament.
Or because of madness and mental disorder.
Or out of overestimation.
Or one declares enlightenment rightly.
These are the five ways of declaring enlightenment.”
Numbered Discourses 5.94
10. With Kakudha
Living Comfortably
“Mendicants, there are these five ways of living comfortably.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ … tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ … catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption …

segs.p: āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.
These are the five ways of living comfortably.”
Numbered Discourses 5.95
10. With Kakudha
Unshakable

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu nacirasseva akuppaṁ paṭivijjhati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant who has five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, dhammapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, niruttipaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāpatto hoti, yathāvimuttaṁ cittaṁ paccavekkhati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant has attained the textual analysis of meaning, text, definition, and eloquence, and they review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu nacirasseva akuppaṁ paṭivijjhatī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who has these five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.”
Numbered Discourses 5.96
10. With Kakudha
Remembering What You’ve Learned

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu ānāpānassatiṁ āsevanto nacirasseva akuppaṁ paṭivijjhati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant cultivating mindfulness of breathing who has five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appaṭṭho hoti appakicco subharo susantoso jīvitaparikkhāresu;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant has few obligations and duties, and is unburdensome and contented with life’s necessities.
They eat little, not devoted to filling their stomach.
They are rarely drowsy, and are dedicated to wakefulness.

segs.p: bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā;
segs.e: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.
They review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu ānāpānassatiṁ āsevanto nacirasseva akuppaṁ paṭivijjhatī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant cultivating mindfulness of breathing who has these five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.”
Numbered Discourses 5.97
10. With Kakudha
Talk

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu ānāpānassatiṁ bhāvento nacirasseva akuppaṁ paṭivijjhati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant developing mindfulness of breathing who has five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appaṭṭho hoti appakicco subharo susantoso jīvitaparikkhāresu;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant has few concerns and duties, and is unburdensome and contented with life’s necessities.
They eat little, not devoted to filling their stomach.
They are rarely drowsy, and are dedicated to wakefulness.
They get to take part in talk about self-effacement that helps open the heart, when they want, without trouble or difficulty. That is,

segs.p: appicchakathā …pe… vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā, evarūpiyā kathāya nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī;
segs.e: talk about fewness of wishes, contentment, seclusion, keeping your distance, arousing energy, ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.
They review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu ānāpānassatiṁ bhāvento nacirasseva akuppaṁ paṭivijjhatī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant developing mindfulness of breathing who has these five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.”
Numbered Discourses 5.98
10. With Kakudha
In the Wilderness

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu ānāpānassatiṁ bahulīkaronto nacirasseva akuppaṁ paṭivijjhati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant practicing mindfulness of breathing who has five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appaṭṭho hoti appakicco subharo susantoso jīvitaparikkhāresu;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant has few obligations and duties, and is unburdensome and contented with life’s necessities.
They eat little, not devoted to filling their stomach.
They are rarely drowsy, and are dedicated to wakefulness.
They live in the wilderness, in remote lodgings.
They review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu ānāpānassatiṁ bahulīkaronto nacirasseva akuppaṁ paṭivijjhatī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant practicing mindfulness of breathing who has these five things will soon penetrate the unshakable.”
Numbered Discourses 5.99
10. With Kakudha
The Lion
“Mendicants, toward evening the lion, king of beasts, emerges from his den,
yawns,
surveys the four quarters,

segs.p: samantā catuddisaṁ anuviloketvā tikkhattuṁ sīhanādaṁ nadati;
segs.e: and roars his lion’s roar three times.
Then he sets out on the hunt.

segs.p: So hatthissa cepi pahāraṁ deti, sakkaccaññeva pahāraṁ deti, no asakkaccaṁ;
segs.e: If he strikes an elephant, he does it carefully, not carelessly.

segs.p: mahiṁsassa cepi pahāraṁ deti, sakkaccaññeva pahāraṁ deti, no asakkaccaṁ;
segs.e: If he strikes a buffalo …

segs.p: gavassa cepi pahāraṁ deti, sakkaccaññeva pahāraṁ deti, no asakkaccaṁ;
segs.e: a cow …

segs.p: dīpissa cepi pahāraṁ deti, sakkaccaññeva pahāraṁ deti, no asakkaccaṁ;
segs.e: a leopard …

segs.p: khuddakānañcepi pāṇānaṁ pahāraṁ deti antamaso sasabiḷārānampi, sakkaccaññeva pahāraṁ deti, no asakkaccaṁ.
segs.e: or any smaller creatures—even a hare or a cat—he does it carefully, not carelessly.
Why is that?
Thinking: ‘May I not lose my way.’

segs.p: Sīhoti kho, bhikkhave, tathāgatassetaṁ adhivacanaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassa.
segs.e: ‘Lion’ is a term for the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tathāgato parisāya dhammaṁ deseti, idamassa hoti sīhanādasmiṁ.
segs.e: When the Realized One teaches Dhamma to an assembly, this is his lion’s roar.

segs.p: Bhikkhūnañcepi, bhikkhave, tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, sakkaccaññeva tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, no asakkaccaṁ;
segs.e: When the Realized One teaches the monks …

segs.p: bhikkhunīnañcepi, bhikkhave, tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, sakkaccaññeva tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, no asakkaccaṁ;
segs.e: nuns …

segs.p: upāsakānañcepi, bhikkhave, tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, sakkaccaññeva tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, no asakkaccaṁ;
segs.e: laymen …

segs.p: upāsikānañcepi, bhikkhave, tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, sakkaccaññeva tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, no asakkaccaṁ;
segs.e: laywomen …

segs.p: puthujjanānañcepi, bhikkhave, tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti antamaso annabhāranesādānampi, sakkaccaññeva tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti, no asakkaccaṁ.
segs.e: or ordinary people—even food-carriers and hunters—he teaches them carefully, not carelessly.
Why is that?
Because the Realized One has respect and reverence for the teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 5.100
10. With Kakudha
With Kakudha
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena kakudho nāma koliyaputto āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa upaṭṭhāko adhunākālaṅkato aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapanno.
segs.e: At that time the Koliyan named Kakudha—Venerable Mahāmoggallāna’s supporter—had recently passed away and been reborn in a certain host of mind-made gods.

segs.p: Tassa evarūpo attabhāvapaṭilābho hoti—seyyathāpi nāma dve vā tīṇi vā māgadhakāni gāmakkhettāni.
segs.e: His incarnation was two or three times the size of a Magadhan village with its fields.

segs.p: So tena attabhāvapaṭilābhena neva attānaṁ no paraṁ byābādheti.
segs.e: But with that incarnation he didn’t obstruct himself or others.

segs.p: Atha kho kakudho devaputto yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho kakudho devaputto āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the godling Kakudha went up to Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,
“Sir, this fixed desire arose in Devadatta:
‘I shall lead the mendicant Saṅgha.’

segs.p: Sahacittuppādā ca, bhante, devadatto tassā iddhiyā parihīno”ti.
segs.e: And as that thought arose, Devadatta lost that psychic power.”
That is what the godling Kakudha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
segs.e: Then he bowed and respectfully circled Mahāmoggallāna, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahāmoggallāna went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened.

segs.p: “Kakudho nāma, bhante, koliyaputto mamaṁ upaṭṭhāko adhunākālaṅkato aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapanno hoti.
Tassa evarūpo attabhāvapaṭilābho—seyyathāpi nāma dve vā tīṇi vā māgadhakāni gāmakkhettāni.
So tena attabhāvapaṭilābhena neva attānaṁ no paraṁ byābādheti.
Atha kho, bhante, kakudho devaputto yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho, bhante, kakudho devaputto maṁ etadavoca:
Sahacittuppādā ca, bhante, devadatto tassā iddhiyā parihīno’ti.
Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.
“Kiṁ pana te, moggallāna, kakudho devaputto cetasā ceto paricca vidito:
segs.e: “But Moggallāna, did you encompass the godling Kakudha’s mind, and know that

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kiñci kakudho devaputto bhāsati sabbaṁ taṁ tatheva hoti, no aññathā’”ti?
segs.e: everything he says is correct and not otherwise?”

segs.p: “Cetasā ceto paricca vidito me, bhante, kakudho devaputto:
segs.e: “Indeed I did, sir.”

segs.p: ‘yaṁ kiñci kakudho devaputto bhāsati sabbaṁ taṁ tatheva hoti, no aññathā’”ti.

segs.e: “Mark these words, Moggallāna!
Mark these words!

segs.p: Idāni so moghapuriso attanāva attānaṁ pātukarissati.
segs.e: Now that futile man Devadatta will expose himself by his own deeds.

segs.p: Pañcime, moggallāna, satthāro santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: Moggallāna, there are these five teachers found in the world.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, moggallāna, ekacco satthā aparisuddhasīlo samāno ‘parisuddhasīlomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddhaṁ me sīlaṁ pariyodātaṁ asaṅkiliṭṭhan’ti.
segs.e: Firstly, some teacher with impure conduct claims: ‘I am pure in ethics. My ethical conduct is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’
But their disciples know:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ kho bhavaṁ satthā aparisuddhasīlo samāno parisuddhasīlomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddhaṁ me sīlaṁ pariyodātaṁ asaṅkiliṭṭhan’ti.
segs.e: ‘This teacher has impure ethical conduct, but claims to be ethically pure.

segs.p: Mayañceva kho pana gihīnaṁ āroceyyāma, nāssassa manāpaṁ.
segs.e: They wouldn’t like it if we were to tell the laypeople.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho panassa amanāpaṁ, kathaṁ naṁ mayaṁ tena samudācareyyāma:
segs.e: And how could we treat them in a way that they don’t like?
But they consent to robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: yaṁ tumo karissati tumova tena paññāyissatī’ti.
segs.e: They themselves will be recognized by their own deeds.’

segs.p: Evarūpaṁ kho, moggallāna, satthāraṁ sāvakā sīlato rakkhanti;
segs.e: The disciples of such a teacher cover up their teacher’s conduct,

segs.p: evarūpo ca pana satthā sāvakehi sīlato rakkhaṁ paccāsīsati.
segs.e: and the teacher expects them to do so.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, moggallāna, idhekacco satthā aparisuddhājīvo samāno ‘parisuddhājīvomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddho me ājīvo pariyodāto asaṅkiliṭṭho’ti.
segs.e: Furthermore, some teacher with impure livelihood claims: ‘I am pure in livelihood. My livelihood is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’
But their disciples know:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ kho bhavaṁ satthā aparisuddhājīvo samāno parisuddhājīvomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddho me ājīvo pariyodāto asaṅkiliṭṭho’ti.
segs.e: ‘This teacher has impure livelihood, but claims to have pure livelihood.

segs.p: Mayañceva kho pana gihīnaṁ āroceyyāma, nāssassa manāpaṁ.
segs.e: They wouldn’t like it if we were to tell the laypeople.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho panassa amanāpaṁ, kathaṁ naṁ mayaṁ tena samudācareyyāma:
segs.e: And how could we treat them in a way that they don’t like?
But they consent to robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: yaṁ tumo karissati tumova tena paññāyissatī’ti.
segs.e: They themselves will be recognized by their own deeds.’

segs.p: Evarūpaṁ kho, moggallāna, satthāraṁ sāvakā ājīvato rakkhanti;
segs.e: The disciples of such a teacher cover up their teacher’s livelihood,

segs.p: evarūpo ca pana satthā sāvakehi ājīvato rakkhaṁ paccāsīsati.
segs.e: and the teacher expects them to do so.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, moggallāna, idhekacco satthā aparisuddhadhammadesano samāno ‘parisuddhadhammadesanomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddhā me dhammadesanā pariyodātā asaṅkiliṭṭhā’ti.
segs.e: Furthermore, some teacher with impure teaching claims: ‘I am pure in teaching. My teaching is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’
But their disciples know:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ kho bhavaṁ satthā aparisuddhadhammadesano samāno parisuddhadhammadesanomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddhā me dhammadesanā pariyodātā asaṅkiliṭṭhā’ti.
segs.e: ‘This teacher has impure teaching, but claims to have pure teaching.

segs.p: Mayañceva kho pana gihīnaṁ āroceyyāma, nāssassa manāpaṁ.
segs.e: They wouldn’t like it if we were to tell the laypeople.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho panassa amanāpaṁ, kathaṁ naṁ mayaṁ tena samudācareyyāma:
segs.e: And how could we treat them in a way that they don’t like?
But they consent to robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: yaṁ tumo karissati tumova tena paññāyissatī’ti.
segs.e: They themselves will be recognized by their own deeds.’

segs.p: Evarūpaṁ kho, moggallāna, satthāraṁ sāvakā dhammadesanato rakkhanti;
segs.e: The disciples of such a teacher cover up their teacher’s teaching,

segs.p: evarūpo ca pana satthā sāvakehi dhammadesanato rakkhaṁ paccāsīsati.
segs.e: and the teacher expects them to do so.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, moggallāna, idhekacco satthā aparisuddhaveyyākaraṇo samāno ‘parisuddhaveyyākaraṇomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddhaṁ me veyyākaraṇaṁ pariyodātaṁ asaṅkiliṭṭhan’ti.
segs.e: Furthermore, some teacher with impure answers claims: ‘I am pure in how I answer. My answers are pure, bright, uncorrupted.’
But their disciples know:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ kho bhavaṁ satthā aparisuddhaveyyākaraṇo samāno parisuddhaveyyākaraṇomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddhaṁ me veyyākaraṇaṁ pariyodātaṁ asaṅkiliṭṭhan’ti.
segs.e: ‘This teacher has impure answers, but claims to have pure answers.

segs.p: Mayañceva kho pana gihīnaṁ āroceyyāma, nāssassa manāpaṁ.
segs.e: They wouldn’t like it if we were to tell the laypeople.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho panassa amanāpaṁ, kathaṁ naṁ mayaṁ tena samudācareyyāma:
segs.e: And how could we treat them in a way that they don’t like?
But they consent to robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: yaṁ tumo karissati tumova tena paññāyissatī’ti.
segs.e: They themselves will be recognized by their own deeds.’

segs.p: Evarūpaṁ kho, moggallāna, satthāraṁ sāvakā veyyākaraṇato rakkhanti;
segs.e: The disciples of such a teacher cover up their teacher’s answers,

segs.p: evarūpo ca pana satthā sāvakehi veyyākaraṇato rakkhaṁ paccāsīsati.
segs.e: and the teacher expects them to do so.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, moggallāna, idhekacco satthā aparisuddhañāṇadassano samāno ‘parisuddhañāṇadassanomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddhaṁ me ñāṇadassanaṁ pariyodātaṁ asaṅkiliṭṭhan’ti.
segs.e: Furthermore, some teacher with impure knowledge and vision claims: ‘I am pure in knowledge and vision. My knowledge and vision are pure, bright, uncorrupted.’
But their disciples know:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ kho bhavaṁ satthā aparisuddhañāṇadassano samāno parisuddhañāṇadassanomhī’ti paṭijānāti ‘parisuddhaṁ me ñāṇadassanaṁ pariyodātaṁ asaṅkiliṭṭhan’ti.
segs.e: ‘This teacher has impure knowledge and vision, but claims to have pure knowledge and vision.

segs.p: Mayañceva kho pana gihīnaṁ āroceyyāma, nāssassa manāpaṁ.
segs.e: They wouldn’t like it if we were to tell the laypeople.

segs.p: Yaṁ kho panassa amanāpaṁ, kathaṁ naṁ mayaṁ tena samudācareyyāma:
segs.e: And how could we treat them in a way that they don’t like?
But they consent to robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: yaṁ tumo karissati tumova tena paññāyissatī’ti.
segs.e: They themselves will be recognized by their own deeds.’

segs.p: Evarūpaṁ kho, moggallāna, satthāraṁ sāvakā ñāṇadassanato rakkhanti;
segs.e: The disciples of such a teacher cover up their teacher’s knowledge and vision,

segs.p: evarūpo ca pana satthā sāvakehi ñāṇadassanato rakkhaṁ paccāsīsati.
segs.e: and the teacher expects them to do so.

segs.p: Ime kho, moggallāna, pañca satthāro santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the five teachers found in the world.

segs.p: Ahaṁ kho pana, moggallāna, parisuddhasīlo samāno ‘parisuddhasīlomhī’ti paṭijānāmi ‘parisuddhaṁ me sīlaṁ pariyodātaṁ asaṅkiliṭṭhan’ti.
segs.e: But Moggallāna, I have pure ethical conduct, and I claim: ‘I am pure in ethical conduct. My ethical conduct is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

segs.p: Na ca maṁ sāvakā sīlato rakkhanti, na cāhaṁ sāvakehi sīlato rakkhaṁ paccāsīsāmi.
segs.e: My disciples don’t cover up my conduct, and I don’t expect them to.

segs.p: Parisuddhājīvo samāno ‘parisuddhājīvomhī’ti paṭijānāmi ‘parisuddho me ājīvo pariyodāto asaṅkiliṭṭho’ti.
segs.e: I have pure livelihood, and I claim: ‘I am pure in livelihood. My livelihood is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

segs.p: Na ca maṁ sāvakā ājīvato rakkhanti, na cāhaṁ sāvakehi ājīvato rakkhaṁ paccāsīsāmi.
segs.e: My disciples don’t cover up my livelihood, and I don’t expect them to.

segs.p: Parisuddhadhammadesano samāno ‘parisuddhadhammadesanomhī’ti paṭijānāmi ‘parisuddhā me dhammadesanā pariyodātā asaṅkiliṭṭhā’ti.
segs.e: I have pure teaching, and I claim: ‘I am pure in teaching. My teaching is pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

segs.p: Na ca maṁ sāvakā dhammadesanato rakkhanti, na cāhaṁ sāvakehi dhammadesanato rakkhaṁ paccāsīsāmi.
segs.e: My disciples don’t cover up my teaching, and I don’t expect them to.

segs.p: Parisuddhaveyyākaraṇo samāno ‘parisuddhaveyyākaraṇomhī’ti paṭijānāmi ‘parisuddhaṁ me veyyākaraṇaṁ pariyodātaṁ asaṅkiliṭṭhan’ti.
segs.e: I have pure answers, and I claim: ‘I am pure in how I answer. My answers are pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

segs.p: Na ca maṁ sāvakā veyyākaraṇato rakkhanti, na cāhaṁ sāvakehi veyyākaraṇato rakkhaṁ paccāsīsāmi.
segs.e: My disciples don’t cover up my answers, and I don’t expect them to.

segs.p: Parisuddhañāṇadassano samāno ‘parisuddhañāṇadassanomhī’ti paṭijānāmi ‘parisuddhaṁ me ñāṇadassanaṁ pariyodātaṁ asaṅkiliṭṭhan’ti.
segs.e: I have pure knowledge and vision, and I claim: ‘I am pure in knowledge and vision. My knowledge and vision are pure, bright, uncorrupted.’

segs.p: Na ca maṁ sāvakā ñāṇadassanato rakkhanti, na cāhaṁ sāvakehi ñāṇadassanato rakkhaṁ paccāsīsāmī”ti.
segs.e: My disciples don’t cover up my knowledge and vision, and I don’t expect them to.”
Numbered Discourses 5.101
11. Living Comfortably
Assurance
“Mendicants, these five qualities make a trainee self-assured.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho hoti, sīlavā hoti, bahussuto hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, paññavā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is faithful, ethical, learned, energetic, and wise.

segs.p: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, assaddhassa sārajjaṁ hoti, saddhassa taṁ sārajjaṁ na hoti.
segs.e: A person of faith doesn’t have the insecurities of someone who lacks faith.
So this quality makes a trainee self-assured.

segs.p: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, dussīlassa sārajjaṁ hoti, sīlavato taṁ sārajjaṁ na hoti.
segs.e: An ethical person doesn’t have the insecurities of someone who is unethical.
So this quality makes a trainee self-assured.

segs.p: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, appassutassa sārajjaṁ hoti, bahussutassa taṁ sārajjaṁ na hoti.
segs.e: A learned person doesn’t have the insecurities of a person of little learning.
So this quality makes a trainee self-assured.

segs.p: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, kusītassa sārajjaṁ hoti, āraddhavīriyassa taṁ sārajjaṁ na hoti.
segs.e: An energetic person doesn’t have the insecurities of a lazy person.
So this quality makes a trainee self-assured.

segs.p: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, duppaññassa sārajjaṁ hoti, paññavato taṁ sārajjaṁ na hoti.
segs.e: A wise person doesn’t have the insecurities of someone who is witless.
So this quality makes a trainee self-assured.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca sekhavesārajjakaraṇā dhammā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five qualities that make a trainee self-assured.”
Numbered Discourses 5.102
11. Living Comfortably
Suspected

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu ussaṅkitaparisaṅkito hoti pāpabhikkhūti api akuppadhammopi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, even if a monk is of impeccable character, he might be suspected and distrusted as a ‘bad monk’ for five reasons.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vesiyāgocaro vā hoti, vidhavāgocaro vā hoti, thullakumārikāgocaro vā hoti, paṇḍakagocaro vā hoti, bhikkhunīgocaro vā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a monk resorts to prostitutes, widows, voluptuous girls, eunuchs, or nuns for alms.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu ussaṅkitaparisaṅkito hoti pāpabhikkhūti api akuppadhammopī”ti.
segs.e: Even if a monk is of impeccable character, he might be suspected and distrusted as a ‘bad monk’ for these five reasons.”
Numbered Discourses 5.103
11. Living Comfortably
A Master Thief

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato mahācoro sandhimpi chindati, nillopampi harati, ekāgārikampi karoti, paripanthepi tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a master thief with five factors breaks into houses, plunders wealth, steals from isolated buildings, and commits highway robbery.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, mahācoro visamanissito ca hoti, gahananissito ca, balavanissito ca, bhogacāgī ca, ekacārī ca.
segs.e: A master thief relies on rough ground, on thick cover, and on the powerful; they pay bribes, and they act alone.
And how does a master thief rely on rough ground?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, mahācoro nadīviduggaṁ vā nissito hoti pabbatavisamaṁ vā.
segs.e: It’s when a master thief relies on inaccessible riverlands or rugged mountains.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, mahācoro visamanissito hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a master thief relies on rough ground.
And how does a master thief rely on thick cover?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, mahācoro tiṇagahanaṁ vā nissito hoti rukkhagahanaṁ vā rodhaṁ vā mahāvanasaṇḍaṁ vā.
segs.e: It’s when a master thief relies on thick grass, thick trees, a blind spot, or a large forest grove.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, mahācoro gahananissito hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a master thief relies on thick cover.
And how does a master thief rely on the powerful?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, mahācoro rājānaṁ vā rājamahāmattānaṁ vā nissito hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a master thief relies on rulers or their chief ministers.
They think:

segs.p: ‘sace maṁ koci kiñci vakkhati, ime me rājāno vā rājamahāmattā vā pariyodhāya atthaṁ bhaṇissantī’ti.
segs.e: ‘If anyone accuses me of anything, these rulers or their chief ministers will speak in my defense in the case.’

segs.p: Sace naṁ koci kiñci āha, tyassa rājāno vā rājamahāmattā vā pariyodhāya atthaṁ bhaṇanti.
segs.e: And that’s exactly what happens.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, mahācoro balavanissito hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a master thief relies on the powerful.
And how does a master thief pay bribes?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, mahācoro aḍḍho hoti mahaddhano mahābhogo.
segs.e: It’s when a master thief is rich, affluent, and wealthy.
They think:

segs.p: ‘sace maṁ koci kiñci vakkhati, ito bhogena paṭisantharissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘If anyone accuses me of anything, I’ll settle it with a bribe.’

segs.p: Sace naṁ koci kiñci āha, tato bhogena paṭisantharati.
segs.e: And that’s exactly what happens.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, mahācoro bhogacāgī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a master thief pays bribes.
And how does a master thief act alone?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, mahācoro ekakova gahaṇāni kattā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a master thief carries out robbery all alone.
Why is that?
So that their secret plans are not leaked to others.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, mahācoro ekacārī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a master thief acts alone.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato mahācoro sandhimpi chindati nillopampi harati ekāgārikampi karoti paripanthepi tiṭṭhati.
segs.e: A master thief with these five factors breaks into houses, plunders wealth, steals from isolated buildings, and commits highway robbery.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato pāpabhikkhu khataṁ upahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo viññūnaṁ, bahuñca apuññaṁ pasavati.
segs.e: In the same way, when a bad mendicant has five qualities, they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, pāpabhikkhu visamanissito ca hoti, gahananissito ca, balavanissito ca, bhogacāgī ca, ekacārī ca.
segs.e: A bad mendicant relies on rough ground, on thick cover, and on the powerful; they pay bribes, and they act alone.
And how does a bad mendicant rely on rough ground?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, pāpabhikkhu visamena kāyakammena samannāgato hoti, visamena vacīkammena samannāgato hoti, visamena manokammena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a bad mendicant has unethical conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pāpabhikkhu visamanissito hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a bad mendicant relies on rough ground.
And how does a bad mendicant rely on thick cover?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, pāpabhikkhu micchādiṭṭhiko hoti antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato.
segs.e: It’s when a bad mendicant has wrong view, he’s attached to an extremist view.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pāpabhikkhu gahananissito hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a bad mendicant relies on thick cover.
And how does a bad mendicant rely on the powerful?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, pāpabhikkhu rājānaṁ vā rājamahāmattānaṁ vā nissito hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a bad mendicant relies on rulers or their chief ministers.
They think:

segs.p: ‘sace maṁ koci kiñci vakkhati, ime me rājāno vā rājamahāmattā vā pariyodhāya atthaṁ bhaṇissantī’ti.
segs.e: ‘If anyone accuses me of anything, these rulers or their chief ministers will speak in my defense in the case.’

segs.p: Sace naṁ koci kiñci āha, tyassa rājāno vā rājamahāmattā vā pariyodhāya atthaṁ bhaṇanti.
segs.e: And that’s exactly what happens.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pāpabhikkhu balavanissito hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a bad mendicant relies on the powerful.
And how does a bad mendicant pay bribes?
It’s when a bad mendicant receives robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.
They think:

segs.p: ‘sace maṁ koci kiñci vakkhati, ito lābhena paṭisantharissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘If anyone accuses me of anything, I’ll settle it with a bribe.’

segs.p: Sace naṁ koci kiñci āha, tato lābhena paṭisantharati.
segs.e: And that’s exactly what happens.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pāpabhikkhu bhogacāgī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a bad mendicant pays bribes.
And how does a bad mendicant act alone?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, pāpabhikkhu ekakova paccantimesu janapadesu nivāsaṁ kappeti.
segs.e: It’s when a bad mendicant dwells alone in the borderlands.

segs.p: So tattha kulāni upasaṅkamanto lābhaṁ labhati.
segs.e: They visit families there to acquire material things.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pāpabhikkhu ekacārī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a bad mendicant acts alone.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato pāpabhikkhu khataṁ upahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo viññūnaṁ, bahuñca apuññaṁ pasavatī”ti.
segs.e: When a bad mendicant possesses these five qualities, they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.”
Numbered Discourses 5.104
11. Living Comfortably
A Delicate Ascetic of Ascetics

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu samaṇesu samaṇasukhumālo hoti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is a delicate ascetic of ascetics.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yācitova bahulaṁ cīvaraṁ paribhuñjati, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ piṇḍapātaṁ paribhuñjati, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ senāsanaṁ paribhuñjati, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ paribhuñjati, appaṁ ayācito.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant usually uses only what they’ve been invited to accept—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick—rarely using them without invitation.

segs.p: Yehi kho pana sabrahmacārīhi saddhiṁ viharati, tyassa manāpeneva bahulaṁ kāyakammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena; manāpeneva bahulaṁ vacīkammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena; manāpeneva bahulaṁ manokammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena;
segs.e: When living with other spiritual practitioners, they usually find themselves treated agreeably by them by way of body, speech, and mind, and rarely disagreeably.
And they are usually presented with agreeable things by them, rarely with disagreeable ones.

segs.p: Yāni kho pana tāni vedayitāni pittasamuṭṭhānāni vā semhasamuṭṭhānāni vā vātasamuṭṭhānāni vā sannipātikāni vā utupariṇāmajāni vā visamaparihārajāni vā opakkamikāni vā kammavipākajāni vā, tānissa na bahudeva uppajjanti.
segs.e: They’re healthy, so the various unpleasant feelings—stemming from disorders of bile, phlegm, wind, or their conjunction; or caused by change in weather, by not taking care of themselves, by exertion, or as the result of past deeds—usually don’t come up.

segs.p: Appābādho hoti, catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī,
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu samaṇesu samaṇasukhumālo hoti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities is a delicate ascetic of ascetics.

segs.p: Yañhi taṁ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya: ‘samaṇesu samaṇasukhumālo’ti, mameva taṁ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya: ‘samaṇesu samaṇasukhumālo’ti.
segs.e: And if anyone should be rightly called a delicate ascetic of ascetics, it’s me.

segs.p: Ahañhi, bhikkhave, yācitova bahulaṁ cīvaraṁ paribhuñjāmi, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ piṇḍapātaṁ paribhuñjāmi, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ senāsanaṁ paribhuñjāmi, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ paribhuñjāmi, appaṁ ayācito.
segs.e: For I usually use only what I’ve been invited to accept.

segs.p: Yehi kho pana bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ viharāmi, te maṁ manāpeneva bahulaṁ kāyakammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena; manāpeneva bahulaṁ vacīkammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena; manāpeneva bahulaṁ manokammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena;
segs.e: When living with other mendicants, I am usually treated agreeably by them.
And I usually present them with agreeable things.

segs.p: Yāni kho pana tāni vedayitāni—pittasamuṭṭhānāni vā semhasamuṭṭhānāni vā vātasamuṭṭhānāni vā sannipātikāni vā utupariṇāmajāni vā visamaparihārajāni vā opakkamikāni vā kammavipākajāni vā—tāni me na bahudeva uppajjanti. Appābādhohamasmi.
segs.e: I’m healthy.

segs.p: catunnaṁ kho panasmi jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī akicchalābhī akasiralābhī,
segs.e: I get the four absorptions when I want, without trouble or difficulty.
And I’ve realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life …

segs.p: Yañhi taṁ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya: ‘samaṇesu samaṇasukhumālo’ti, mameva taṁ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya: ‘samaṇesu samaṇasukhumālo’”ti.
segs.e: So if anyone should be rightly called a delicate ascetic of ascetics, it’s me.”
Numbered Discourses 5.105
11. Living Comfortably
Living Comfortably
“Mendicants, there are these five ways of living comfortably.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno mettaṁ kāyakammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca, mettaṁ vacīkammaṁ … mettaṁ manokammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with kindness by way of body, speech, and mind, both in public and in private.

segs.p: Yāni tāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññuppasatthāni aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṁvattanikāni, tathārūpehi sīlehi sīlasāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca.
segs.e: They live according to the precepts shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. Those precepts are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segs.p: Yāyaṁ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya, tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhisāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca.
segs.e: They live according to the view shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. That view is noble and emancipating, and delivers one who applies it to the complete ending of suffering.
These are the five ways of living comfortably.”
Numbered Discourses 5.106
11. Living Comfortably
With Ānanda

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhu saṅghe viharanto phāsuṁ vihareyyā”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, how could a mendicant live comfortably while staying in a monastic community?”

segs.p: “Yato kho, ānanda, bhikkhu attanā sīlasampanno hoti, no paraṁ adhisīle sampavattā;
segs.e: “It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in their own ethical conduct, but they don’t urge others to be ethical.

segs.p: ettāvatāpi kho, ānanda, bhikkhu saṅghe viharanto phāsuṁ vihareyyā”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant could live comfortably while staying in a monastic community.”

segs.p: “Siyā pana, bhante, aññopi pariyāyo yathā bhikkhu saṅghe viharanto phāsuṁ vihareyyā”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, could there be another way for a mendicant to live comfortably while staying in a monastic community?”
“There could, Ānanda.

segs.p: Yato kho, ānanda, bhikkhu attanā sīlasampanno hoti, no paraṁ adhisīle sampavattā;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in their own ethical conduct, but they don’t urge others to be ethical.
And they watch themselves, but don’t watch others.

segs.p: ettāvatāpi kho, ānanda, bhikkhu saṅghe viharanto phāsuṁ vihareyyā”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant could live comfortably while staying in a monastic community.”

segs.p: “Siyā pana, bhante, aññopi pariyāyo yathā bhikkhu saṅghe viharanto phāsuṁ vihareyyā”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, could there be another way for a mendicant to live comfortably while staying in a monastic community?”
“There could, Ānanda.

segs.p: Yato kho, ānanda, bhikkhu attanā sīlasampanno hoti, no paraṁ adhisīle sampavattā;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in their own ethical conduct, but they don’t urge others to be ethical.
And they watch themselves, but don’t watch others.

segs.p: apaññāto ca hoti, tena ca apaññātakena no paritassati;
segs.e: And they’re not well-known, but aren’t bothered by that.

segs.p: ettāvatāpi kho, ānanda, bhikkhu saṅghe viharanto phāsuṁ vihareyyā”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant could live comfortably while staying in a monastic community.”

segs.p: “Siyā pana, bhante, aññopi pariyāyo yathā bhikkhu saṅghe viharanto phāsuṁ vihareyyā”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, could there be another way for a mendicant to live comfortably while staying in a monastic community?”
“There could, Ānanda.

segs.p: Yato kho, ānanda, bhikkhu attanā sīlasampanno hoti, no paraṁ adhisīle sampavattā;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in their own ethical conduct, but they don’t urge others to be ethical.
And they watch themselves, but don’t watch others.

segs.p: apaññāto ca hoti, tena ca apaññātakena no paritassati;
segs.e: And they’re not well-known, but aren’t bothered by that.

segs.p: catunnañca jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī;
segs.e: And they get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: ettāvatāpi kho, ānanda, bhikkhu saṅghe viharanto phāsuṁ vihareyyā”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant could live comfortably while staying in a monastic community.”

segs.p: “Siyā pana, bhante, aññopi pariyāyo yathā bhikkhu saṅghe viharanto phāsuṁ vihareyyā”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, might there be another way for a mendicant to live comfortably while staying in a monastic community?”
“There could, Ānanda.

segs.p: Yato kho, ānanda, bhikkhu attanā sīlasampanno hoti, no paraṁ adhisīle sampavattā;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in their own ethical conduct, but they don’t urge others to be ethical.
And they watch themselves, but don’t watch others.

segs.p: apaññāto ca hoti, tena ca apaññātakena no paritassati;
segs.e: And they’re not well-known, but aren’t bothered by that.

segs.p: catunnañca jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī;
segs.e: And they get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: And they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: ettāvatāpi kho, ānanda, bhikkhu saṅghe viharanto phāsuṁ vihareyya.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant could live comfortably while staying in a monastic community.

segs.p: Imamhā cāhaṁ, ānanda, phāsuvihārā añño phāsuvihāro uttaritaro vā paṇītataro vā natthīti vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: And I say that there is no better or finer way of living comfortably than this.”
Numbered Discourses 5.107
11. Living Comfortably
Ethics

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlasampanno hoti, samādhisampanno hoti, paññāsampanno hoti, vimuttisampanno hoti, vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is accomplished in ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 5.108
11. Living Comfortably
An adept

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asekhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when they have the entire spectrum of the adept’s ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 5.109
11. Living Comfortably
All Four Quarters

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu cātuddiso hoti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is at ease in any quarter.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu;
segs.e: It’s when mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā;
segs.e: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.
They’re content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī;
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Imehi, kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu cātuddiso hotī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities is at ease in any quarter.”
Numbered Discourses 5.110
11. Living Comfortably
Wilderness

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has five qualities they’re ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s totally full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, reciting them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segs.p: āraddhavīriyo viharati thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu;
segs.e: They live with energy roused up. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

segs.p: catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī;
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevitun”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these five qualities they’re ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.”
Numbered Discourses 5.111
12. At Andhakavinda
Visiting Families

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato kulūpako bhikkhu kulesu appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities who visits families is disliked and disagreeable, not respected or admired.
What five?

segs.p: Asanthavavissāsī ca hoti, anissaravikappī ca, vissaṭṭhupasevī ca, upakaṇṇakajappī ca, atiyācanako ca.
segs.e: They act as though they're familiar with people they hardly know. They give away things they don’t own. They over-associate with close friends. They whisper in the ear. And they ask for too much.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato kulūpako bhikkhu kulesu appiyo ca hoti amanāpo ca agaru ca abhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities who visits families is disliked and disagreeable, not respected or admired.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato kulūpako bhikkhu kulesu piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A mendicant with five qualities who visits families is dear and beloved, respected and admired.
What five?

segs.p: Na asanthavavissāsī ca hoti, na anissaravikappī ca, na vissaṭṭhupasevī ca, na upakaṇṇakajappī ca, na atiyācanako ca.
segs.e: They don’t act as though they're familiar with people they hardly know. They don’t give away things they don’t own. They don’t over-associate with close friends. They don’t whisper in the ear. And they don’t ask for too much.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato kulūpako bhikkhu kulesu piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities who visits families is dear and beloved, respected and admired.”
Numbered Discourses 5.112
12. At Andhakavinda
A Second Monk

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato pacchāsamaṇo na ādātabbo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, you shouldn’t take a second monk with five qualities.
What five?

segs.p: Atidūre vā gacchati accāsanne vā, na pattapariyāpannaṁ gaṇhati, āpattisāmantā bhaṇamānaṁ na nivāreti, bhaṇamānassa antarantarā kathaṁ opāteti, duppañño hoti jaḷo eḷamūgo.
segs.e: They walk too far away or too close behind. They don’t take your bowl when it’s full. They don’t warn you when your speech is bordering on an offense. They keep on interrupting while you’re speaking. And they’re witless, dull, and idiotic.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato pacchāsamaṇo na ādātabbo.
segs.e: You shouldn’t take a second monk these five qualities.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato pacchāsamaṇo ādātabbo.
segs.e: You should take a second monk with five qualities.
What five?

segs.p: Nātidūre gacchati na accāsanne, pattapariyāpannaṁ gaṇhati, āpattisāmantā bhaṇamānaṁ nivāreti, bhaṇamānassa na antarantarā kathaṁ opāteti, paññavā hoti ajaḷo aneḷamūgo.
segs.e: They don’t walk too far away or too close behind. They take your bowl when it is full. They warn you when your speech is bordering on an offense. They don’t interrupt while you’re speaking. And they’re wise, bright, and clever.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato pacchāsamaṇo ādātabbo”ti.
segs.e: You should take a second monk with these five qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 5.113
12. At Andhakavinda
Right Immersion

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo sammāsamādhiṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant who has five qualities can’t enter and remain in right immersion.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkhamo hoti rūpānaṁ, akkhamo saddānaṁ, akkhamo gandhānaṁ, akkhamo rasānaṁ, akkhamo phoṭṭhabbānaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant can’t endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo sammāsamādhiṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant who possesses these five qualities can’t enter and remain in right immersion.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo sammāsamādhiṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant who has five qualities can enter and remain in right immersion.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khamo hoti rūpānaṁ, khamo saddānaṁ, khamo gandhānaṁ, khamo rasānaṁ, khamo phoṭṭhabbānaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant can endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo sammāsamādhiṁ upasampajja viharitun”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who possesses these five qualities can enter and remain in right immersion.”
Numbered Discourses 5.114
12. At Andhakavinda
At Andhakavinda

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā magadhesu viharati andhakavinde.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Magadhans at Andhakavinda.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Ye te, ānanda, bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ, te vo, ānanda, bhikkhū pañcasu dhammesu samādapetabbā nivesetabbā patiṭṭhāpetabbā.
segs.e: “Ānanda, those mendicants who are junior, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training should be encouraged, supported, and established in five things.
What five?

segs.p: ‘Etha tumhe, āvuso, sīlavā hotha, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvutā viharatha ācāragocarasampannā aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvino, samādāya sikkhatha sikkhāpadesū’ti—iti pātimokkhasaṁvare samādapetabbā nivesetabbā patiṭṭhāpetabbā.
segs.e: They should be encouraged, supported, and established in restraint in the monastic code: ‘Reverends, please be ethical. Live restrained in the monastic code, conducting yourselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, keep the rules you’ve undertaken.’

segs.p: ‘Etha tumhe, āvuso, indriyesu guttadvārā viharatha ārakkhasatino nipakkasatino, sārakkhitamānasā satārakkhena cetasā samannāgatā’ti—iti indriyasaṁvare samādapetabbā nivesetabbā patiṭṭhāpetabbā.
segs.e: They should be encouraged, supported, and established in sense restraint: ‘Reverends, please live with sense doors guarded, mindfully alert and on guard, with protected mind, having a heart protected by mindfulness.’

segs.p: ‘Etha tumhe, āvuso, appabhassā hotha, bhasse pariyantakārino’ti—iti bhassapariyante samādapetabbā nivesetabbā patiṭṭhāpetabbā.
segs.e: They should be encouraged, supported, and established in limiting their speech: ‘Reverends, please speak little. Put a limit on your speech.’

segs.p: ‘Etha tumhe, āvuso, āraññikā hotha, araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevathā’ti—iti kāyavūpakāse samādapetabbā nivesetabbā patiṭṭhāpetabbā.
segs.e: They should be encouraged, supported, and established in retreat: ‘Reverends, please live in the wilderness. Frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.’

segs.p: ‘Etha tumhe, āvuso, sammādiṭṭhikā hotha sammādassanena samannāgatā’ti—iti sammādassane samādapetabbā nivesetabbā patiṭṭhāpetabbā.
segs.e: They should be encouraged, supported, and established in right perspective: ‘Reverends, please hold right view and have right perspective.’

segs.p: Ye te, ānanda, bhikkhū navā acirapabbajitā adhunāgatā imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ, te vo, ānanda, bhikkhū imesu pañcasu dhammesu samādapetabbā nivesetabbā patiṭṭhāpetabbā”ti.
segs.e: Those mendicants who are junior, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training should be encouraged, supported, and established by you in these five things.”
Numbered Discourses 5.115
12. At Andhakavinda
Stingy

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a nun with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?

segs.p: Āvāsamaccharinī hoti, kulamaccharinī hoti, lābhamaccharinī hoti, vaṇṇamaccharinī hoti, dhammamaccharinī hoti.
segs.e: She is stingy with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teaching.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: A nun with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: A nun with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What five?

segs.p: Na āvāsamaccharinī hoti, na kulamaccharinī hoti, na lābhamaccharinī hoti, na vaṇṇamaccharinī hoti, na dhammamaccharinī hoti.
segs.e: She is not stingy with dwellings, families, material things, praise, or the teaching.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: A nun with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.116
12. At Andhakavinda
Praise

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a nun with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?
Without examining or scrutinizing, she praises those deserving of criticism,
and criticizes those deserving of praise.

segs.p: ananuvicca apariyogāhetvā appasādanīye ṭhāne pasādaṁ upadaṁseti,
segs.e: She arouses faith in things that are dubious,

segs.p: ananuvicca apariyogāhetvā pasādanīye ṭhāne appasādaṁ upadaṁseti,
segs.e: and doesn’t arouse faith in things that are inspiring.
And she wastes gifts given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: A nun with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: A nun with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What five?
After examining and scrutinizing, she criticizes those deserving of criticism,
and praises those deserving of praise.

segs.p: anuvicca pariyogāhetvā appasādanīye ṭhāne appasādaṁ upadaṁseti,
segs.e: She doesn’t arouse faith in things that are dubious,

segs.p: anuvicca pariyogāhetvā pasādanīye ṭhāne pasādaṁ upadaṁseti,
segs.e: and does arouse faith in things that are inspiring.
And she doesn’t waste gifts given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: A nun with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.117
12. At Andhakavinda
Jealous

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a nun with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?
Without examining or scrutinizing, she praises those deserving of criticism,
and criticizes those deserving of praise.
She is jealous,
stingy,
and wastes gifts given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: A nun with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: A nun with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What five?
After examining and scrutinizing, she criticizes those deserving of criticism,
and praises those deserving of praise.
She is not jealous,
or stingy,
and doesn’t waste gifts given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: A nun with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.118
12. At Andhakavinda
Having Wrong View

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a nun with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?
Without examining or scrutinizing, she praises those deserving of criticism,
and criticizes those deserving of praise.
She has wrong view
and wrong purpose,
and wastes gifts given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: A nun with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: A nun with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What five?
After examining and scrutinizing, she criticizes those deserving of criticism,
and praises those deserving of praise.
She has right view
and right purpose,
and doesn’t waste gifts given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: A nun with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.119
12. At Andhakavinda
Wrong Speech

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.

Numbered Discourses 5.120
12. At Andhakavinda
Wrong Effort

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a nun with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?
Without examining or scrutinizing, she praises those deserving of criticism,
and criticizes those deserving of praise.
She has wrong effort and
wrong mindfulness,
and wastes gifts given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: A nun with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

She has right effort and
right mindfulness,
