segs.e: A nun with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.121
13. Sick
Sick

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena gilānasālā tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to the infirmary, where

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ dubbalaṁ gilānakaṁ;
segs.e: he saw a certain mendicant who was weak and sick.
He sat down on the seat spread out,
and addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “Yaṁ kiñci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṁ dubbalaṁ gilānakaṁ pañca dhammā na vijahanti, tassetaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
segs.e: “Mendicants, if a weak and sick mendicant does not neglect five things, it can be expected that

segs.p: ‘nacirasseva āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissatī’ti.
segs.e: they will soon realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asubhānupassī kāye viharati, āhāre paṭikūlasaññī, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññī, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī, maraṇasaññā kho panassa ajjhattaṁ sūpaṭṭhitā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant meditates observing the ugliness of the body, perceives the repulsiveness of food, perceives dissatisfaction with the whole world, observes the impermanence of all conditions, and has well established the perception of their own death.

segs.p: Yaṁ kiñci, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṁ dubbalaṁ gilānakaṁ ime pañca dhammā na vijahanti, tassetaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ:
segs.e: If a weak and sick mendicant does not neglect these five things, it can be expected that
they will soon realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.”
Numbered Discourses 5.122
13. Sick
Mindfulness Well Established

segs.p: “Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā pañca dhamme bhāveti pañca dhamme bahulīkaroti, tassa dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—
segs.e: “Mendicants, any monk or nun who develops and cultivates five qualities can expect one of two results:

segs.p: diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā.
segs.e: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ajjhattaññeva sati sūpaṭṭhitā hoti dhammānaṁ udayatthagāminiyā paññāya, asubhānupassī kāye viharati, āhāre paṭikūlasaññī, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññī, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant has well established mindfulness inside themselves in order to understand the arising and passing away of phenomena, meditates observing the ugliness of the body, perceives the repulsiveness of food, perceives dissatisfaction with the whole world, and observes the impermanence of all conditions.

segs.p: Yo hi koci, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā ime pañca dhamme bhāveti ime pañca dhamme bahulīkaroti, tassa dvinnaṁ phalānaṁ aññataraṁ phalaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—
segs.e: Any monk or nun who develops and cultivates these five qualities can expect one of two results:

segs.p: diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā”ti.
segs.e: enlightenment in this very life, or if there’s residue left behind, non-return.”
Numbered Discourses 5.123
13. Sick
A Carer (1st)

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato gilāno dūpaṭṭhāko hoti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a patient with five qualities is hard to care for.
What five?

segs.p: Asappāyakārī hoti, sappāye mattaṁ na jānāti, bhesajjaṁ nappaṭisevitā hoti, atthakāmassa gilānupaṭṭhākassa na yathābhūtaṁ ābādhaṁ āvikattā hoti abhikkamantaṁ vā abhikkamatīti paṭikkamantaṁ vā paṭikkamatīti ṭhitaṁ vā ṭhitoti, uppannānaṁ sārīrikānaṁ vedanānaṁ dukkhānaṁ tibbānaṁ kharānaṁ kaṭukānaṁ asātānaṁ amanāpānaṁ pāṇaharānaṁ anadhivāsakajātiko hoti.
segs.e: They do what is unsuitable. They don’t know moderation in what is suitable. They don’t take their medicine. Though their carer wants what’s best for them, they don’t accurately report their symptoms by saying when they’re getting worse, getting better, or staying the same. And they cannot endure physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato gilāno dūpaṭṭhāko hoti.
segs.e: A patient with these five qualities is hard to care for.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato gilāno sūpaṭṭhāko hoti.
segs.e: A patient with five qualities is easy to care for.
What five?

segs.p: Sappāyakārī hoti, sappāye mattaṁ jānāti, bhesajjaṁ paṭisevitā hoti, atthakāmassa gilānupaṭṭhākassa yathābhūtaṁ ābādhaṁ āvikattā hoti abhikkamantaṁ vā abhikkamatīti paṭikkamantaṁ vā paṭikkamatīti ṭhitaṁ vā ṭhitoti, uppannānaṁ sārīrikānaṁ vedanānaṁ dukkhānaṁ tibbānaṁ kharānaṁ kaṭukānaṁ asātānaṁ amanāpānaṁ pāṇaharānaṁ adhivāsakajātiko hoti.
segs.e: They do what is suitable. They know moderation in what is suitable. They take their medicine. Because their carer wants what’s best for them, they accurately report their symptoms by saying when they’re getting worse, getting better, or staying the same. And they can endure physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato gilāno sūpaṭṭhāko hotī”ti.
segs.e: A patient with these five qualities is easy to care for.”
Numbered Discourses 5.124
13. Sick
A Carer (2nd)

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato gilānupaṭṭhāko nālaṁ gilānaṁ upaṭṭhātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a carer with five qualities is not competent to care for a patient.
What five?
They’re unable to prepare medicine.

segs.p: sappāyāsappāyaṁ na jānāti, asappāyaṁ upanāmeti, sappāyaṁ apanāmeti;
segs.e: They don’t know what is suitable and unsuitable, so they supply what is unsuitable and remove what is suitable.
They care for the sick for the sake of material benefits, not out of love.

segs.p: jegucchī hoti uccāraṁ vā passāvaṁ vā vantaṁ vā kheḷaṁ vā nīharituṁ;
segs.e: They’re disgusted to remove feces, urine, vomit, or spit.

segs.p: nappaṭibalo hoti gilānaṁ kālena kālaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetuṁ samādapetuṁ samuttejetuṁ sampahaṁsetuṁ.
segs.e: They’re unable to educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire the patient with a Dhamma talk from time to time.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato gilānupaṭṭhāko nālaṁ gilānaṁ upaṭṭhātuṁ.
segs.e: A carer with these five qualities is not competent to care for a patient.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato gilānupaṭṭhāko alaṁ gilānaṁ upaṭṭhātuṁ.
segs.e: A carer with five qualities is competent to care for a patient.
What five?
They’re able to prepare medicine.

segs.p: sappāyāsappāyaṁ jānāti, asappāyaṁ apanāmeti, sappāyaṁ upanāmeti;
segs.e: They know what is suitable and unsuitable, so they remove what is unsuitable and supply what is suitable.
They care for the sick out of love, not for the sake of material benefits.

segs.p: ajegucchī hoti uccāraṁ vā passāvaṁ vā vantaṁ vā kheḷaṁ vā nīharituṁ;
segs.e: They’re not disgusted to remove feces, urine, vomit, or spit.

segs.p: paṭibalo hoti gilānaṁ kālena kālaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetuṁ samādapetuṁ samuttejetuṁ sampahaṁsetuṁ.
segs.e: They’re able to educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire the patient with a Dhamma talk from time to time.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato gilānupaṭṭhāko alaṁ gilānaṁ upaṭṭhātun”ti.
segs.e: A carer with these five qualities is competent to care for a patient.”
Numbered Discourses 5.125
13. Sick
Longevity (1st)
“Mendicants, these five things impede longevity.
What five?

segs.p: Asappāyakārī hoti, sappāye mattaṁ na jānāti, apariṇatabhojī ca hoti, akālacārī ca hoti, abrahmacārī ca.
segs.e: Doing what is unsuitable, not knowing moderation in what is suitable, eating food unfit for consumption, activity at unsuitable times, and unchastity.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā anāyussā.
segs.e: These are the five things that impede longevity.
These five things promote longevity.
What five?

segs.p: Sappāyakārī hoti, sappāye mattaṁ jānāti, pariṇatabhojī ca hoti, kālacārī ca hoti, brahmacārī ca.
segs.e: Doing what is suitable, knowing moderation in what is suitable, eating food fit for consumption, activity at suitable times, and chastity.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā āyussā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five things that promote longevity.”
Numbered Discourses 5.126
13. Sick
Longevity (2nd)
“Mendicants, these five things impede longevity.
What five?

segs.p: Asappāyakārī hoti, sappāye mattaṁ na jānāti, apariṇatabhojī ca hoti, dussīlo ca, pāpamitto ca.
segs.e: Doing what is unsuitable, not knowing moderation in what is suitable, eating food unfit for consumption, unethical behavior, and bad friends.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā anāyussā.
segs.e: These are the five things that impede longevity.
These five things promote longevity.
What five?

segs.p: Sappāyakārī hoti, sappāye mattaṁ jānāti, pariṇatabhojī ca hoti, sīlavā ca, kalyāṇamitto ca.
segs.e: Doing what is suitable, knowing moderation in what is suitable, eating food fit for consumption, ethical conduct, and good friends.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā āyussā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five things that promote longevity.”
Numbered Discourses 5.127
13. Sick
Living Apart

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṁ saṅghamhā vapakāsituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is not fit to live apart from a Saṅgha community.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asantuṭṭho hoti itarītarena cīvarena, asantuṭṭho hoti itarītarena piṇḍapātena, asantuṭṭho hoti itarītarena senāsanena, asantuṭṭho hoti itarītarena gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, kāmasaṅkappabahulo ca viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is not content with any kind of robe, almsfood, lodging, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And they have a lot of sensual thoughts.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṁ saṅghamhā vapakāsituṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities is not fit to live apart from a Saṅgha community.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ saṅghamhā vapakāsituṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant with five qualities is fit to live apart from a Saṅgha community.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītarena cīvarena, santuṭṭho hoti itarītarena piṇḍapātena, santuṭṭho hoti itarītarena senāsanena, santuṭṭho hoti itarītarena gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, nekkhammasaṅkappabahulo ca viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is content with any kind of robe, almsfood, lodging, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And they think a lot about renunciation.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ saṅghamhā vapakāsitun”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities is fit to live apart from a Saṅgha community.”
Numbered Discourses 5.128
13. Sick
An Ascetic’s Happiness
“Mendicants, there are these five kinds of suffering for an ascetic.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asantuṭṭho hoti itarītarena cīvarena, asantuṭṭho hoti itarītarena piṇḍapātena, asantuṭṭho hoti itarītarena senāsanena, asantuṭṭho hoti itarītarena gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, anabhirato ca brahmacariyaṁ carati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is not content with any kind of robe, almsfood, lodging, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And they lead the spiritual life dissatisfied.
These are five kinds of suffering for an ascetic.
There are these five kinds of happiness for an ascetic.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītarena cīvarena, santuṭṭho hoti itarītarena piṇḍapātena, santuṭṭho hoti itarītarena senāsanena, santuṭṭho hoti itarītarena gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, abhirato ca brahmacariyaṁ carati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is content with any kind of robe, almsfood, lodging, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And they lead the spiritual life satisfied.
These are five kinds of happiness for an ascetic.”
Numbered Discourses 5.129
13. Sick
Fatal Wounds
“Mendicants, these five fatal wounds lead to a place of loss, to hell.
What five?

segs.p: Mātā jīvitā voropitā hoti, pitā jīvitā voropito hoti, arahaṁ jīvitā voropito hoti, tathāgatassa duṭṭhena cittena lohitaṁ uppāditaṁ hoti, saṅgho bhinno hoti.
segs.e: Murdering your mother or father or a perfected one; maliciously shedding the blood of a Realized One; and causing a schism in the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca āpāyikā nerayikā parikuppā atekicchā”ti.
segs.e: These five fatal wounds lead to a place of loss, to hell.”
Numbered Discourses 5.130
13. Sick
Loss
“Mendicants, there are these five losses.
What five?
Loss of relatives, wealth, health, ethics, and view.

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, sattā ñātibyasanahetu vā bhogabyasanahetu vā rogabyasanahetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: It is not because of loss of relatives, wealth, or health that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Sīlabyasanahetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā diṭṭhibyasanahetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: It is because of loss of ethics or view that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.
These are the five losses.
There are these five endowments.
What five?
Endowment with relatives, wealth, health, ethics, and view.

segs.p: Na, bhikkhave, sattā ñātisampadāhetu vā bhogasampadāhetu vā ārogyasampadāhetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: It is not because of endowment with relatives, wealth, or health that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Sīlasampadāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā diṭṭhisampadāhetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: It is because of endowment with ethics or view that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.
These are the five endowments.”
Numbered Discourses 5.131
14. Kings
Wielding Power (1st)

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rājā cakkavattī dhammeneva cakkaṁ vatteti;
segs.e: “Mendicants, possessing five factors a wheel-turning monarch wields power only in a principled manner.

segs.p: taṁ hoti cakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ kenaci manussabhūtena paccatthikena pāṇinā.
segs.e: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī atthaññū ca hoti, dhammaññū ca, mattaññū ca, kālaññū ca, parisaññū ca.
segs.e: A wheel-turning monarch knows what is right, knows principle, knows moderation, knows the right time, and knows the assembly.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi aṅgehi samannāgato rājā cakkavattī dhammeneva cakkaṁ pavatteti;
segs.e: A wheel-turning monarch who possesses these five factors wields power only in a principled manner.

segs.p: taṁ hoti cakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ kenaci manussabhūtena paccatthikena pāṇinā.
segs.e: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho dhammeneva anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavatteti;
segs.e: In the same way, possessing five qualities a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha rolls forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma only in a principled manner.

segs.p: taṁ hoti cakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: And that wheel cannot be rolled back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho atthaññū, dhammaññū, mattaññū, kālaññū, parisaññū.
segs.e: A Realized One knows what is right, knows principle, knows moderation, knows the right time, and knows the assembly.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho dhammeneva anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavatteti;
segs.e: Possessing these five qualities a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha rolls forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma only in a principled manner.

segs.p: taṁ hoti dhammacakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: And that wheel cannot be rolled back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 5.132
14. Kings
Wielding Power (2nd)

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño cakkavattissa jeṭṭho putto pitarā pavattitaṁ cakkaṁ dhammeneva anuppavatteti;
segs.e: “Mendicants, possessing five factors a wheel-turning monarch’s eldest son continues to wield the power set in motion by his father only in a principled manner.

segs.p: taṁ hoti cakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ kenaci manussabhūtena paccatthikena pāṇinā.
segs.e: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño cakkavattissa jeṭṭho putto atthaññū ca hoti, dhammaññū ca, mattaññū ca, kālaññū ca, parisaññū ca.
segs.e: A wheel-turning monarch’s oldest son knows what is right, knows principle, knows moderation, knows the right time, and knows the assembly.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño cakkavattissa jeṭṭho putto pitarā pavattitaṁ cakkaṁ dhammeneva anuppavatteti;
segs.e: A wheel-turning monarch’s oldest son who possesses these five factors continues to wield the power set in motion by his father only in a principled manner.

segs.p: taṁ hoti cakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ kenaci manussabhūtena paccatthikena pāṇinā.
segs.e: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato sāriputto tathāgatena anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavattitaṁ sammadeva anuppavatteti;
segs.e: In the same way, possessing five qualities Sāriputta rightly keeps rolling the supreme Wheel of Dhamma that was rolled forth by the Realized One.

segs.p: taṁ hoti cakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: And that wheel cannot be turned back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, sāriputto atthaññū, dhammaññū, mattaññū, kālaññū, parisaññū.
segs.e: Sāriputta knows what is right, knows principle, knows moderation, knows the right time, and knows the assembly.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato sāriputto tathāgatena anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavattitaṁ sammadeva anuppavatteti;
segs.e: Possessing these five qualities Sāriputta rightly keeps rolling the supreme Wheel of Dhamma that was rolled forth by the Realized One.

segs.p: taṁ hoti cakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: And that wheel cannot be turned back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 5.133
14. Kings
A Principled King

segs.p: “Yopi so, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā, sopi na arājakaṁ cakkaṁ vattetī”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, even a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king, does not wield power without having their own king.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “ko pana, bhante, rañño cakkavattissa dhammikassa dhammarañño rājā”ti?
segs.e: “But who is the king of the wheel-turning monarch, the just and principled king?”
“It is principle, monk,” said the Buddha.

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhu, rājā cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaññeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahati antojanasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Monk, a wheel-turning monarch provides just protection and security for his court, relying only on principle—honoring, respecting, and venerating principle, having principle as his flag, banner, and authority.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, rājā cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaññeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahati khattiyesu anuyantesu …pe… balakāyasmiṁ brāhmaṇagahapatikesu negamajānapadesu samaṇabrāhmaṇesu migapakkhīsu.
segs.e: He provides just protection and security for his aristocrats, vassals, troops, brahmins and householders, people of town and country, ascetics and brahmins, beasts and birds.

segs.p: Sa kho so, bhikkhu, rājā cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaññeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahitvā antojanasmiṁ dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahitvā khattiyesu anuyantesu balakāyasmiṁ brāhmaṇagahapatikesu negamajānapadesu samaṇabrāhmaṇesu migapakkhīsu dhammeneva cakkaṁ pavatteti;
segs.e: When he has done this, he wields power only in a principled manner.

segs.p: taṁ hoti cakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ kenaci manussabhūtena paccatthikena pāṇinā.
segs.e: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhu, tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaññeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahati bhikkhūsu:
segs.e: In the same way, monk, a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, a just and principled king, provides just protection and security for the monks, relying only on principle—honoring, respecting, and venerating principle, having principle as his flag, banner, and authority.

segs.p: ‘evarūpaṁ kāyakammaṁ sevitabbaṁ, evarūpaṁ kāyakammaṁ na sevitabbaṁ;
segs.e: ‘This kind of bodily action should be cultivated. This kind of bodily action should not be cultivated.

segs.p: evarūpaṁ vacīkammaṁ sevitabbaṁ, evarūpaṁ vacīkammaṁ na sevitabbaṁ;
segs.e: This kind of verbal action should be cultivated. This kind of verbal action should not be cultivated.

segs.p: evarūpaṁ manokammaṁ sevitabbaṁ, evarūpaṁ manokammaṁ na sevitabbaṁ;
segs.e: This kind of mental action should be cultivated. This kind of mental action should not be cultivated.

segs.p: evarūpo ājīvo sevitabbo, evarūpo ājīvo na sevitabbo;
segs.e: This kind of livelihood should be cultivated. This kind of livelihood should not be cultivated.

segs.p: evarūpo gāmanigamo sevitabbo, evarūpo gāmanigamo na sevitabbo’ti.
segs.e: This kind of village or town should be cultivated. This kind of village or town should not be cultivated.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaññeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahati bhikkhunīsu …pe… upāsakesu …pe… upāsikāsu:
segs.e: In the same way, monk, a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, a just and principled king, provides just protection and security for the nuns … laymen … laywomen, relying only on principle—honoring, respecting, and venerating principle, having principle as his flag, banner, and authority.

segs.p: ‘evarūpaṁ kāyakammaṁ sevitabbaṁ, evarūpaṁ kāyakammaṁ na sevitabbaṁ;
segs.e: ‘This kind of bodily action should be cultivated. This kind of bodily action should not be cultivated.

segs.p: evarūpaṁ vacīkammaṁ sevitabbaṁ, evarūpaṁ vacīkammaṁ na sevitabbaṁ;
segs.e: This kind of verbal action should be cultivated. This kind of verbal action should not be cultivated.

segs.p: evarūpaṁ manokammaṁ sevitabbaṁ, evarūpaṁ manokammaṁ na sevitabbaṁ;
segs.e: This kind of mental action should be cultivated. This kind of mental action should not be cultivated.

segs.p: evarūpo ājīvo sevitabbo, evarūpo ājīvo na sevitabbo;
segs.e: This kind of livelihood should be cultivated. This kind of livelihood should not be cultivated.

segs.p: evarūpo gāmanigamo sevitabbo, evarūpo gāmanigamo na sevitabbo’ti.
segs.e: This kind of village or town should be cultivated. This kind of village or town should not be cultivated.’

segs.p: Sa kho so, bhikkhu, tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaññeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahitvā bhikkhūsu, dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahitvā bhikkhunīsu, dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahitvā upāsakesu, dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahitvā upāsikāsu dhammeneva anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavatteti;
segs.e: When a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has provided just protection and security for the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, he rolls forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma only in a principled manner.

segs.p: taṁ hoti cakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: And that wheel cannot be rolled back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 5.134
14. Kings
In Whatever Region

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto yassaṁ yassaṁ disāyaṁ viharati, sakasmiṁyeva vijite viharati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, with five factors an anointed aristocratic king lives in his own realm, no matter what region he lives in.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto ubhato sujāto hoti mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena;
segs.e: An anointed aristocratic king is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.
He is rich, affluent, and wealthy, with a full treasury and storehouses.

segs.p: balavā kho pana hoti caturaṅginiyā senāya samannāgato assavāya ovādapaṭikarāya;
segs.e: He is powerful, having an army of four divisions that is obedient and carries out instructions.

segs.p: pariṇāyako kho panassa hoti paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī paṭibalo atītānāgatapaccuppanne atthe cintetuṁ;
segs.e: He has a commander who is astute, competent, and intelligent, able to think issues through as they bear upon the past, future, and present.
These four things bring his glory to fruition.

segs.p: So iminā yasapañcamena dhammena samannāgato yassaṁ yassaṁ disāyaṁ viharati, sakasmiṁyeva vijite viharati.
segs.e: With these five qualities, including glory, an anointed aristocratic king lives in his own realm, no matter what direction he lives in.
Why is that?
Because that is how it is for victors.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu yassaṁ yassaṁ disāyaṁ viharati, vimuttacittova viharati.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities lives with mind freed, no matter what region they live in.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu—
segs.e: It’s when mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.
This is like the anointed aristocratic king’s impeccable birth.

segs.p: bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā—
segs.e: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segs.p: rājāva khattiyo muddhāvasitto aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo paripuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāro;
segs.e: This is like the anointed aristocratic king being rich, affluent, and wealthy, with full treasury and storehouses.

segs.p: āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu—
segs.e: They live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.
This is like the anointed aristocratic king having power.

segs.p: paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā—
segs.e: They’re wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.
This is like the anointed aristocratic king having a commander.
These four qualities bring their freedom to fruition.

segs.p: So iminā vimuttipañcamena dhammena samannāgato yassaṁ yassaṁ disāyaṁ viharati vimuttacittova viharati.
segs.e: With these five qualities, including freedom, they live in their own realm, no matter what region they live in.
Why is that?
Because that is how it is for those whose mind is free.”
Numbered Discourses 5.135
14. Kings
Aspiration (1st)

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa jeṭṭho putto rajjaṁ pattheti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, an anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son with five factors aspires to kingship.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa jeṭṭho putto ubhato sujāto hoti mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena;
segs.e: It’s when an anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

segs.p: abhirūpo hoti dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato;
segs.e: He is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.
He is dear and beloved to his parents.
He is dear and beloved to the people of town and country.

segs.p: yāni tāni raññaṁ khattiyānaṁ muddhāvasittānaṁ sippaṭṭhānāni hatthismiṁ vā assasmiṁ vā rathasmiṁ vā dhanusmiṁ vā tharusmiṁ vā tattha sikkhito hoti anavayo.
segs.e: He is trained and skilled in the arts of anointed aristocratic kings, such as elephant riding, horse riding, driving a chariot, archery, and swordsmanship.
He thinks:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ khomhi ubhato sujāto mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena.
segs.e: ‘I’m well born on both my mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.
Why shouldn’t I aspire to kingship?

segs.p: Ahaṁ khomhi abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato.
segs.e: I’m attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.
Why shouldn’t I aspire to kingship?
I’m dear and beloved to my parents.
Why shouldn’t I aspire to kingship?
I’m dear and beloved to the people of town and country.
Why shouldn’t I aspire to kingship?

segs.p: Ahaṁ khomhi yāni tāni raññaṁ khattiyānaṁ muddhāvasittānaṁ sippaṭṭhānāni hatthismiṁ vā assasmiṁ vā rathasmiṁ vā dhanusmiṁ vā tharusmiṁ vā, tattha sikkhito anavayo.
segs.e: I’m trained and skilled in the arts of anointed aristocratic kings, such as elephant riding, horse riding, driving a chariot, archery, and swordsmanship.
Why shouldn’t I aspire to kingship?’

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa jeṭṭho putto rajjaṁ pattheti.
segs.e: An anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son with these five factors aspires to kingship.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pattheti.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities aspires to end the defilements.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṁ:
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Appābādho hoti appātaṅko, samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya majjhimāya padhānakkhamāya;
segs.e: They are rarely ill or unwell. Their stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold, but just right, and fit for meditation.

segs.p: asaṭho hoti amāyāvī, yathābhūtaṁ attānaṁ āvikattā satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu;
segs.e: They’re not devious or deceitful. They reveal themselves honestly to the Teacher or sensible spiritual companions.

segs.p: āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu;
segs.e: They live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

segs.p: paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
segs.e: They’re wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.
They think:
‘I am a person of faith; I have faith in the Realized One’s awakening …

segs.p: “itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā”ti.

segs.e: Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?

segs.p: Ahaṁ khomhi appābādho appātaṅko samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya majjhimāya padhānakkhamāya.
segs.e: I’m rarely ill or unwell. My stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold, but just right, and fit for meditation.
Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?

segs.p: Ahaṁ khomhi asaṭho amāyāvī yathābhūtaṁ attānaṁ āvikattā satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu.
segs.e: I’m not devious or deceitful. I reveal myself honestly to the Teacher or sensible spiritual companions.
Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?

segs.p: Ahaṁ khomhi āraddhavīriyo viharāmi akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.
segs.e: I live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. I’m strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.
Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?

segs.p: Ahaṁ khomhi paññavā udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
segs.e: I’m wise. I have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.
Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?’

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ patthetī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities aspires to end the defilements.”
Numbered Discourses 5.136
14. Kings
Aspiration (2nd)

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa jeṭṭho putto oparajjaṁ pattheti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, an anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son with five factors aspires to become a viceroy.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa jeṭṭho putto ubhato sujāto hoti mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena;
segs.e: It’s when an anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

segs.p: abhirūpo hoti dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato;
segs.e: He is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.
He is dear and beloved to his parents.
He is dear and beloved to the armed forces.

segs.p: paṇḍito hoti viyatto medhāvī paṭibalo atītānāgatapaccuppanne atthe cintetuṁ.
segs.e: He is astute, competent, and intelligent, able to think issues through as they bear upon the past, future, and present.
He thinks:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ khomhi ubhato sujāto mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena.
segs.e: ‘I’m well born …

segs.p: Ahaṁ khomhi abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato.
segs.e: attractive …
dear and beloved to my parents …
dear and beloved to the armed forces …

segs.p: Ahaṁ khomhi paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī paṭibalo atītānāgatapaccuppanne atthe cintetuṁ.
segs.e: I’m astute, competent, and intelligent, able to think issues through as they bear upon the past, future, and present.
Why shouldn’t I aspire to become a viceroy?’

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa jeṭṭho putto oparajjaṁ pattheti.
segs.e: An anointed aristocratic king’s eldest son with these five factors aspires to become a viceroy.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pattheti.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities aspires to end the defilements.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s totally full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, reciting them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.
Their mind is firmly established in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

segs.p: āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu;
segs.e: They live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

segs.p: paññavā hoti, udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
segs.e: They’re wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.
They think:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ khomhi sīlavā, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharāmi ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhāmi sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: ‘I’m ethical …

segs.p: Ahaṁ khomhi bahussuto sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpā me dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
segs.e: learned …
mindful …

segs.p: Ahaṁ khomhi āraddhavīriyo viharāmi akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.
segs.e: energetic …

segs.p: Ahaṁ khomhi paññavā udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.
segs.e: wise. I have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.
Why shouldn’t I aspire to end the defilements?’

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ patthetī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities aspires to end the defilements.”
Numbered Discourses 5.137
14. Kings
Little Sleep

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, appaṁ rattiyā supanti, bahuṁ jagganti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these five sleep little at night, staying mostly awake.
What five?

segs.p: Itthī, bhikkhave, purisādhippāyā appaṁ rattiyā supati, bahuṁ jaggati.
segs.e: A woman longing for a man.

segs.p: Puriso, bhikkhave, itthādhippāyo appaṁ rattiyā supati, bahuṁ jaggati.
segs.e: A man longing for a woman.

segs.p: Coro, bhikkhave, ādānādhippāyo appaṁ rattiyā supati, bahuṁ jaggati.
segs.e: A thief longing for their loot.

segs.p: Rājā, bhikkhave, rājakaraṇīyesu yutto appaṁ rattiyā supati, bahuṁ jaggati.
segs.e: A king busy with his duties.

segs.p: Bhikkhu, bhikkhave, visaṁyogādhippāyo appaṁ rattiyā supati, bahuṁ jaggati.
segs.e: A mendicant longing for freedom from the yoke.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca appaṁ rattiyā supanti, bahuṁ jaggantī”ti.
segs.e: These five sleep little at night, staying mostly awake.”
Numbered Discourses 5.138
14. Kings
Eating Food

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño nāgo bhattādako ca hoti okāsapharaṇo ca laṇḍasāraṇo ca salākaggāhī ca rañño nāgotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a royal bull elephant with five factors eats food, takes up space, drops dung, and takes a ticket, yet is still reckoned a royal bull elephant.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti rūpānaṁ, akkhamo saddānaṁ, akkhamo gandhānaṁ, akkhamo rasānaṁ, akkhamo phoṭṭhabbānaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant can’t endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño nāgo bhattādako ca okāsapharaṇo ca laṇḍasāraṇo ca salākaggāhī ca, rañño nāgotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: A royal bull elephant with these five factors eats food, takes up space, drops dung, and takes a ticket, yet is still reckoned a royal bull elephant.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhattādako ca hoti, okāsapharaṇo ca mañcapīṭhamaddano ca salākaggāhī ca, bhikkhutveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities eats food, takes up space, tramples beds and chairs, and takes a ticket, yet is still reckoned a mendicant.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkhamo hoti rūpānaṁ, akkhamo saddānaṁ, akkhamo gandhānaṁ, akkhamo rasānaṁ, akkhamo phoṭṭhabbānaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant can’t endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhattādako ca hoti okāsapharaṇo ca mañcapīṭhamaddano ca salākaggāhī ca, bhikkhutveva saṅkhaṁ gacchatī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities eats food, takes up space, tramples beds and chairs, and takes a ticket, yet is still reckoned a mendicant.”
Numbered Discourses 5.139
14. Kings
Cannot Endure

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño nāgo na rājāraho hoti na rājabhoggo, na rañño aṅgaṁtveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a royal bull elephant with five factors is not worthy of a king, not fit to serve a king, and is not reckoned a factor of kingship.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti rūpānaṁ, akkhamo saddānaṁ, akkhamo gandhānaṁ, akkhamo rasānaṁ, akkhamo phoṭṭhabbānaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant can’t endure sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti rūpānaṁ?
segs.e: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can’t endure sights?

segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant gone to battle falters and founders at the sight of a division of elephants, of cavalry, of chariots, or of infantry. It doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti rūpānaṁ.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant can’t endure sights.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti saddānaṁ?
segs.e: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can’t endure sounds?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo saṅgāmagato hatthisaddaṁ vā sutvā assasaddaṁ vā sutvā rathasaddaṁ vā sutvā pattisaddaṁ vā sutvā bheripaṇavasaṅkhatiṇavaninnādasaddaṁ vā sutvā saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ.
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant gone to battle falters and founders at the sound of a division of elephants, of cavalry, of chariots, or of infantry, or the thunder of the drums, kettledrums, horns, and cymbals. It doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti saddānaṁ.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant can’t endure sounds.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti gandhānaṁ?
segs.e: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can’t endure smells?

segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant gone to battle falters and founders when it smells the odor of the feces and urine of battle-hardened, pedigree royal bull elephants. It doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti gandhānaṁ.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant can’t endure smells.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti rasānaṁ?
segs.e: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can’t endure tastes?

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti rasānaṁ.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant can’t endure tastes.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti phoṭṭhabbānaṁ?
segs.e: And how is it that a royal bull elephant can’t endure touches?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo saṅgāmagato ekena vā saravegena viddho, dvīhi vā tīhi vā catūhi vā pañcahi vā saravegehi viddho saṁsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati na sakkoti saṅgāmaṁ otarituṁ.
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant gone to battle falters and founders when struck by a swift arrow, or by two, three, four, or five swift arrows. It doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo akkhamo hoti phoṭṭhabbānaṁ.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant can’t endure touches.

segs.e: And how is it that a mendicant can’t endure sights?

Numbered Discourses 5.140
14. Kings
A Listener

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño nāgo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅgaṁtveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a royal bull elephant with five factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo sotā ca hoti, hantā ca, rakkhitā ca, khantā ca, gantā ca.
segs.e: A royal bull elephant listens, destroys, protects, endures, and goes fast.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo sotā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a royal bull elephant listen?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo yamenaṁ hatthidammasārathi kāraṇaṁ kāreti—
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens to whatever task the elephant trainer has it do,

segs.p: yadi vā katapubbaṁ yadi vā akatapubbaṁ—
segs.e: whether or not it has done it before.

segs.p: taṁ aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbaṁ cetasā samannāharitvā ohitasoto suṇāti.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo sotā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant listens.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo hantā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a royal bull elephant destroy?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo saṅgāmagato hatthimpi hanati, hatthāruhampi hanati, assampi hanati, assāruhampi hanati, rathampi hanati, rathikampi hanati, pattikampi hanati.
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle destroys elephants with their riders, horses with their riders, chariots and charioteers, and foot soldiers.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo hantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant destroys.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo rakkhitā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a royal bull elephant protect?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo saṅgāmagato rakkhati purimaṁ kāyaṁ, rakkhati pacchimaṁ kāyaṁ, rakkhati purime pāde, rakkhati pacchime pāde, rakkhati sīsaṁ, rakkhati kaṇṇe, rakkhati dante, rakkhati soṇḍaṁ, rakkhati vāladhiṁ, rakkhati hatthāruhaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle protects its fore-quarters and hind-quarters, its fore-feet and hind-feet, and its head, ears, tusks, trunk, tail, and rider.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo rakkhitā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant protects.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo khantā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a royal bull elephant endure?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo saṅgāmagato khamo hoti sattippahārānaṁ asippahārānaṁ usuppahārānaṁ pharasuppahārānaṁ bheripaṇavasaṅkhatiṇavaninnādasaddānaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle endures being struck by spears, swords, arrows, and axes; it endures the thunder of the drums, kettledrums, horns, and cymbals.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo khantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant endures.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo gantā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a royal bull elephant go fast?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo yamenaṁ hatthidammasārathi disaṁ peseti—
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant swiftly goes in whatever direction the elephant trainer sends it,

segs.p: yadi vā gatapubbaṁ yadi vā agatapubbaṁ—
segs.e: whether or not it has been there before.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo gantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant goes fast.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño nāgo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅgantveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: A royal bull elephant with these five factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sotā ca hoti, hantā ca, rakkhitā ca, khantā ca, gantā ca.
segs.e: A mendicant listens, destroys, protects, endures, and goes fast.
And how does a mendicant listen?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye desiyamāne aṭṭhiṅkatvā manasi katvā sabbaṁ cetasā samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṁ suṇāti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens when the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One is being taught.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sotā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant listens.
And how does a mendicant destroy?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṁ kāmavitakkaṁ nādhivāseti, pajahati vinodeti hanati byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti; uppannaṁ byāpādavitakkaṁ …pe… uppannaṁ vihiṁsāvitakkaṁ …pe… uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti, pajahati vinodeti hanati byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t tolerate a sensual, malicious, or cruel thought. They don’t tolerate any bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen, but give them up, dispel them, calm them, eliminate them, and obliterate them.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant destroys.
And how does a mendicant protect?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.
segs.e: When a mendicant sees a sight with the eyes, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ cakkhundriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati; rakkhati cakkhundriyaṁ; cakkhundriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving its restraint.
Hearing a sound with their ears …
Smelling an odor with their nose …
Tasting a flavor with their tongue …
Encountering a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.
segs.e: Knowing an idea with their mind, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ manindriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati; rakkhati manindriyaṁ; manindriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rakkhitā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant protects.
And how does a mendicant endure?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya ḍaṁsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṁ; duruttānaṁ durāgatānaṁ vacanapathānaṁ uppannānaṁ sārīrikānaṁ vedanānaṁ dukkhānaṁ tibbānaṁ kharānaṁ kaṭukānaṁ asātānaṁ amanāpānaṁ pāṇaharānaṁ adhivāsakajātiko hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant endures cold, heat, hunger, and thirst; the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles; rude and unwelcome criticism; and puts up with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant endures.
And how does a mendicant go fast?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yā sā disā agatapubbā iminā dīghena addhunā, yadidaṁ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṁ, taṁ khippaññeva gantā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant swiftly goes in the direction they’ve never gone before in all this long time; that is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant goes fast.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 5.141
15. At Tikaṇḍakī
Scorn
“Mendicants, these five individuals are found in the world.
What five?

segs.p: Datvā avajānāti, saṁvāsena avajānāti, ādheyyamukho hoti, lolo hoti, mando momūho hoti.
segs.e: One gives then scorns, one lives together then scorns, one is gullible for gossip, one is impulsive, and one is dull and stupid.
And how does an individual give then scorn?
It’s when an individual gives an individual robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.
They think:
‘I give;
this one receives.’
They give to them, then they scorn them.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo datvā avajānāti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual gives then scorns.
And how does an individual live together then scorn?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, puggalo puggalena saddhiṁ saṁvasati dve vā tīṇi vā vassāni.
segs.e: It’s when an individual lives with someone else for two or three years.
They live together with them, then they scorn them.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo saṁvāsena avajānāti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual lives together then scorns.
And how is an individual gullible for gossip?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo parassa vaṇṇe vā avaṇṇe vā bhāsiyamāne taṁ khippaññeva adhimuccitā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when they’re very quick to believe what a certain individual says in praise or criticism of another.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo ādheyyamukho hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is gullible for gossip.
And how is an individual impulsive?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ittarasaddho hoti ittarabhattī ittarapemo ittarappasādo.
segs.e: It’s when a certain individual is fickle in faith, devotion, fondness, and confidence.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo lolo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is impulsive.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo mando momūho hoti?
segs.e: And how is an individual dull and stupid?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo kusalākusale dhamme na jānāti, sāvajjānavajje dhamme na jānāti, hīnappaṇīte dhamme na jānāti, kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāge dhamme na jānāti.
segs.e: It’s when they don’t know the difference between qualities that are skillful and unskillful, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, and those with a portion of dark or bright.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo mando momūho hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is dull and stupid.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the five individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 5.142
15. At Tikaṇḍakī
Transgression
“Mendicants, these five individuals are found in the world.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ārabhati ca vippaṭisārī ca hoti;
segs.e: One individual transgresses and regrets it.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti.
segs.e: And they don’t truly understand the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where those arisen bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ārabhati, na vippaṭisārī hoti;
segs.e: One individual transgresses and doesn’t regret it.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti.
segs.e: And they don’t understand …

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo na ārabhati, vippaṭisārī hoti;
segs.e: One individual doesn’t transgress yet still feels regret.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti.
segs.e: And they don’t understand …

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo na ārabhati na vippaṭisārī hoti;
segs.e: One individual neither transgresses nor regrets.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti.
segs.e: But they don’t understand …

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo na ārabhati na vippaṭisārī hoti;
segs.e: One individual neither transgresses nor regrets.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti.
segs.e: And they do understand where those arisen bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo ārabhati ca vippaṭisārī ca hoti,
segs.e: Take the case of the individual who transgresses and regrets it.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti,
segs.e: And they don’t truly understand the freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom where those arisen bad, unskillful qualities cease without remainder.
They should be told:

segs.p: ‘āyasmato kho ārambhajā āsavā saṁvijjanti, vippaṭisārajā āsavā pavaḍḍhanti, sādhu vatāyasmā ārambhaje āsave pahāya vippaṭisāraje āsave paṭivinodetvā cittaṁ paññañca bhāvetu;
segs.e: ‘Venerable, the defilements born of transgression are found in you, and the defilements born of regret grow. You would do well to give up the defilements born of transgression and dispel the defilements born of regret, and then develop the mind and wisdom.

segs.p: evamāyasmā amunā pañcamena puggalena samasamo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: In this way you’ll become just like the fifth individual.’

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo ārabhati na vippaṭisārī hoti,
segs.e: Take the case of the individual who transgresses and doesn’t regret it.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti,
segs.e: And they don’t understand …
They should be told:

segs.p: ‘āyasmato kho ārambhajā āsavā saṁvijjanti, vippaṭisārajā āsavā na pavaḍḍhanti, sādhu vatāyasmā ārambhaje āsave pahāya cittaṁ paññañca bhāvetu;
segs.e: ‘Venerable, the defilements born of transgression are found in you, but the defilements born of regret don’t grow. You would do well to give up the defilements born of transgression, and then develop the mind and wisdom.

segs.p: evamāyasmā amunā pañcamena puggalena samasamo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: In this way you’ll become just like the fifth individual.’

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo na ārabhati vippaṭisārī hoti,
segs.e: Take the case of the individual who doesn’t transgress yet feels regret.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti,
segs.e: And they don’t understand …
They should be told:

segs.p: ‘āyasmato kho ārambhajā āsavā na saṁvijjanti, vippaṭisārajā āsavā pavaḍḍhanti, sādhu vatāyasmā vippaṭisāraje āsave paṭivinodetvā cittaṁ paññañca bhāvetu;
segs.e: ‘Venerable, the defilements born of transgression are not found in you, yet the defilements born of regret grow. You would do well to dispel the defilements born of regret, and then develop the mind and wisdom.

segs.p: evamāyasmā amunā pañcamena puggalena samasamo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: In this way you’ll become just like the fifth individual.’

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo na ārabhati na vippaṭisārī hoti,
segs.e: Take the case of the individual who neither transgresses nor regrets.

segs.p: tañca cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti yatthassa te uppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti,
segs.e: But they don’t understand …
They should be told:

segs.p: ‘āyasmato kho ārambhajā āsavā na saṁvijjanti, vippaṭisārajā āsavā na pavaḍḍhanti, sādhu vatāyasmā cittaṁ paññañca bhāvetu;
segs.e: ‘Venerable, the defilements born of transgression are not found in you, and the defilements born of regret don’t grow. You would do well to develop the mind and wisdom.

segs.p: evamāyasmā amunā pañcamena puggalena samasamo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: In this way you’ll become just like the fifth individual.’

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, ime cattāro puggalā amunā pañcamena puggalena evaṁ ovadiyamānā evaṁ anusāsiyamānā anupubbena āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpuṇantī”ti.
segs.e: And so, mendicants, when these four individuals are advised and instructed by comparison with the fifth individual, they gradually attain the ending of defilements.”
Numbered Discourses 5.143
15. At Tikaṇḍakī
At Sārandada

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Vesālī for alms.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena pañcamattānaṁ licchavisatānaṁ sārandade cetiye sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: Now at that time around five hundred Licchavis were sitting together at the Sārandada Shrine, and this discussion came up among them,
“The appearance of five treasures is rare in the world.
What five?

segs.p: Hatthiratanassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ, assaratanassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ, maṇiratanassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ, itthiratanassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ, gahapatiratanassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: The elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, and the householder-treasure.

segs.p: Imesaṁ pañcannaṁ ratanānaṁ pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: The appearance of these five treasures is rare in the world.”

segs.p: Atha kho te licchavī magge purisaṁ ṭhapesuṁ:
segs.e: Then those Licchavis sent a man out on to the road, saying,

segs.p: “yadā tvaṁ, ambho purisa, passeyyāsi bhagavantaṁ, atha amhākaṁ āroceyyāsī”ti.
segs.e: “My man, please tell us when you see the Buddha.”

segs.p: Addasā kho so puriso bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ;
segs.e: That man saw the Buddha coming off in the distance.

segs.p: disvāna yena te licchavī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te licchavī etadavoca:
segs.e: He went to the Licchavis and said,

segs.p: “ayaṁ so, bhante, bhagavā gacchati arahaṁ sammāsambuddho;
segs.e: “Sirs, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha is coming.
Please go at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho te licchavī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho te licchavī bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then those Licchavis went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhante, yena sārandadaṁ cetiyaṁ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā”ti.
segs.e: “Please go to the Sārandada Shrine, out of sympathy.”
The Buddha consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā yena sārandadaṁ cetiyaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā te licchavī etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha went up to the Sārandada Shrine. He sat down on the seat spread out and said to the Licchavis,

segs.p: “kāya nuttha, licchavī, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā, kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā”ti?
segs.e: “Licchavis, what were you sitting talking about just now? What conversation was left unfinished?”

segs.p: “Idha, bhante, amhākaṁ sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: “Well, sir, this discussion came up among us while we were sitting together:
‘The appearance of five treasures is rare in the world. …’”

segs.p: Hatthiratanassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ, assaratanassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ, maṇiratanassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ, itthiratanassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ, gahapatiratanassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
Imesaṁ pañcannaṁ ratanānaṁ pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmin’”ti.
“Kāmādhimuttānaṁ vata bho licchavīnaṁ kāmaṁyeva ārabbha antarākathā udapādi.
segs.e: “You Licchavis are so fixated on sensual pleasures, that’s the only discussion that came up!

segs.p: Pañcannaṁ, licchavī, ratanānaṁ pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: Licchavis, the appearance of five treasures is rare in the world.
What five?

segs.p: Tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ,
segs.e: The appearance of a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: tathāgatappaveditassa dhammavinayassa desetā puggalo dullabho lokasmiṁ,
segs.e: A teacher of the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One.

segs.p: tathāgatappaveditassa dhammavinayassa desitassa viññātā puggalo dullabho lokasmiṁ,
segs.e: An individual who understands the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One.

segs.p: tathāgatappaveditassa dhammavinayassa desitassa viññātā dhammānudhammappaṭipanno puggalo dullabho lokasmiṁ,
segs.e: An individual who practices in line with the teaching.
An individual who is grateful and thankful.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, licchavī, pañcannaṁ ratanānaṁ pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: The appearance of these five treasures is rare in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 5.144
15. At Tikaṇḍakī
At Tikaṇḍakī

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sākete viharati tikaṇḍakīvane.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāketa in Tikaṇḍakī Wood.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kālena kālaṁ appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant would do well to meditate from time to time perceiving the following: the repulsive in the unrepulsive,

segs.p: Sādhu, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kālena kālaṁ paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya.
segs.e: the unrepulsive in the repulsive,

segs.p: Sādhu, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kālena kālaṁ appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya.
segs.e: the repulsive in both the unrepulsive and the repulsive, and

segs.p: Sādhu, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kālena kālaṁ paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya.
segs.e: the unrepulsive in both the repulsive and the unrepulsive.

segs.p: Sādhu, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kālena kālaṁ paṭikūlañca appaṭikūlañca tadubhayaṁ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyya sato sampajāno.
segs.e: A mendicant would do well to meditate from time to time staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive.

segs.p: Kiñca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthavasaṁ paṭicca appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya?
segs.e: For what reason should a mendicant meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive?
‘May greed not arise in me for things that arouse greed.’

segs.p: idaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthavasaṁ paṭicca appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya.
segs.e: A mendicant should meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive for this reason.

segs.p: Kiñca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthavasaṁ paṭicca paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya?
segs.e: For what reason should a mendicant meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive?
‘May hate not arise in me for things that provoke hate.’ …

segs.p: idaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthavasaṁ paṭicca paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya.
Kiñca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthavasaṁ paṭicca appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya?
segs.e: For what reason should a mendicant meditate perceiving the repulsive in both the unrepulsive and the repulsive?

segs.p: ‘Mā me rajanīyesu dhammesu rāgo udapādi, mā me dosanīyesu dhammesu doso udapādī’ti—
segs.e: ‘May greed not arise in me for things that arouse greed. May hate not arise in me for things that provoke hate.’ …

segs.p: idaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthavasaṁ paṭicca appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya.
Kiñca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthavasaṁ paṭicca paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya?
segs.e: For what reason should a mendicant meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in both the repulsive and the unrepulsive?

segs.p: ‘Mā me dosanīyesu dhammesu doso udapādi, mā me rajanīyesu dhammesu rāgo udapādī’ti—
segs.e: ‘May hate not arise in me for things that provoke hate. May greed not arise in me for things that arouse greed.’ …

segs.p: idaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthavasaṁ paṭicca paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya.
Kiñca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthavasaṁ paṭicca paṭikūlañca appaṭikūlañca tadubhayaṁ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyya?
segs.e: For what reason should a mendicant meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive?

segs.p: ‘Sato sampajāno mā me kvacani katthaci kiñcanaṁ rajanīyesu dhammesu rāgo udapādi, mā me kvacani katthaci kiñcanaṁ dosanīyesu dhammesu doso udapādi, mā me kvacani katthaci kiñcanaṁ mohanīyesu dhammesu moho udapādī’ti—
segs.e: ‘May no greed for things that arouse greed, hate for things that provoke hate, or delusion for things that promote delusion arise in me in any way at all.’

segs.p: idaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu atthavasaṁ paṭicca paṭikūlañca appaṭikūlañca tadubhayaṁ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyya sato sampajāno”ti.
segs.e: For this reason a mendicant should meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive.”
Numbered Discourses 5.145
15. At Tikaṇḍakī
Hell

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī hoti.
segs.e: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, and consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.146
15. At Tikaṇḍakī
A Friend

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu mitto na sevitabbo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, you shouldn’t associate with a mendicant friend who has five qualities.
What five?

segs.p: Kammantaṁ kāreti, adhikaraṇaṁ ādiyati, pāmokkhesu bhikkhūsu paṭiviruddho hoti, dīghacārikaṁ anavatthacārikaṁ anuyutto viharati, nappaṭibalo hoti kālena kālaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetuṁ samādapetuṁ samuttejetuṁ sampahaṁsetuṁ.
segs.e: They start up work projects. They take up disciplinary issues. They conflict with leading mendicants. They like long and aimless wandering. They’re unable to educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire you from time to time with a Dhamma talk.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu mitto na sevitabbo.
segs.e: Mendicants, you shouldn’t associate with a mendicant friend who possesses these five qualities.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu mitto sevitabbo.
segs.e: You should associate with a mendicant friend who has five qualities.
What five?

segs.p: Na kammantaṁ kāreti, na adhikaraṇaṁ ādiyati, na pāmokkhesu bhikkhūsu paṭiviruddho hoti, na dīghacārikaṁ anavatthacārikaṁ anuyutto viharati, paṭibalo hoti kālena kālaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetuṁ samādapetuṁ samuttejetuṁ sampahaṁsetuṁ.
segs.e: They don’t start up work projects. They don’t take up disciplinary issues. They don’t conflict with leading mendicants. They don’t like long and aimless wandering. They’re able to educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire you from time to time with a Dhamma talk.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu mitto sevitabbo”ti.
segs.e: You should associate with a mendicant friend who possesses these five qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 5.147
15. At Tikaṇḍakī
Gifts of an Untrue Person
“Mendicants, there are these five gifts of an untrue person.
What five?

segs.p: Asakkaccaṁ deti, acittīkatvā deti, asahatthā deti, apaviddhaṁ deti, anāgamanadiṭṭhiko deti.
segs.e: They give carelessly. They give thoughtlessly. They don’t give with their own hand. They give the dregs. They give without consideration for consequences.
These are the five gifts of an untrue person.
There are these five gifts of a true person.
What five?

segs.p: Sakkaccaṁ deti, cittīkatvā deti, sahatthā deti, anapaviddhaṁ deti, āgamanadiṭṭhiko deti.
segs.e: They give carefully. They give thoughtfully. They give with their own hand. They don’t give the dregs. They give with consideration for consequences.
These are the five gifts of a true person.”
Numbered Discourses 5.148
15. At Tikaṇḍakī
Gifts of a True Person
“There are these five gifts of a true person.
What five?

segs.p: Saddhāya dānaṁ deti, sakkaccaṁ dānaṁ deti, kālena dānaṁ deti, anuggahitacitto dānaṁ deti, attānañca parañca anupahacca dānaṁ deti.
segs.e: They give a gift out of faith. They give a gift carefully. They give a gift at the right time. They give a gift with no strings attached. They give a gift without damaging themselves or others.

segs.p: Saddhāya kho pana, bhikkhave, dānaṁ datvā yattha yattha tassa dānassa vipāko nibbattati, aḍḍho ca hoti mahaddhano mahābhogo, abhirūpo ca hoti dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato.
segs.e: Having given a gift out of faith, in whatever place the result of that gift manifests they become rich, affluent, and wealthy. And they’re attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.

segs.p: Sakkaccaṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, dānaṁ datvā yattha yattha tassa dānassa vipāko nibbattati, aḍḍho ca hoti mahaddhano mahābhogo.
segs.e: Having given a gift carefully, in whatever place the result of that gift manifests they become rich, affluent, and wealthy.

segs.p: Yepissa te honti puttāti vā dārāti vā dāsāti vā pessāti vā kammakarāti vā, tepi sussūsanti sotaṁ odahanti aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapenti.
segs.e: And their children, wives, bondservants, servants, and workers want to listen. They actively listen and try to understand.

segs.p: Kālena kho pana, bhikkhave, dānaṁ datvā yattha yattha tassa dānassa vipāko nibbattati, aḍḍho ca hoti mahaddhano mahābhogo;
segs.e: Having given a gift at the right time, in whatever place the result of that gift manifests they become rich, affluent, and wealthy.
And when the time is right, their needs are amply satisfied.

segs.p: Anuggahitacitto kho pana, bhikkhave, dānaṁ datvā yattha yattha tassa dānassa vipāko nibbattati, aḍḍho ca hoti mahaddhano mahābhogo;
segs.e: Having given a gift with no strings attached, in whatever place the result of that gift manifests they become rich, affluent, and wealthy.

segs.p: uḷāresu ca pañcasu kāmaguṇesu bhogāya cittaṁ namati.
segs.e: And their mind tends to enjoy the five refined kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: Attānañca parañca anupahacca kho pana, bhikkhave, dānaṁ datvā yattha yattha tassa dānassa vipāko nibbattati, aḍḍho ca hoti mahaddhano mahābhogo;
segs.e: Having given a gift without damaging themselves or others, in whatever place the result of that gift manifests they become rich, affluent, and wealthy.

segs.p: na cassa kutoci bhogānaṁ upaghāto āgacchati aggito vā udakato vā rājato vā corato vā appiyato vā dāyādato.
segs.e: And no damage comes to their property from anywhere, whether fire, flood, rulers, bandits, or unloved heirs.
These are the five gifts of a true person.”
Numbered Discourses 5.149
15. At Tikaṇḍakī
Temporarily Free (1st)

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā samayavimuttassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these five things lead to the decline of a mendicant who is temporarily free.
What five?

segs.p: Kammārāmatā, bhassārāmatā, niddārāmatā, saṅgaṇikārāmatā, yathāvimuttaṁ cittaṁ na paccavekkhati.
segs.e: They relish work, talk, sleep, and company. And they don’t review the extent of their mind’s freedom.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā samayavimuttassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the decline of a mendicant who is temporarily free.

segs.p: Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā samayavimuttassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant who is temporarily free.
What five?

segs.p: Na kammārāmatā, na bhassārāmatā, na niddārāmatā, na saṅgaṇikārāmatā, yathāvimuttaṁ cittaṁ paccavekkhati.
segs.e: They don’t relish work, talk, sleep, and company. And they review the extent of their mind’s freedom.
