segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā samayavimuttassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant who is temporarily free.”
Numbered Discourses 5.150
15. At Tikaṇḍakī
Temporarily Free (2nd)

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā samayavimuttassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these five things lead to the decline of a mendicant who is temporarily free.
What five?

segs.p: Kammārāmatā, bhassārāmatā, niddārāmatā, indriyesu aguttadvāratā, bhojane amattaññutā.
segs.e: They relish work, talk, and sleep. They don’t guard the sense doors and they eat too much.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā samayavimuttassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the decline of a mendicant who is temporarily free.

segs.p: Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā samayavimuttassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant who is temporarily free.
What five?

segs.p: Na kammārāmatā, na bhassārāmatā, na niddārāmatā, indriyesu guttadvāratā, bhojane mattaññutā.
segs.e: They don’t relish work, talk, and sleep. They guard the sense doors and they have moderation in eating.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā samayavimuttassa bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These five things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant who is temporarily free.”
Numbered Discourses 5.151
16. The True Teaching
The Sure Path (1st)

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with five qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities even when listening to the true teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Kathaṁ paribhoti, kathikaṁ paribhoti, attānaṁ paribhoti, vikkhittacitto dhammaṁ suṇāti, anekaggacitto ayoniso ca manasi karoti.
segs.e: They disparage the talk, the speaker, or themselves. They listen with scattered and disunified mind. They apply the mind irrationally.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with these five qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, even when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with five qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Na kathaṁ paribhoti, na kathikaṁ paribhoti, na attānaṁ paribhoti, avikkhittacitto dhammaṁ suṇāti, ekaggacitto yoniso ca manasi karoti.
segs.e: They don’t disparage the talk, the speaker, or themselves. They listen with unscattered and unified mind. They apply the mind rationally.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattan”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these five qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 5.152
16. The True Teaching
The Sure Path (2nd)

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with five qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities even when listening to the true teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Kathaṁ paribhoti, kathikaṁ paribhoti, attānaṁ paribhoti, duppañño hoti jaḷo eḷamūgo, anaññāte aññātamānī hoti.
segs.e: They disparage the talk, the speaker, or themselves. They’re witless, dull, and idiotic. They think they know what they don’t know.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with these five qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, even when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with five qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Na kathaṁ paribhoti, na kathikaṁ paribhoti, na attānaṁ paribhoti, paññavā hoti ajaḷo aneḷamūgo, na anaññāte aññātamānī hoti.
segs.e: They don’t disparage the talk, the speaker, or themselves. They’re wise, bright, and clever. They don’t think they know what they don’t know.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattan”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these five qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 5.153
16. The True Teaching
The Sure Path (3rd)

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with five qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities even when listening to the true teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Makkhī dhammaṁ suṇāti makkhapariyuṭṭhito, upārambhacitto dhammaṁ suṇāti randhagavesī, dhammadesake āhatacitto hoti khīlajāto, duppañño hoti jaḷo eḷamūgo, anaññāte aññātamānī hoti.
segs.e: They listen to the teaching bent only on putting it down. They listen to the teaching with a hostile, fault-finding mind. They’re antagonistic to the teacher, planning to attack them. They’re witless, dull, and idiotic. And they think they know what they don’t know.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇantopi saddhammaṁ abhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with these five qualities is unable to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities even when listening to the true teaching.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Someone with five qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Amakkhī dhammaṁ suṇāti na makkhapariyuṭṭhito, anupārambhacitto dhammaṁ suṇāti na randhagavesī, dhammadesake anāhatacitto hoti akhīlajāto, paññavā hoti ajaḷo aneḷamūgo, na anaññāte aññātamānī hoti.
segs.e: They don’t listen to the teaching bent only on putting it down. They don’t listen to the teaching with a hostile, fault-finding mind. They’re not antagonistic to the teacher, and not planning to attack them. They’re wise, bright, and clever. And they don’t think they know what they don’t know.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato suṇanto saddhammaṁ bhabbo niyāmaṁ okkamituṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattan”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these five qualities is able to step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities when listening to the true teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 5.154
16. The True Teaching
The Decline of the True Teaching (1st)

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these five things lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na sakkaccaṁ dhammaṁ suṇanti, na sakkaccaṁ dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇanti, na sakkaccaṁ dhammaṁ dhārenti, na sakkaccaṁ dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthaṁ upaparikkhanti, na sakkaccaṁ atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammaṁ paṭipajjanti.
segs.e: It’s when mendicants don’t carefully listen to the teachings, memorize them, and remember them. They don’t carefully examine the meaning of teachings that they remember. And they don’t carefully practice in line with the meaning and the teaching they’ve understood.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sakkaccaṁ dhammaṁ suṇanti, sakkaccaṁ dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇanti, sakkaccaṁ dhammaṁ dhārenti, sakkaccaṁ dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthaṁ upaparikkhanti, sakkaccaṁ atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammaṁ paṭipajjanti.
segs.e: It’s when mendicants carefully listen to the teachings, memorize them, and remember them. They carefully examine the meaning of teachings that they remember. And they carefully practice in line with the meaning and the teaching they’ve understood.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 5.155
16. The True Teaching
The Decline of the True Teaching (2nd)

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these five things lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhū dhammaṁ na pariyāpuṇanti—
segs.e: It’s when the mendicants don’t memorize the teaching—

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the first thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ na vitthārena paresaṁ desenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants don’t explain the teaching in detail to others as they learned and memorized it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the second thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ na vitthārena paraṁ vācenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants don’t make others recite the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the third thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ na vitthārena sajjhāyaṁ karonti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants don’t rehearse the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fourth thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ na cetasā anuvitakkenti anuvicārenti manasānupekkhanti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants don’t think about and consider the teaching in their hearts, examining it with their minds as they learned and memorized it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fifth thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.
What five?
It’s when the mendicants memorize the teaching—

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the first thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ desenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants explain the teaching in detail to others as they learned and memorized it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the second thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paraṁ vācenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants make others recite the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the third thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena sajjhāyaṁ karonti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants rehearse the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fourth thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakkenti anuvicārenti manasānupekkhanti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants think about and consider the teaching in their hearts, examining it with their minds as they learned and memorized it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fifth thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 5.156
16. The True Teaching
The Decline of the True Teaching (3rd)

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these five things lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhū duggahitaṁ suttantaṁ pariyāpuṇanti dunnikkhittehi padabyañjanehi.
segs.e: It’s when the mendicants memorize discourses that they learned incorrectly, with misplaced words and phrases.

segs.p: Dunnikkhittassa, bhikkhave, padabyañjanassa atthopi dunnayo hoti.
segs.e: When the words and phrases are misplaced, the meaning is misinterpreted.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the first thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū dubbacā honti, dovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā, akkhamā appadakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsaniṁ.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants are hard to admonish, having qualities that make them hard to admonish. They’re impatient, and don’t take instruction respectfully.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the second thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā, te na sakkaccaṁ suttantaṁ paraṁ vācenti;
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants who are very learned—inheritors of the heritage, who have memorized the teachings, the monastic law, and the outlines—don’t carefully make others recite the discourses.

segs.p: tesaṁ accayena chinnamūlako suttanto hoti appaṭisaraṇo.
segs.e: When they pass away, the discourses are cut off at the root, with no one to preserve them.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the third thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, therā bhikkhū bāhulikā honti sāthalikā okkamane pubbaṅgamā paviveke nikkhittadhurā, na vīriyaṁ ārabhanti appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: Furthermore, the senior mendicants are indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion, not rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
Those who come after them follow their example.

segs.p: Sāpi hoti bāhulikā sāthalikā okkamane pubbaṅgamā paviveke nikkhittadhurā, na vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: They too are indulgent and slack …

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fourth thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, saṅgho bhinno hoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, there’s a schism in the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Saṅghe kho pana, bhikkhave, bhinne aññamaññaṁ akkosā ca honti, aññamaññaṁ paribhāsā ca honti, aññamaññaṁ parikkhepā ca honti, aññamaññaṁ pariccajanā ca honti.
segs.e: When the Saṅgha is split, they abuse, insult, block, and forsake each other.

segs.p: Tattha appasannā ceva nappasīdanti, pasannānañca ekaccānaṁ aññathattaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This doesn’t inspire confidence in those without it, and it causes some with confidence to change their minds.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fifth thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhū suggahitaṁ suttantaṁ pariyāpuṇanti sunikkhittehi padabyañjanehi.
segs.e: It’s when the mendicants memorize discourses that have been learned correctly, with well placed words and phrases.

segs.p: Sunikkhittassa, bhikkhave, padabyañjanassa atthopi sunayo hoti.
segs.e: When the words and phrases are well organized, the meaning is correctly interpreted.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the first thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū suvacā honti sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā, khamā padakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsaniṁ.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants are easy to admonish, having qualities that make them easy to admonish. They’re patient, and take instruction respectfully.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the second thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā, te sakkaccaṁ suttantaṁ paraṁ vācenti;
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants who are very learned—inheritors of the heritage, who have memorized the teachings, the monastic law, and the outlines—carefully make others recite the discourses.

segs.p: tesaṁ accayena na chinnamūlako suttanto hoti sappaṭisaraṇo.
segs.e: When they pass away, the discourses aren’t cut off at the root, and they have someone to preserve them.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the third thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, therā bhikkhū na bāhulikā honti na sāthalikā, okkamane nikkhittadhurā paviveke pubbaṅgamā; vīriyaṁ ārabhanti appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: Furthermore, the senior mendicants are not indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion. They rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
Those who come after them follow their example.

segs.p: Sāpi hoti na bāhulikā na sāthalikā, okkamane nikkhittadhurā paviveke pubbaṅgamā, vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: They too are not indulgent or slack …

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fourth thing …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, saṅgho samaggo sammodamāno avivadamāno ekuddeso phāsuṁ viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, the Saṅgha lives comfortably, in harmony, appreciating each other, without dispute, with one recitation.

segs.p: Saṅghe kho pana, bhikkhave, samagge na ceva aññamaññaṁ akkosā honti, na ca aññamaññaṁ paribhāsā honti, na ca aññamaññaṁ parikkhepā honti, na ca aññamaññaṁ pariccajanā honti.
segs.e: When the Saṅgha is in harmony, they don’t abuse, insult, block, or forsake each other.

segs.p: Tattha appasannā ceva pasīdanti, pasannānañca bhiyyobhāvo hoti.
segs.e: This inspires confidence in those without it, and increases confidence in those who have it.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fifth thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These five things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 5.157
16. The True Teaching
Inappropriate Talk

segs.p: “Pañcannaṁ, bhikkhave, puggalānaṁ kathā dukkathā puggale puggalaṁ upanidhāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, it is inappropriate to speak to five individuals by comparing that individual with someone else.
What five?
It’s inappropriate to talk to an unfaithful person about faith.
It’s inappropriate to talk to an unethical person about ethics.
It’s inappropriate to talk to an unlearned person about learning.
It’s inappropriate to talk to a stingy person about generosity.
It’s inappropriate to talk to a witless person about wisdom.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, assaddhassa saddhākathā dukkathā?
segs.e: And why is it inappropriate to talk to an unfaithful person about faith?

segs.p: Assaddho, bhikkhave, saddhākathāya kacchamānāya abhisajjati kuppati byāpajjati patitthīyati kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: When an unfaithful person is spoken to about faith they lose their temper, becoming annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, and displaying annoyance, hate, and bitterness.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tañhi so, bhikkhave, saddhāsampadaṁ attani na samanupassati, na ca labhati tatonidānaṁ pītipāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: Not seeing that faith in themselves, they don’t get the rapture and joy that faith brings.
That’s why it’s inappropriate to talk to an unfaithful person about faith.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, dussīlassa sīlakathā dukkathā?
segs.e: And why is it inappropriate to talk to an unethical person about ethics?

segs.p: Dussīlo, bhikkhave, sīlakathāya kacchamānāya abhisajjati kuppati byāpajjati patitthīyati kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: When an unethical person is spoken to about ethics they lose their temper …
Why is that?

segs.p: Tañhi so, bhikkhave, sīlasampadaṁ attani na samanupassati na ca labhati tatonidānaṁ pītipāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: Not seeing that ethical conduct in themselves, they don’t get the rapture and joy that ethical conduct brings.
That’s why it’s inappropriate to talk to an unethical person about ethics.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, appassutassa bāhusaccakathā dukkathā?
segs.e: And why is it inappropriate to talk to an unlearned person about learning?

segs.p: Appassuto, bhikkhave, bāhusaccakathāya kacchamānāya abhisajjati kuppati byāpajjati patitthīyati kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: When an unlearned person is spoken to about learning they lose their temper …
Why is that?

segs.p: Tañhi so, bhikkhave, sutasampadaṁ attani na samanupassati, na ca labhati tatonidānaṁ pītipāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: Not seeing that learning in themselves, they don’t get the rapture and joy that learning brings.
That’s why it’s inappropriate to talk to an unlearned person about learning.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, maccharissa cāgakathā dukkathā?
segs.e: And why is it inappropriate to talk to a stingy person about generosity?

segs.p: Maccharī, bhikkhave, cāgakathāya kacchamānāya abhisajjati kuppati byāpajjati patitthīyati kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: When a stingy person is spoken to about generosity they lose their temper …
Why is that?

segs.p: Tañhi so, bhikkhave, cāgasampadaṁ attani na samanupassati na ca labhati tatonidānaṁ pītipāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: Not seeing that generosity in themselves, they don’t get the rapture and joy that generosity brings.
That’s why it’s inappropriate to talk to a stingy person about generosity.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, duppaññassa paññākathā dukkathā?
segs.e: And why is it inappropriate to talk to a witless person about wisdom?

segs.p: Duppañño, bhikkhave, paññākathāya kacchamānāya abhisajjati kuppati byāpajjati patitthīyati kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: When a witless person is spoken to about wisdom they lose their temper, becoming annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, and displaying annoyance, hate, and bitterness.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tañhi so, bhikkhave, paññāsampadaṁ attani na samanupassati, na ca labhati tatonidānaṁ pītipāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: Not seeing that wisdom in themselves, they don’t get the rapture and joy that wisdom brings.
That’s why it’s inappropriate to talk to a witless person about wisdom.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ puggalānaṁ kathā dukkathā puggale puggalaṁ upanidhāya.
segs.e: It is inappropriate to speak to these five individuals by comparing that individual with someone else.

segs.p: Pañcannaṁ, bhikkhave, puggalānaṁ kathā sukathā puggale puggalaṁ upanidhāya.
segs.e: It is appropriate to speak to five individuals by comparing that individual with someone else.
What five?
It’s appropriate to talk to a faithful person about faith.
It’s appropriate to talk to an ethical person about ethical conduct.
It’s appropriate to talk to a learned person about learning.
It’s appropriate to talk to a generous person about generosity.
It’s appropriate to talk to a wise person about wisdom.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, saddhassa saddhākathā sukathā?
segs.e: And why is it appropriate to talk to a faithful person about faith?

segs.p: Saddho, bhikkhave, saddhākathāya kacchamānāya nābhisajjati na kuppati na byāpajjati na patitthīyati na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: When a faithful person is spoken to about faith they don’t lose their temper, they don’t get annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, or display annoyance, hate, and bitterness.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tañhi so, bhikkhave, saddhāsampadaṁ attani samanupassati labhati ca tatonidānaṁ pītipāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: Seeing that faith in themselves, they get the rapture and joy that faith brings.
That’s why it’s appropriate to talk to a faithful person about faith.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, sīlavato sīlakathā sukathā?
segs.e: And why is it appropriate to talk to an ethical person about ethical conduct?

segs.p: Sīlavā, bhikkhave, sīlakathāya kacchamānāya nābhisajjati na kuppati na byāpajjati na patitthīyati na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: When an ethical person is spoken to about ethical conduct they don’t lose their temper …
Why is that?

segs.p: Tañhi so, bhikkhave, sīlasampadaṁ attani samanupassati, labhati ca tatonidānaṁ pītipāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: Seeing that ethical conduct in themselves, they get the rapture and joy that ethical conduct brings.
That’s why it’s appropriate to talk to an ethical person about ethical conduct.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, bahussutassa bāhusaccakathā sukathā?
segs.e: And why is it appropriate to talk to a learned person about learning?

segs.p: Bahussuto, bhikkhave, bāhusaccakathāya kacchamānāya nābhisajjati na kuppati na byāpajjati na patitthīyati na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: When a learned person is spoken to about learning they don’t lose their temper …
Why is that?

segs.p: Tañhi so, bhikkhave, sutasampadaṁ attani samanupassati, labhati ca tatonidānaṁ pītipāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: Seeing that learning in themselves, they get the rapture and joy that learning brings.
That’s why it’s appropriate to talk to a learned person about learning.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, cāgavato cāgakathā sukathā?
segs.e: And why is it appropriate to talk to a generous person about generosity?

segs.p: Cāgavā, bhikkhave, cāgakathāya kacchamānāya nābhisajjati na kuppati na byāpajjati na patitthīyati na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: When a generous person is spoken to about generosity they don’t lose their temper …
Why is that?

segs.p: Tañhi so, bhikkhave, cāgasampadaṁ attani samanupassati, labhati ca tatonidānaṁ pītipāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: Seeing that generosity in themselves, they get the rapture and joy that generosity brings.
That’s why it’s appropriate to talk to a generous person about generosity.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, bhikkhave, paññavato paññākathā sukathā?
segs.e: And why is it appropriate to talk to a wise person about wisdom?

segs.p: Paññavā, bhikkhave, paññākathāya kacchamānāya nābhisajjati na kuppati na byāpajjati na patitthīyati na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: When a wise person is spoken to about wisdom they don’t lose their temper, they don’t get annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, or display annoyance, hate, and bitterness.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tañhi so, bhikkhave, paññāsampadaṁ attani samanupassati labhati ca tatonidānaṁ pītipāmojjaṁ.
segs.e: Seeing that wisdom in themselves, they get the rapture and joy that wisdom brings.
That’s why it’s appropriate to talk to a wise person about wisdom.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ puggalānaṁ kathā sukathā puggale puggalaṁ upanidhāyā”ti.
segs.e: It is appropriate to speak to these five individuals by comparing that individual with someone else.”
Numbered Discourses 5.158
16. The True Teaching
Timidity

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu sārajjaṁ okkanto hoti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with five qualities is overcome by timidity.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu assaddho hoti, dussīlo hoti, appassuto hoti, kusīto hoti, duppañño hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is faithless, unethical, with little learning, lazy, and witless.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu sārajjaṁ okkanto hoti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities is overcome by timidity.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu visārado hoti.
segs.e: A mendicant with five qualities is self-assured.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho hoti, sīlavā hoti, bahussuto hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, paññavā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is faithful, ethical, learned, energetic, and wise.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu visārado hotī”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities is self-assured.”
Numbered Discourses 5.159
16. The True Teaching
With Udāyī
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā udāyī mahatiyā gihiparisāya parivuto dhammaṁ desento nisinno hoti.
segs.e: Now, at that time Venerable Udāyī was sitting teaching Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly of laypeople.

segs.p: Addasā kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ mahatiyā gihiparisāya parivutaṁ dhammaṁ desentaṁ nisinnaṁ.
segs.e: Seeing this, Venerable Ānanda

segs.p: Disvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “āyasmā, bhante, udāyī mahatiyā gihiparisāya parivuto dhammaṁ desetī”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, Venerable Udāyī is teaching Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly of laypeople.”

segs.p: “Na kho, ānanda, sukaraṁ paresaṁ dhammaṁ desetuṁ.
segs.e: “Ānanda, it’s not easy to teach Dhamma to others.

segs.p: Paresaṁ, ānanda, dhammaṁ desentena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṁ upaṭṭhāpetvā paresaṁ dhammo desetabbo.
segs.e: You should establish five things in yourself before teaching Dhamma to others.
What five?
You should teach Dhamma to others thinking: ‘I will teach step by step.’ …
‘I will teach showing my method.’ …

segs.p: ‘anuddayataṁ paṭicca kathaṁ kathessāmī’ti paresaṁ dhammo desetabbo;
segs.e: ‘I will teach out of kindness.’ …

segs.p: ‘na āmisantaro kathaṁ kathessāmī’ti paresaṁ dhammo desetabbo;
segs.e: ‘I will not teach while secretly hoping to profit.’ …

segs.p: ‘attānañca parañca anupahacca kathaṁ kathessāmī’ti paresaṁ dhammo desetabbo.
segs.e: ‘I will teach without damaging myself or others.’

segs.p: Na kho, ānanda, sukaraṁ paresaṁ dhammaṁ desetuṁ.
segs.e: It’s not easy to teach Dhamma to others.

segs.p: Paresaṁ, ānanda, dhammaṁ desentena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṁ upaṭṭhāpetvā paresaṁ dhammo desetabbo”ti.
segs.e: You should establish these five things in yourself before teaching Dhamma to others.”
Numbered Discourses 5.160
16. The True Teaching
Hard to Dispel
“Mendicants, these five things are hard to dispel once they’ve arisen.
What five?

segs.p: Uppanno rāgo duppaṭivinodayo, uppanno doso duppaṭivinodayo, uppanno moho duppaṭivinodayo, uppannaṁ paṭibhānaṁ duppaṭivinodayaṁ, uppannaṁ gamikacittaṁ duppaṭivinodayaṁ.
segs.e: Greed, hate, delusion, the feeling of being inspired to speak out, and thoughts of traveling.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca uppannā duppaṭivinodayā”ti.
segs.e: These five things are hard to dispel once they’ve arisen.”
Numbered Discourses 5.161
17. Resentment
Getting Rid of Resentment (1st)

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, āghātapaṭivinayā yattha bhikkhuno uppanno āghāto sabbaso paṭivinetabbo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant should use these five ways to completely get rid of resentment when it has arisen toward anyone.
What five?

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, puggale āghāto jāyetha, mettā tasmiṁ puggale bhāvetabbā;
segs.e: You should develop love for an individual you resent.
That’s how to get rid of resentment for that individual.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, puggale āghāto jāyetha, karuṇā tasmiṁ puggale bhāvetabbā;
segs.e: You should develop compassion for an individual you resent. …

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, puggale āghāto jāyetha, upekkhā tasmiṁ puggale bhāvetabbā;
segs.e: You should develop equanimity for an individual you resent. …

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, puggale āghāto jāyetha, asatiamanasikāro tasmiṁ puggale āpajjitabbo;
segs.e: You should disregard an individual you resent, paying no attention to them. …

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, puggale āghāto jāyetha, kammassakatā tasmiṁ puggale adhiṭṭhātabbā:
segs.e: You should focus on the ownership of deeds regarding that individual:
‘This venerable is the owner of their deeds and heir to their deeds. Deeds are their womb, their relative, and their refuge.

segs.p: yaṁ kammaṁ karissati kalyāṇaṁ vā pāpakaṁ vā tassa dāyādo bhavissatī’ti;
segs.e: They shall be the heir of whatever deeds they do, whether good or bad.’
That’s how to get rid of resentment for that individual.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca āghātapaṭivinayā, yattha bhikkhuno uppanno āghāto sabbaso paṭivinetabbo”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant should use these five ways to completely get rid of resentment when it has arisen toward anyone.”
Numbered Discourses 5.162
17. Resentment
Getting Rid of Resentment (2nd)

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Venerable Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.
Sāriputta said this:

segs.p: “Pañcime, āvuso, āghātapaṭivinayā yattha bhikkhuno uppanno āghāto sabbaso paṭivinetabbo.
segs.e: “Reverends, a mendicant should use these five ways to completely get rid of resentment when it has arisen toward anyone.
What five?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, ekacco puggalo aparisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti parisuddhavacīsamācāro;
segs.e: In the case of an individual whose behavior by way of body is impure, but whose behavior by way of speech is pure,
you should get rid of resentment for that kind of individual.

segs.p: Idha panāvuso, ekacco puggalo aparisuddhavacīsamācāro hoti parisuddhakāyasamācāro;
segs.e: In the case of an individual whose behavior by way of speech is impure, but whose behavior by way of body is pure, …

segs.p: Idha panāvuso, ekacco puggalo aparisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti aparisuddhavacīsamācāro, labhati ca kālena kālaṁ cetaso vivaraṁ cetaso pasādaṁ;
segs.e: In the case of an individual whose behavior by way of body and speech is impure, but who gets an openness and clarity of heart from time to time, …

segs.p: Idha panāvuso, ekacco puggalo aparisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti aparisuddhavacīsamācāro, na ca labhati kālena kālaṁ cetaso vivaraṁ cetaso pasādaṁ;
segs.e: In the case of an individual whose behavior by way of body and speech is impure, and who doesn’t get an openness and clarity of heart from time to time, …

segs.p: Idha panāvuso, ekacco puggalo parisuddhakāyasamācāro parisuddhavacīsamācāro, labhati ca kālena vā kālaṁ cetaso vivaraṁ cetaso pasādaṁ;
segs.e: In the case of an individual whose behavior by way of body and speech is pure, and who gets an openness and clarity of heart from time to time,
you should get rid of resentment for that kind of individual.

segs.p: Tatrāvuso, yvāyaṁ puggalo aparisuddhakāyasamācāro parisuddhavacīsamācāro, kathaṁ tasmiṁ puggale āghāto paṭivinetabbo?
segs.e: How should you get rid of resentment for an individual whose behavior by way of body is impure, but whose behavior by way of speech is pure?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, bhikkhu paṁsukūliko rathiyāya nantakaṁ disvā vāmena pādena niggaṇhitvā dakkhiṇena pādena pattharitvā, yo tattha sāro taṁ paripātetvā ādāya pakkameyya;
segs.e: Suppose a mendicant wearing rag robes sees a rag by the side of the road. They’d hold it down with the left foot, spread it out with the right foot, tear out what was intact, and take it away with them.

segs.p: evamevaṁ khvāvuso, yvāyaṁ puggalo aparisuddhakāyasamācāro parisuddhavacīsamācāro, yāssa aparisuddhakāyasamācāratā na sāssa tasmiṁ samaye manasi kātabbā, yā ca khvassa parisuddhavacīsamācāratā sāssa tasmiṁ samaye manasi kātabbā.
segs.e: In the same way, at that time you should ignore that individual’s impure behavior by way of body and focus on their pure behavior by way of speech.
That’s how to get rid of resentment for that individual.

segs.p: Tatrāvuso, yvāyaṁ puggalo aparisuddhavacīsamācāro parisuddhakāyasamācāro, kathaṁ tasmiṁ puggale āghāto paṭivinetabbo?
segs.e: How should you get rid of resentment for an individual whose behavior by way of speech is impure, but whose behavior by way of body is pure?
Suppose there was a lotus pond enveloped with moss and aquatic plants.

segs.p: Atha puriso āgaccheyya ghammābhitatto ghammapareto kilanto tasito pipāsito.
segs.e: Then along comes a person struggling in the oppressive heat, weary, thirsty, and parched.

segs.p: So taṁ pokkharaṇiṁ ogāhetvā ubhohi hatthehi iticiti ca sevālapaṇakaṁ apaviyūhitvā añjalinā pivitvā pakkameyya.
segs.e: They’d plunge into the lotus pond, sweep apart the moss and aquatic plants, drink from their cupped hands, and be on their way.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, yvāyaṁ puggalo aparisuddhavacīsamācāro parisuddhakāyasamācāro, yāssa aparisuddhavacīsamācāratā na sāssa tasmiṁ samaye manasi kātabbā, yā ca khvassa parisuddhakāyasamācāratā sāssa tasmiṁ samaye manasi kātabbā.
segs.e: In the same way, at that time you should ignore that individual’s impure behavior by way of speech and focus on their pure behavior by way of body.
That’s how to get rid of resentment for that individual.

segs.p: Tatrāvuso, yvāyaṁ puggalo aparisuddhakāyasamācāro aparisuddhavacīsamācāro labhati ca kālena kālaṁ cetaso vivaraṁ cetaso pasādaṁ, kathaṁ tasmiṁ puggale āghāto paṭivinetabbo?
segs.e: How should you get rid of resentment for an individual whose behavior by way of body and speech is impure, but who gets an openness and clarity of heart from time to time?
Suppose there was a little water in a cow’s hoofprint.

segs.p: Atha puriso āgaccheyya ghammābhitatto ghammapareto kilanto tasito pipāsito.
segs.e: Then along comes a person struggling in the oppressive heat, weary, thirsty, and parched.
They might think:
‘This little bit of water is in a cow’s hoofprint.

segs.p: Sacāhaṁ añjalinā vā pivissāmi bhājanena vā khobhessāmipi taṁ loḷessāmipi taṁ apeyyampi taṁ karissāmi.
segs.e: If I drink it with my cupped hands or a bowl, I’ll stir it and disturb it, making it undrinkable.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ catukkuṇḍiko nipatitvā gopītakaṁ pivitvā pakkameyyan’ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I get down on all fours and drink it up like a cow, then be on my way?’

segs.p: So catukkuṇḍiko nipatitvā gopītakaṁ pivitvā pakkameyya.
segs.e: So that’s what they do.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, yvāyaṁ puggalo aparisuddhakāyasamācāro aparisuddhavacīsamācāro labhati ca kālena kālaṁ cetaso vivaraṁ cetaso pasādaṁ, yāssa aparisuddhakāyasamācāratā na sāssa tasmiṁ samaye manasi kātabbā;
segs.e: In the same way, at that time you should ignore that individual’s impure behavior by way of speech and body,

segs.p: yāpissa aparisuddhavacīsamācāratā na sāpissa tasmiṁ samaye manasi kātabbā.
Yañca kho so labhati kālena kālaṁ cetaso vivaraṁ cetaso pasādaṁ, tamevassa tasmiṁ samaye manasi kātabbaṁ.
segs.e: and focus on the fact that they get an openness and clarity of heart from time to time.
That’s how to get rid of resentment for that individual.

segs.p: Tatrāvuso, yvāyaṁ puggalo aparisuddhakāyasamācāro aparisuddhavacīsamācāro na ca labhati kālena kālaṁ cetaso vivaraṁ cetaso pasādaṁ, kathaṁ tasmiṁ puggale āghāto paṭivinetabbo?
segs.e: How should you get rid of resentment for an individual whose behavior by way of body and speech is impure, and who doesn’t get an openness and clarity of heart from time to time?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, puriso ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno addhānamaggappaṭipanno.
segs.e: Suppose a person was traveling along a road, and they were sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Tassa puratopissa dūre gāmo pacchatopissa dūre gāmo.
segs.e: And it was a long way to a village, whether ahead or behind.

segs.p: So na labheyya sappāyāni bhojanāni, na labheyya sappāyāni bhesajjāni, na labheyya patirūpaṁ upaṭṭhākaṁ, na labheyya gāmantanāyakaṁ.
segs.e: And they didn’t have any suitable food or medicine, or a competent carer, or someone to bring them within a village.
Another person traveling along the road might see them,

segs.p: So tasmiṁ purise kāruññaṁyeva upaṭṭhāpeyya, anuddayaṁyeva upaṭṭhāpeyya, anukampaṁyeva upaṭṭhāpeyya:
segs.e: and think of them with nothing but compassion, kindness, and sympathy:

segs.p: ‘aho vatāyaṁ puriso labheyya sappāyāni bhojanāni, labheyya sappāyāni bhesajjāni, labheyya patirūpaṁ upaṭṭhākaṁ, labheyya gāmantanāyakaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Oh, may this person get suitable food or medicine, or a competent carer, or someone to bring them within a village.
Why is that?
So that they don’t come to ruin right here.’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, yvāyaṁ puggalo aparisuddhakāyasamācāro aparisuddhavacīsamācāro na ca labhati kālena kālaṁ cetaso vivaraṁ cetaso pasādaṁ, evarūpepi, āvuso, puggale kāruññaṁyeva upaṭṭhāpetabbaṁ anuddayāyeva upaṭṭhāpetabbā anukampāyeva upaṭṭhāpetabbā:
segs.e: In the same way, at that time you should ignore that individual’s impure behavior by way of speech and body, and the fact that they don’t get an openness and clarity of heart from time to time, and think of them with nothing but compassion, kindness, and sympathy:

segs.p: ‘aho vata ayamāyasmā kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāveyya, vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāveyya, manoduccaritaṁ pahāya manosucaritaṁ bhāveyya.
segs.e: ‘Oh, may this venerable give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.
Why is that?

segs.p: Māyaṁ āyasmā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjī’ti.
segs.e: So that, when their body breaks up, after death, they’re not reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.’
That’s how to get rid of resentment for that individual.

segs.p: Tatrāvuso, yvāyaṁ puggalo parisuddhakāyasamācāro parisuddhavacīsamācāro labhati ca kālena kālaṁ cetaso vivaraṁ cetaso pasādaṁ, kathaṁ tasmiṁ puggale āghāto paṭivinetabbo?
segs.e: How should you get rid of resentment for an individual whose behavior by way of body and speech is pure, and who gets an openness and clarity of heart from time to time?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, pokkharaṇī acchodakā sātodakā sītodakā setakā supatitthā ramaṇīyā nānārukkhehi sañchannā.
segs.e: Suppose there was a lotus pond with clear, sweet, cool water, clean, with smooth banks, delightful, and shaded by many trees.

segs.p: Atha puriso āgaccheyya ghammābhitatto ghammapareto kilanto tasito pipāsito.
segs.e: Then along comes a person struggling in the oppressive heat, weary, thirsty, and parched.

segs.p: So taṁ pokkharaṇiṁ ogāhetvā nhātvā ca pivitvā ca paccuttaritvā tattheva rukkhacchāyāya nisīdeyya vā nipajjeyya vā.
segs.e: They’d plunge into the lotus pond to bathe and drink. And after emerging they’d sit or lie down right there in the shade of the trees.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, yvāyaṁ puggalo parisuddhakāyasamācāro parisuddhavacīsamācāro labhati ca kālena kālaṁ cetaso vivaraṁ cetaso pasādaṁ, yāpissa parisuddhakāyasamācāratā sāpissa tasmiṁ samaye manasi kātabbā;
segs.e: In the same way, at that time you should focus on that individual’s pure behavior by way of body and speech, and on the fact that they get an openness and clarity of heart from time to time.

segs.p: yāpissa parisuddhavacīsamācāratā sāpissa tasmiṁ samaye manasi kātabbā;
yampi labhati kālena kālaṁ cetaso vivaraṁ cetaso pasādaṁ, tampissa tasmiṁ samaye manasi kātabbaṁ.

segs.e: That’s how to get rid of resentment for that individual.

segs.p: Samantapāsādikaṁ, āvuso, puggalaṁ āgamma cittaṁ pasīdati.
segs.e: Relying on an individual who is impressive all around, the mind becomes confident.

segs.p: Ime kho, āvuso, pañca āghātapaṭivinayā, yattha bhikkhuno uppanno āghāto sabbaso paṭivinetabbo”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant should use these five ways to completely get rid of resentment when it has arisen toward anyone.”
Numbered Discourses 5.163
17. Resentment
Discussions

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Venerable Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.
Sāriputta said this:

segs.p: “Pañcahāvuso, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ sākaccho sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: “A mendicant with five qualities is fit to hold a discussion with their spiritual companions.
What five?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu attanā ca sīlasampanno hoti, sīlasampadākathāya ca āgataṁ pañhaṁ byākattā hoti;
segs.e: A mendicant is personally accomplished in ethics, and answers questions that come up when discussing accomplishment in ethics.

segs.p: attanā ca samādhisampanno hoti, samādhisampadākathāya ca āgataṁ pañhaṁ byākattā hoti;
segs.e: They’re personally accomplished in immersion, …

segs.p: attanā ca paññāsampanno hoti, paññāsampadākathāya ca āgataṁ pañhaṁ byākattā hoti;
segs.e: They’re personally accomplished in wisdom, …

segs.p: attanā ca vimuttisampanno hoti, vimuttisampadākathāya ca āgataṁ pañhaṁ byākattā hoti;
segs.e: They’re personally accomplished in freedom, …

segs.p: attanā ca vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno hoti, vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadākathāya ca āgataṁ pañhaṁ byākattā hoti.
segs.e: They’re personally accomplished in the knowledge and vision of freedom, and they answer questions that come up when discussing accomplishment in the knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, āvuso, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ sākaccho sabrahmacārīnan”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities is fit to hold a discussion with their spiritual companions.”
Numbered Discourses 5.164
17. Resentment
Sharing a Way of Life

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi …pe…
segs.e: There Venerable Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: pañcahi, āvuso, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁsājīvo sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: “A mendicant with five qualities is fit to share their life with their spiritual companions.
What five?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu attanā ca sīlasampanno hoti, sīlasampadākathāya ca āgataṁ pañhaṁ byākattā hoti;
segs.e: A mendicant is personally accomplished in ethics, and answers questions that come up when discussing accomplishment in ethics.

segs.p: attanā ca samādhisampanno hoti, samādhisampadākathāya ca āgataṁ pañhaṁ byākattā hoti;
segs.e: They’re personally accomplished in immersion, …

segs.p: attanā ca paññāsampanno hoti, paññāsampadākathāya ca āgataṁ pañhaṁ byākattā hoti;
segs.e: They’re personally accomplished in wisdom, …

segs.p: attanā ca vimuttisampanno hoti, vimuttisampadākathāya ca āgataṁ pañhaṁ byākattā hoti;
segs.e: They’re personally accomplished in freedom, …

segs.p: attanā ca vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno hoti, vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadākathāya ca āgataṁ pañhaṁ byākattā hoti.
segs.e: They’re personally accomplished in the knowledge and vision of freedom, and they answer questions that come up when discussing accomplishment in the knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, āvuso, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁsājīvo sabrahmacārīnan”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities is fit to share their life with their spiritual companions.”
Numbered Discourses 5.165
17. Resentment
Asking Questions

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi …pe… “yo hi koci, āvuso, paraṁ pañhaṁ pucchati, sabbo so pañcahi ṭhānehi, etesaṁ vā aññatarena.
segs.e: There Venerable Sāriputta addressed the mendicants: … “Whoever asks a question of another, does so for one or other of these five reasons.
What five?

segs.p: Mandattā momūhattā paraṁ pañhaṁ pucchati, pāpiccho icchāpakato paraṁ pañhaṁ pucchati, paribhavaṁ paraṁ pañhaṁ pucchati, aññātukāmo paraṁ pañhaṁ pucchati, atha vā panevaṁcitto paraṁ pañhaṁ pucchati:
segs.e: Someone asks a question of another from stupidity and folly. Or they ask from corrupt wishes, being of wishful temperament. Or they ask in order to disparage. Or they ask wanting to understand. Or they ask with the thought,

segs.p: ‘sace me pañhaṁ puṭṭho sammadeva byākarissati iccetaṁ kusalaṁ, no ce me pañhaṁ puṭṭho sammadeva byākarissati ahamassa sammadeva byākarissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘If they correctly answer the question I ask it’s good. If not, I’ll correctly answer it for them.’

segs.p: Yo hi koci, āvuso, paraṁ pañhaṁ pucchati, sabbo so imehi pañcahi ṭhānehi, etesaṁ vā aññatarena.
segs.e: Whoever asks a question of another, does so for one or other of these five reasons.

segs.p: Ahaṁ kho panāvuso, evaṁcitto paraṁ pañhaṁ pucchāmi:
segs.e: As for myself, I ask with the thought,

segs.p: ‘sace me pañhaṁ puṭṭho sammadeva byākarissati iccetaṁ kusalaṁ, no ce me pañhaṁ puṭṭho sammadeva byākarissati, ahamassa sammadeva byākarissāmī’”ti.
segs.e: ‘If they correctly answer the question I ask it’s good. If not, I’ll correctly answer it for them.’”
Numbered Discourses 5.166
17. Resentment
Cessation

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi …pe…
segs.e: There Venerable Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlasampanno samādhisampanno paññāsampanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
segs.e: “Reverends, take a mendicant who is accomplished in ethics, immersion, and wisdom. They might enter into and emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling.
That is possible.

segs.p: No ce diṭṭheva dhamme aññaṁ ārādheyya, atikkammeva kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
segs.e: If they don’t reach enlightenment in this very life, then, surpassing the company of gods that consume edible food, they’re reborn in a certain host of mind-made gods. There they might enter into and emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling.
That is possible.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā udāyī āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Udāyī said to him,

segs.p: “aṭṭhānaṁ kho etaṁ, āvuso sāriputta, anavakāso yaṁ so bhikkhu atikkammeva kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
segs.e: “This is not possible, Reverend Sāriputta, it cannot happen!”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho …pe… tatiyampi kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: But for a second … and a third time Sāriputta repeated his statement.

segs.p: “idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlasampanno samādhisampanno paññāsampanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
No ce diṭṭheva dhamme aññaṁ ārādheyya, atikkammeva kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
Tatiyampi kho āyasmā udāyī āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And for a third time, Udāyī said to him,

segs.p: “aṭṭhānaṁ kho etaṁ, āvuso sāriputta, anavakāso yaṁ so bhikkhu atikkammeva kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
segs.e: “This is not possible, Reverend Sāriputta, it cannot happen!”
Then Venerable Sāriputta thought,

segs.p: “yāvatatiyakampi kho me āyasmā udāyī paṭikkosati, na ca me koci bhikkhu anumodati.
segs.e: “Venerable Udāyī disagrees with me three times, and not one mendicant agrees with me.
Why don’t I go to see the Buddha?”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: and said to the mendicants:

segs.p: “idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlasampanno samādhisampanno paññāsampanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
segs.e: “Reverends, take a mendicant who is accomplished in ethics, immersion, and wisdom. They might enter into and emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling.
That is possible.

segs.p: No ce diṭṭheva dhamme aññaṁ ārādheyya, atikkammeva kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
segs.e: If they don’t reach enlightenment in this very life, they’re reborn in the company of a certain host of mind-made gods, who surpass the gods that consume edible food. There they might enter into and emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling.
That is possible.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā udāyī āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Udāyī said to him,

segs.p: “aṭṭhānaṁ kho etaṁ, āvuso sāriputta, anavakāso yaṁ so bhikkhu atikkammeva kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
segs.e: “This is not possible, Reverend Sāriputta, it cannot happen!”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho …pe… tatiyampi kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: But for a second … and a third time Sāriputta repeated his statement.

segs.p: “idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlasampanno samādhisampanno paññāsampanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
No ce diṭṭheva dhamme aññaṁ ārādheyya, atikkammeva kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
Tatiyampi kho āyasmā udāyī āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: And for a third time, Udāyī said to him,

segs.p: “aṭṭhānaṁ kho etaṁ, āvuso sāriputta, anavakāso yaṁ so bhikkhu atikkammeva kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
segs.e: “This is not possible, Reverend Sāriputta, it cannot happen!”
Then Venerable Sāriputta thought,

segs.p: “bhagavatopi kho me sammukhā āyasmā udāyī yāvatatiyakaṁ paṭikkosati, na ca me koci bhikkhu anumodati.
segs.e: “Even in front of the Buddha Venerable Udāyī disagrees with me three times, and not one mendicant agrees with me.
I’d better stay silent.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto tuṇhī ahosi.
segs.e: Then Sāriputta fell silent.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ udāyiṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Udāyī,

segs.p: “kaṁ pana tvaṁ, udāyi, manomayaṁ kāyaṁ paccesī”ti?
segs.e: “But Udāyī, do you believe in a mind-made body?”
“For those gods, sir, who are formless, made of perception.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho tuyhaṁ, udāyi, bālassa abyattassa bhaṇitena.
segs.e: “Udāyī, what has an incompetent fool like you got to say?
How on earth could you imagine you’ve got something worth saying!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Ānanda,

segs.p: “atthi nāma, ānanda, theraṁ bhikkhuṁ vihesiyamānaṁ ajjhupekkhissatha.
segs.e: “Ānanda! How can you just watch while a senior mendicant is being harassed?

segs.p: Na hi nāma, ānanda, kāruññampi bhavissati theramhi bhikkhumhi vihesiyamānamhī”ti.
segs.e: Don’t you have any compassion for a senior mendicant who is being harassed?”
Then the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlasampanno samādhisampanno paññāsampanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
segs.e: “Mendicants, take a mendicant who is accomplished in ethics, immersion, and wisdom. They might enter into and emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling.
That is possible.

segs.p: No ce diṭṭheva dhamme aññaṁ ārādheyya, atikkammeva kabaḷīkārāhārabhakkhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ aññataraṁ manomayaṁ kāyaṁ upapanno saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajjeyyāpi vuṭṭhaheyyāpi—
segs.e: If they don’t reach enlightenment in this very life, they’re reborn in the company of a certain host of mind-made gods, who surpass the gods that consume edible food. There they might enter into and emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling.
That is possible.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṁ pāvisi.
segs.e: When he had spoken, the Holy One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando acirapakkantassa bhagavato yenāyasmā upavāṇo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ upavāṇaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, not long after the Buddha had left, Venerable Ānanda went to Venerable Upavāṇa and said to him,
“Reverend Upavāṇa, they’ve been harassing other senior mendicants,
but I didn’t question them.

segs.p: Anacchariyaṁ kho, panetaṁ āvuso upavāṇa, yaṁ bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito etadeva ārabbha udāhareyya yathā āyasmantaṁyevettha upavāṇaṁ paṭibhāseyya.
segs.e: I wouldn’t be surprised if the Buddha brings this up when he comes out of retreat later this afternoon. He might even call upon Venerable Upavāṇa himself.
And right now I feel insecure.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena upaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ upavāṇaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to the assembly hall. He sat down on the seat spread out and said to Upavāṇa,

segs.p: “Katihi nu kho, upavāṇa, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti?
segs.e: “Upavāṇa, how many qualities should a senior mendicant have to be dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired?”

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhante, dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “Sir, a senior mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhante, thero bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s totally full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, reciting them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segs.p: kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā;
segs.e: They’re a good speaker who enunciates well, with a polished, clear, and articulate voice that expresses the meaning.

segs.p: catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī;
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.
They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhante, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
“Good, good, Upavāṇa!

segs.p: Imehi kho, upavāṇa, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato thero bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: A senior mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.

segs.p: Ime ce, upavāṇa, pañca dhammā therassa bhikkhuno na saṁvijjeyyuṁ, taṁ sabrahmacārī na sakkareyyuṁ na garuṁ kareyyuṁ na māneyyuṁ na pūjeyyuṁ khaṇḍiccena pāliccena valittacatāya.
segs.e: If these five qualities are not found in a senior mendicant, why would their spiritual companions honor, respect, revere, or venerate them? Because of their broken teeth, gray hair, and wrinkled skin?

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, upavāṇa, ime pañca dhammā therassa bhikkhuno saṁvijjanti, tasmā taṁ sabrahmacārī sakkaronti garuṁ karonti mānenti pūjentī”ti.
segs.e: But since these five qualities are found in a senior mendicant, their spiritual companions honor, respect, revere, or venerate them.”
Numbered Discourses 5.167
17. Resentment
Accusation

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “codakena, āvuso, bhikkhunā paraṁ codetukāmena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṁ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo.
segs.e: “Reverends, a mendicant who wants to accuse another should first establish five things in themselves.
What five?
I will speak at the right time, not at the wrong time.
I will speak truthfully, not falsely.
I will speak gently, not harshly.
I will speak beneficially, not harmfully.
I will speak lovingly, not from secret hate.

segs.p: Codakena, āvuso, bhikkhunā paraṁ codetukāmena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṁ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo.
segs.e: A mendicant who wants to accuse another should first establish these five things in themselves.

segs.p: Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ passāmi akālena codiyamānaṁ no kālena kupitaṁ, abhūtena codiyamānaṁ no bhūtena kupitaṁ, pharusena codiyamānaṁ no saṇhena kupitaṁ, anatthasaṁhitena codiyamānaṁ no atthasaṁhitena kupitaṁ, dosantarena codiyamānaṁ no mettacittena kupitaṁ.
segs.e: Take a case where I see a certain individual being accused at the wrong time, not being disturbed at the right time. They’re accused falsely, not disturbed truthfully. They’re accused harshly, not disturbed gently. They’re accused harmfully, not disturbed beneficially. They’re accused with secret hate, not disturbed lovingly.

segs.p: Adhammacuditassa, āvuso, bhikkhuno pañcahākārehi avippaṭisāro upadahātabbo:
segs.e: The mendicant who is accused improperly should be reassured in five ways.

segs.p: ‘akālenāyasmā cudito no kālena, alaṁ te avippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: ‘Venerable, you were accused at the wrong time, not at the right time. There’s no need for you to feel remorse.

segs.p: abhūtenāyasmā cudito no bhūtena, alaṁ te avippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You were accused falsely, not truthfully. …

segs.p: pharusenāyasmā cudito no saṇhena, alaṁ te avippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You were accused harshly, not gently. …

segs.p: anatthasaṁhitenāyasmā cudito no atthasaṁhitena, alaṁ te avippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You were accused harmfully, not beneficially. …

segs.p: dosantarenāyasmā cudito no mettacittena, alaṁ te avippaṭisārāyā’ti.
segs.e: You were accused with secret hate, not lovingly. There’s no need for you to feel remorse.’

segs.p: Adhammacuditassa, āvuso, bhikkhuno imehi pañcahākārehi avippaṭisāro upadahātabbo.
segs.e: A mendicant who is accused improperly should be reassured in these five ways.

segs.p: Adhammacodakassa, āvuso, bhikkhuno pañcahākārehi vippaṭisāro upadahātabbo:
segs.e: The mendicant who makes improper accusations should be chastened in five ways.

segs.p: ‘akālena te, āvuso, codito no kālena, alaṁ te vippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: ‘Reverend, you made an accusation at the wrong time, not at the right time. There’s a reason for you to feel remorse.

segs.p: abhūtena te, āvuso, codito no bhūtena, alaṁ te vippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You made an accusation falsely, not truthfully. …

segs.p: pharusena te, āvuso, codito no saṇhena, alaṁ te vippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You made an accusation harshly, not gently. …

segs.p: anatthasaṁhitena te, āvuso, codito no atthasaṁhitena, alaṁ te vippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You made an accusation harmfully, not beneficially. …

segs.p: dosantarena te, āvuso, codito no mettacittena, alaṁ te vippaṭisārāyā’ti.
segs.e: You made an accusation with secret hate, not lovingly. There’s a reason for you to feel remorse.’

segs.p: Adhammacodakassa, āvuso, bhikkhuno imehi pañcahākārehi vippaṭisāro upadahātabbo.
segs.e: The mendicant who makes improper accusations should be chastened in these five ways.
Why is that?

segs.p: Yathā na aññopi bhikkhu abhūtena codetabbaṁ maññeyyāti.
segs.e: So that another mendicant wouldn’t think to make a false accusation.

segs.p: Idha panāhaṁ, āvuso, ekaccaṁ puggalaṁ passāmi kālena codiyamānaṁ no akālena kupitaṁ, bhūtena codiyamānaṁ no abhūtena kupitaṁ, saṇhena codiyamānaṁ no pharusena kupitaṁ, atthasaṁhitena codiyamānaṁ no anatthasaṁhitena kupitaṁ, mettacittena codiyamānaṁ no dosantarena kupitaṁ.
segs.e: Take a case where I see a certain individual being accused at the right time, not being disturbed at the wrong time. They’re accused truthfully, not disturbed falsely. They’re accused gently, not disturbed harshly. They’re accused beneficially, not disturbed harmfully. They’re accused lovingly, not disturbed with secret hate.

segs.p: Dhammacuditassa, āvuso, bhikkhuno pañcahākārehi vippaṭisāro upadahātabbo:
segs.e: The mendicant who is accused properly should be chastened in five ways.

segs.p: ‘kālenāyasmā cudito no akālena, alaṁ te vippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: ‘Venerable, you were accused at the right time, not at the wrong time. There’s a reason for you to feel remorse.

segs.p: bhūtenāyasmā cudito no abhūtena, alaṁ te vippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You were accused truthfully, not falsely. …

segs.p: saṇhenāyasmā cudito no pharusena, alaṁ te vippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You were accused gently, not harshly. …

segs.p: atthasaṁhitenāyasmā cudito no anatthasaṁhitena, alaṁ te vippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You were accused beneficially, not harmfully. …

segs.p: mettacittenāyasmā cudito no dosantarena, alaṁ te vippaṭisārāyā’ti.
segs.e: You were accused lovingly, not with secret hate. There’s a reason for you to feel remorse.’

segs.p: Dhammacuditassa, āvuso, bhikkhuno imehi pañcahākārehi vippaṭisāro upadahātabbo.
segs.e: The mendicant who is accused properly should be chastened in these five ways.

segs.p: Dhammacodakassa, āvuso, bhikkhuno pañcahākārehi avippaṭisāro upadahātabbo:
segs.e: The mendicant who makes proper accusations should be reassured in five ways.

segs.p: ‘kālena te, āvuso, codito no akālena, alaṁ te avippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: ‘Reverend, you made an accusation at the right time, not at the wrong time. There’s no need for you to feel remorse.

segs.p: bhūtena te, āvuso, codito no abhūtena, alaṁ te avippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You made an accusation truthfully, not falsely. …

segs.p: saṇhena te, āvuso, codito no pharusena, alaṁ te avippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You made an accusation gently, not harshly. …

segs.p: atthasaṁhitena te, āvuso, codito no anatthasaṁhitena, alaṁ te avippaṭisārāya;
segs.e: You made an accusation beneficially, not harmfully. …

segs.p: mettacittena te, āvuso, codito no dosantarena, alaṁ te avippaṭisārāyā’ti.
segs.e: You made an accusation lovingly, not with secret hate. There’s no need for you to feel remorse.’

segs.p: Dhammacodakassa, āvuso, bhikkhuno imehi pañcahākārehi avippaṭisāro upadahātabbo.
segs.e: The mendicant who makes proper accusations should be reassured in these five ways.
Why is that?

segs.p: Yathā aññopi bhikkhu bhūtena coditabbaṁ maññeyyāti.
segs.e: So that another mendicant would think to make a true accusation.

segs.p: Cuditena, āvuso, puggalena dvīsu dhammesu patiṭṭhātabbaṁ—
segs.e: An individual who is accused should ground themselves in two things:
truth and an even temper.

segs.p: Mañcepi, āvuso, pare codeyyuṁ kālena vā akālena vā bhūtena vā abhūtena vā saṇhena vā pharusena vā atthasaṁhitena vā anatthasaṁhitena vā mettacittā vā dosantarā vā, ahampi dvīsuyeva dhammesu patiṭṭhaheyyaṁ—
segs.e: Even if others accuse me—at the right time or the wrong time, truthfully or falsely, gently or harshly, beneficially or harmfully, lovingly or with secret hate—I will still ground myself in two things:
truth and an even temper.
If I know that
that quality is found in me, I will tell them that it is.
If I know that
that quality is not found in me, I will tell them that it is not.”

segs.p: “Evampi kho te, sāriputta, vuccamānā atha ca panidhekacce moghapurisā na padakkhiṇaṁ gaṇhantī”ti.
segs.e: “Even when you speak like this, Sāriputta, there are still some futile people here who do not respectfully take it up.”

segs.p: “Ye te, bhante, puggalā assaddhā jīvikatthā na saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitā saṭhā māyāvino ketabino uddhatā unnaḷā capalā mukharā vikiṇṇavācā indriyesu aguttadvārā bhojane amattaññuno jāgariyaṁ ananuyuttā sāmaññe anapekkhavanto sikkhāya na tibbagāravā bāhulikā sāthalikā okkamane pubbaṅgamā paviveke nikkhittadhurā kusītā hīnavīriyā muṭṭhassatino asampajānā asamāhitā vibbhantacittā duppaññā eḷamūgā, te mayā evaṁ vuccamānā na padakkhiṇaṁ gaṇhanti.
segs.e: “Sir, there are those faithless individuals who went forth from the lay life to homelessness not out of faith but to earn a livelihood. They’re devious, deceitful, and sneaky. They’re haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, and loose-tongued. They do not guard their sense doors or eat in moderation, and they are not dedicated to wakefulness. They don’t care about the ascetic life, and don’t keenly respect the training. They’re indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion, lazy, and lacking energy. They’re unmindful, lacking situational awareness and immersion, with straying minds, witless and idiotic. When I speak to them like this, they don’t respectfully take it up.

segs.p: Ye pana te, bhante, kulaputtā saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitā asaṭhā amāyāvino aketabino anuddhatā anunnaḷā acapalā amukharā avikiṇṇavācā indriyesu guttadvārā bhojane mattaññuno jāgariyaṁ anuyuttā sāmaññe apekkhavanto sikkhāya tibbagāravā na bāhulikā na sāthalikā okkamane nikkhittadhurā paviveke pubbaṅgamā āraddhavīriyā pahitattā upaṭṭhitassatino sampajānā samāhitā ekaggacittā paññavanto aneḷamūgā, te mayā evaṁ vuccamānā padakkhiṇaṁ gaṇhantī”ti.
segs.e: Sir, there are those gentlemen who went forth from the lay life to homelessness out of faith. They’re not devious, deceitful, and sneaky. They’re not haughty, insolent, fickle, scurrilous, and loose-tongued. They guard their sense doors and eat in moderation, and they are dedicated to wakefulness. They care about the ascetic life, and keenly respect the training. They’re not indulgent or slack, nor are they leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion. They’re energetic and determined. They’re mindful, with situational awareness, immersion, and unified minds; wise and clever. When I speak to them like this, they do respectfully take it up.”

segs.p: “Ye te, sāriputta, puggalā assaddhā jīvikatthā na saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitā saṭhā māyāvino ketabino uddhatā unnaḷā capalā mukharā vikiṇṇavācā indriyesu aguttadvārā bhojane amattaññuno jāgariyaṁ ananuyuttā sāmaññe anapekkhavanto sikkhāya na tibbagāravā bāhulikā sāthalikā okkamane pubbaṅgamā paviveke nikkhittadhurā kusītā hīnavīriyā muṭṭhassatino asampajānā asamāhitā vibbhantacittā duppaññā eḷamūgā, tiṭṭhantu te.
segs.e: “Sāriputta, those faithless individuals who went forth from the lay life to homelessness not out of faith but to earn a livelihood … Leave them be.

segs.p: Ye pana te, sāriputta, kulaputtā saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitā asaṭhā amāyāvino aketabino anuddhatā anunnaḷā acapalā amukharā avikiṇṇavācā indriyesu guttadvārā bhojane mattaññuno jāgariyaṁ anuyuttā sāmaññe apekkhavanto sikkhāya tibbagāravā na bāhulikā na sāthalikā okkamane nikkhittadhurā paviveke pubbaṅgamā āraddhavīriyā pahitattā upaṭṭhitassatino sampajānā samāhitā ekaggacittā paññavanto aneḷamūgā, te tvaṁ, sāriputta, vadeyyāsi.
segs.e: But those gentlemen who went forth from the lay life to homelessness out of faith … You should speak to them.
Sāriputta, you should advise your spiritual companions!
You should instruct your spiritual companions!
Thinking: ‘I will draw my spiritual companions away from false teachings and ground them in true teachings.’
That’s how you should train.”
Numbered Discourses 5.168
17. Resentment
Ethics

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Venerable Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, an unethical person, who lacks ethics, has destroyed a vital condition for right immersion.

segs.p: sammāsamādhimhi asati sammāsamādhivipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṁ;
segs.e: When there is no right immersion, one who lacks right immersion has destroyed a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

segs.p: yathābhūtañāṇadassane asati yathābhūtañāṇadassanavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti nibbidāvirāgo;
segs.e: When there is no true knowledge and vision, one who lacks true knowledge and vision has destroyed a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

segs.p: nibbidāvirāge asati nibbidāvirāgavipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṁ.
segs.e: When there is no disillusionment and dispassion, one who lacks disillusionment and dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.
Suppose there was a tree that lacked branches and foliage.

segs.p: Tassa papaṭikāpi na pāripūriṁ gacchati, tacopi pheggupi sāropi na pāripūriṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Its shoots, bark, softwood, and heartwood would not grow to fullness.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti sammāsamādhi;
segs.e: In the same way, an unethical person, who lacks ethics, has destroyed a vital condition for right immersion.

segs.p: sammāsamādhimhi asati sammāsamādhivipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṁ;
segs.e: When there is no right immersion, one who lacks right immersion has destroyed a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

segs.p: yathābhūtañāṇadassane asati yathābhūtañāṇadassanavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti nibbidāvirāgo;
segs.e: When there is no true knowledge and vision, one who lacks true knowledge and vision has destroyed a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

segs.p: nibbidāvirāge asati nibbidāvirāgavipannassa hatūpanisaṁ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṁ.
segs.e: When there is no disillusionment and dispassion, one who lacks disillusionment and dispassion has destroyed a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Sīlavato, āvuso, sīlasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti sammāsamādhi;
segs.e: An ethical person, who has fulfilled ethics, has fulfilled a vital condition for right immersion.

segs.p: sammāsamādhimhi sati sammāsamādhisampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṁ;
segs.e: When there is right immersion, one who has fulfilled right immersion has fulfilled a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

segs.p: yathābhūtañāṇadassane sati yathābhūtañāṇadassanasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti nibbidāvirāgo;
segs.e: When there is true knowledge and vision, one who has fulfilled true knowledge and vision has fulfilled a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

segs.p: nibbidāvirāge sati nibbidāvirāgasampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṁ.
segs.e: When there is disillusionment and dispassion, one who has fulfilled disillusionment and dispassion has fulfilled a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, rukkho, sākhāpalāsasampanno. Tassa papaṭikāpi pāripūriṁ gacchati, tacopi pheggupi sāropi pāripūriṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Suppose there was a tree that was complete with branches and foliage. Its shoots, bark, softwood, and heartwood would grow to fullness.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, āvuso, sīlavato sīlasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti sammāsamādhi;
segs.e: In the same way, an ethical person, who has fulfilled ethics, has fulfilled a vital condition for right immersion.

segs.p: sammāsamādhimhi sati sammāsamādhisampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṁ;
segs.e: When there is right immersion, one who has fulfilled right immersion has fulfilled a vital condition for true knowledge and vision.

segs.p: yathābhūtañāṇadassane sati yathābhūtañāṇadassanasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti nibbidāvirāgo;
segs.e: When there is true knowledge and vision, one who has fulfilled true knowledge and vision has fulfilled a vital condition for disillusionment and dispassion.

segs.p: nibbidāvirāge sati nibbidāvirāgasampannassa upanisasampannaṁ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanan”ti.
segs.e: When there is disillusionment and dispassion, one who has fulfilled disillusionment and dispassion has fulfilled a vital condition for knowledge and vision of freedom.”
Numbered Discourses 5.169
17. Resentment
Quick-witted

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to him:

segs.p: “Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu khippanisanti ca hoti, kusalesu dhammesu suggahitaggāhī ca, bahuñca gaṇhāti, gahitañcassa nappamussatī”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, how are we to define a mendicant who is quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings, who learns well, learns much, and does not forget what they’ve learned?”
“Well, Venerable Ānanda, you’re very learned.
Why don’t you clarify this yourself?”

segs.p: “Tenahāvuso sāriputta, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, Reverend Sāriputta, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”
