segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmato ānandassa paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” Sāriputta replied.
Venerable Ānanda said this:

segs.p: “Idhāvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu atthakusalo ca hoti, dhammakusalo ca, byañjanakusalo ca, niruttikusalo ca, pubbāparakusalo ca.
segs.e: “It’s when a mendicant is skilled in the meaning, skilled in the teaching, skilled in definition, skilled in phrasing, and skilled in sequence.

segs.p: Ettāvatā kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu khippanisanti ca hoti kusalesu dhammesu, suggahitaggāhī ca, bahuñca gaṇhāti, gahitañcassa nappamussatī”ti.
segs.e: That is how to define a mendicant who is quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings, who learns well, learns much, and does not forget what they’ve learned.”
“It’s incredible, it’s amazing!
How well this was said by Venerable Ānanda!

segs.p: Imehi ca mayaṁ pañcahi dhammehi samannāgataṁ āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ dhārema:
segs.e: And we will remember Venerable Ānanda as someone who possesses these five qualities:

segs.p: ‘āyasmā ānando atthakusalo dhammakusalo byañjanakusalo niruttikusalo pubbāparakusalo’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Reverend Ānanda is skilled in the meaning, skilled in the teaching, skilled in definition, skilled in phrasing, and skilled in sequence.’”
Numbered Discourses 5.170
17. Resentment
With Bhaddaji

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ānando kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Ānanda was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā bhaddaji yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Bhaddaji went up to Venerable Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ bhaddajiṁ āyasmā ānando etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and Venerable Ānanda said to him:

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, āvuso bhaddaji, dassanānaṁ aggaṁ, kiṁ savanānaṁ aggaṁ, kiṁ sukhānaṁ aggaṁ, kiṁ saññānaṁ aggaṁ, kiṁ bhavānaṁ aggan”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend Bhaddaji, what is the best sight, the best sound, the best happiness, the best perception, and the best state of existence?”

segs.p: “Atthāvuso, brahmā abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthudaso vasavattī, yo taṁ brahmānaṁ passati, idaṁ dassanānaṁ aggaṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend, there is this Divinity, the vanquisher, the unvanquished, the universal seer, the wielder of power. When you see the Divinity, that’s the best sight.

segs.p: Atthāvuso, ābhassarā nāma devā sukhena abhisannā parisannā.
segs.e: There are the gods called ‘of sublime luminosity’, who are drenched and steeped in pleasure.
Every so often they feel inspired to exclaim:
‘Oh, what bliss! Oh, what bliss!’

segs.p: Yo taṁ saddaṁ suṇāti, idaṁ savanānaṁ aggaṁ.
segs.e: When you hear that, it’s the best sound.
There are the gods called ‘of universal beauty’.

segs.p: Te santaṁyeva tusitā sukhaṁ paṭivedenti, idaṁ sukhānaṁ aggaṁ.
segs.e: Since they’re truly content, they experience pleasure. This is the best happiness.

segs.p: Atthāvuso, ākiñcaññāyatanūpagā devā, idaṁ saññānaṁ aggaṁ.
segs.e: There are the gods reborn in the dimension of nothingness. This is the best perception.

segs.p: Atthāvuso, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagā devā, idaṁ bhavānaṁ aggan”ti.
segs.e: There are the gods reborn in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. This is the best state of existence.”

segs.p: “Sameti kho idaṁ āyasmato bhaddajissa, yadidaṁ bahunā janenā”ti?
segs.e: “So, Venerable Bhaddaji, do you agree with what most people say about this?”
“Well, Venerable Ānanda, you’re very learned.
Why don’t you clarify this yourself?”

segs.p: “Tenahāvuso bhaddaji, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, Reverend Bhaddaji, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā bhaddaji āyasmato ānandassa paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” Bhaddaji replied.
Ānanda said this:

segs.p: “Yathā passato kho, āvuso, anantarā āsavānaṁ khayo hoti, idaṁ dassanānaṁ aggaṁ.
segs.e: “What you see when the defilements are ended without delay is the best sight.

segs.p: Yathā suṇato anantarā āsavānaṁ khayo hoti, idaṁ savanānaṁ aggaṁ.
segs.e: What you hear when the defilements are ended without delay is the best sound.

segs.p: Yathā sukhitassa anantarā āsavānaṁ khayo hoti, idaṁ sukhānaṁ aggaṁ.
segs.e: The happiness you feel when the defilements are ended without delay is the best happiness.

segs.p: Yathā saññissa anantarā āsavānaṁ khayo hoti, idaṁ saññānaṁ aggaṁ.
segs.e: What you perceive when the defilements are ended without delay is the best perception.

segs.p: Yathā bhūtassa anantarā āsavānaṁ khayo hoti, idaṁ bhavānaṁ aggan”ti.
segs.e: The state of existence in which the defilements are ended without delay is the best state of existence.”
Numbered Discourses 5.171
18. A Lay Follower
Timidity
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato upāsako sārajjaṁ okkanto hoti.
segs.e: “A lay follower with five qualities is overcome by timidity.
What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī hoti.
segs.e: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, and consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato upāsako sārajjaṁ okkanto hoti.
segs.e: A lay follower with these five qualities is overcome by timidity.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato upāsako visārado hoti.
segs.e: A lay follower with five qualities is self-assured.
What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato upāsako visārado hotī”ti.
segs.e: A lay follower with these five qualities is self-assured.”
Numbered Discourses 5.172
18. A Lay Follower
Assured

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato upāsako avisārado agāraṁ ajjhāvasati.
segs.e: “A lay follower living at home with five qualities is not self-assured.
What five?
They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, and consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato upāsako avisārado agāraṁ ajjhāvasati.
segs.e: A lay follower living at home with these five qualities is not self-assured.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato upāsako visārado agāraṁ ajjhāvasati.
segs.e: A lay follower living at home with these five qualities is self-assured.
What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato upāsako visārado agāraṁ ajjhāvasatī”ti.
segs.e: A lay follower living at home with these five qualities is self-assured.”
Numbered Discourses 5.173
18. A Lay Follower
Hell

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato upāsako yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a lay follower with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?
They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, and consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato upāsako yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: A lay follower with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato upāsako yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: A lay follower with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato upāsako yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: A lay follower with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.174
18. A Lay Follower
Threats

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Pañca, gahapati, bhayāni verāni appahāya ‘dussīlo’ iti vuccati, nirayañca upapajjati.
segs.e: “Householder, unless these five fears and enmities are given up, one is said to be unethical, and is reborn in hell.
What five?
Killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: imāni kho, gahapati, pañca bhayāni verāni appahāya ‘dussīlo’ iti vuccati, nirayañca upapajjati.
segs.e: Unless these five fears and enmities are given up, one is said to be unethical, and is reborn in hell.

segs.p: Pañca, gahapati, bhayāni verāni pahāya ‘sīlavā’ iti vuccati, sugatiñca upapajjati.
segs.e: Once these five fears and enmities are given up, one is said to be ethical, and is reborn in a good place.
What five?
Killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: imāni kho, gahapati, pañca bhayāni verāni pahāya ‘sīlavā’ iti vuccati, sugatiñca upapajjati.
segs.e: Once these five fears and enmities are given up, one is said to be ethical, and is reborn in a good place.

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, pāṇātipātī pāṇātipātapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti, pāṇātipātā paṭivirato neva diṭṭhadhammikaṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, na samparāyikaṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, na cetasikaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: Anyone who kills living creatures brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. Anyone who refrains from killing living creatures does not brim with fear and enmity either in this life or in lives to come, and doesn’t experience mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: So that fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from killing living creatures.
Anyone who steals …
Anyone who commits sexual misconduct …
Anyone who lies …

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato neva diṭṭhadhammikaṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, na samparāyikaṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, na cetasikaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: Anyone who consumes beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness. Anyone who refrains from beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants does not brim with fear and enmity either in this life or in lives to come, and doesn’t experience mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: Surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hotīti.
segs.e: So that fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants.
Someone in this world
who kills living creatures,
speaks falsely, steals,
commits adultery,
and indulges in drinking
beer and wine—
unless they give up these five threats,
they’re said to be unethical.
When their body breaks up, that witless person
is reborn in hell.
But someone in this world
who doesn’t kill living creatures,
speak falsely, steal,
commit adultery,
or indulge in drinking
beer and wine—
having given up these five threats,
they’re said to be ethical.
When their body breaks up, that wise person
is reborn in a good place.”
Numbered Discourses 5.175
18. A Lay Follower
Corpse-worker

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato upāsako upāsakacaṇḍālo ca hoti upāsakamalañca upāsakapatikuṭṭho ca.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a lay follower with five qualities is a corpse-worker, a stain, and a reject among lay followers.
What five?
They’re faithless.
They’re unethical.

segs.p: kotūhalamaṅgaliko hoti, maṅgalaṁ pacceti no kammaṁ;
segs.e: They follow boisterous, superstitious rites, believing in omens rather than deeds.
They seek outside of the Buddhist community for those worthy of religious donations.
And they make offerings there first.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato upāsako upāsakacaṇḍālo ca hoti upāsakamalañca upāsakapatikuṭṭho ca.
segs.e: A lay follower with these five qualities is a corpse-worker, a stain, and a reject among lay followers.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato upāsako upāsakaratanañca hoti upāsakapadumañca upāsakapuṇḍarīkañca.
segs.e: A lay follower with five qualities is a gem, a pink lotus, and a white lotus among lay followers.
What five?
They’re faithful.
They’re ethical.

segs.p: akotūhalamaṅgaliko hoti, kammaṁ pacceti no maṅgalaṁ;
segs.e: They don’t practice boisterous, superstitious rites, and believe in deeds rather than omens.
They don’t seek outside of the Buddhist community for those worthy of religious donations.
And they don’t make offerings there first.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato upāsako upāsakaratanañca hoti upāsakapadumañca upāsakapuṇḍarīkañcā”ti.
segs.e: A lay follower with these five qualities is a gem, a pink lotus, and a white lotus among lay followers.”
Numbered Discourses 5.176
18. A Lay Follower
Rapture

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati pañcamattehi upāsakasatehi parivuto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, escorted by around five hundred lay followers, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:
“Householders, you have supplied the mendicant Saṅgha with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Na kho, gahapati, tāvatakeneva tuṭṭhi karaṇīyā:
segs.e: But you should not be content with just this much.
So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘kinti mayaṁ kālena kālaṁ pavivekaṁ pītiṁ upasampajja vihareyyāmā’ti.
segs.e: ‘How can we, from time to time, enter and dwell in the rapture of seclusion?’
That’s how you should train.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Sāriputta said to the Buddha,
“It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!
How well said this was by the Buddha:
‘Householders, you have supplied the mendicant Saṅgha with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Na kho, gahapati, tāvatakeneva tuṭṭhi karaṇīyā—
segs.e: But you should not be content with just this much.
So you should train like this:

segs.p: kinti mayaṁ kālena kālaṁ pavivekaṁ pītiṁ upasampajja vihareyyāmāti.
segs.e: “How can we, from time to time, enter and dwell in the rapture of seclusion?”
That’s how you should train.’

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhante, samaye ariyasāvako pavivekaṁ pītiṁ upasampajja viharati, pañcassa ṭhānāni tasmiṁ samaye na honti.
segs.e: At a time when a noble disciple enters and dwells in the rapture of seclusion, five things aren’t present in him.

segs.p: Yampissa kāmūpasaṁhitaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ, tampissa tasmiṁ samaye na hoti.
segs.e: The pain and sadness connected with sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Yampissa kāmūpasaṁhitaṁ sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, tampissa tasmiṁ samaye na hoti.
segs.e: The pleasure and happiness connected with sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Yampissa akusalūpasaṁhitaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ, tampissa tasmiṁ samaye na hoti.
segs.e: The pain and sadness connected with the unskillful.

segs.p: Yampissa akusalūpasaṁhitaṁ sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, tampissa tasmiṁ samaye na hoti.
segs.e: The pleasure and happiness connected with the unskillful.

segs.p: Yampissa kusalūpasaṁhitaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ, tampissa tasmiṁ samaye na hoti.
segs.e: The pain and sadness connected with the skillful.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhante, samaye ariyasāvako pavivekaṁ pītiṁ upasampajja viharati, imānissa pañca ṭhānāni tasmiṁ samaye na hontī”ti.
segs.e: At a time when a noble disciple enters and dwells in the rapture of seclusion, these five things aren’t present in him.”
“Good, good, Sāriputta!

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, sāriputta, samaye ariyasāvako pavivekaṁ pītiṁ upasampajja viharati, pañcassa ṭhānāni tasmiṁ samaye na honti.
segs.e: At a time when a noble disciple enters and dwells in the rapture of seclusion, five things aren’t present in him.

segs.p: Yampissa kāmūpasaṁhitaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ, tampissa tasmiṁ samaye na hoti.
segs.e: The pain and sadness connected with sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Yampissa kāmūpasaṁhitaṁ sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, tampissa tasmiṁ samaye na hoti.
segs.e: The pleasure and happiness connected with sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Yampissa akusalūpasaṁhitaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ, tampissa tasmiṁ samaye na hoti.
segs.e: The pain and sadness connected with the unskillful.

segs.p: Yampissa akusalūpasaṁhitaṁ sukhaṁ somanassaṁ, tampissa tasmiṁ samaye na hoti.
segs.e: The pleasure and happiness connected with the unskillful.

segs.p: Yampissa kusalūpasaṁhitaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ, tampissa tasmiṁ samaye na hoti.
segs.e: The pain and sadness connected with the skillful.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, sāriputta, samaye ariyasāvako pavivekaṁ pītiṁ upasampajja viharati, imānissa pañca ṭhānāni tasmiṁ samaye na hontī”ti.
segs.e: At a time when a noble disciple enters and dwells in the rapture of seclusion, these five things aren’t present in him.”
Numbered Discourses 5.177
18. A Lay Follower
Trades
“Mendicants, a lay follower should not engage in these five trades.
What five?
Trade in weapons, living creatures, meat, intoxicants, and poisons.

segs.p: imā kho, bhikkhave, pañca vaṇijjā upāsakena akaraṇīyā”ti.
segs.e: A lay follower should not engage in these five trades.”
Numbered Discourses 5.178
18. A Lay Follower
Kings
“What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu tumhehi diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā:
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard
of a person who has given up killing living creatures,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā pāṇātipātā veramaṇihetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karontī’”ti?
segs.e: and the kings have them arrested for that, and execute, imprison, or banish them, or do what the case requires?”
“No, sir.”
“Good, mendicants!

segs.p: Mayāpi kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, neva diṭṭhaṁ na sutaṁ:
segs.e: I too have never seen or heard of such a thing.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā pāṇātipātā veramaṇihetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karontī’ti.
Api ca khvassa tatheva pāpakammaṁ pavedenti:
segs.e: Rather, the kings are informed of someone’s bad deed:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ puriso itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā jīvitā voropesīti.
segs.e: ‘This person has murdered a man or a woman.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā pāṇātipātahetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karonti.
segs.e: The kings have them arrested for killing, and execute, imprison, or banish them, or do what the case requires.

segs.p: Api nu tumhehi evarūpaṁ diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā’”ti?
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard of such a case?”
“Sir, we have seen it and heard of it, and we will hear of it again.”
“What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu tumhehi diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā:
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard
of a person who has given up stealing,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā adinnādānā veramaṇihetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karontī’”ti?
segs.e: and the kings have them arrested for that …?”
“No, sir.”
“Good, mendicants!

segs.p: Mayāpi kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, neva diṭṭhaṁ na sutaṁ:
segs.e: I too have never seen or heard of such a thing.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā adinnādānā veramaṇihetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karontī’ti.
Api ca khvassa tatheva pāpakammaṁ pavedenti:
segs.e: Rather, the kings are informed of someone’s bad deed:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ puriso gāmā vā araññā vā adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādiyīti.
segs.e: ‘This person took something from a village or wilderness, with the intention to commit theft.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā adinnādānahetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karonti.
segs.e: The kings have them arrested for stealing …

segs.p: Api nu tumhehi evarūpaṁ diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā’”ti?
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard of such a case?”
“Sir, we have seen it and heard of it, and we will hear of it again.”
“What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu tumhehi diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā:
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard
of a person who has given up sexual misconduct,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇihetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karontī’”ti?
segs.e: and the kings have them arrested for that …?”
“No, sir.”
“Good, mendicants!

segs.p: Mayāpi kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, neva diṭṭhaṁ na sutaṁ:
segs.e: I too have never seen or heard of such a thing.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇihetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karontī’ti.
Api ca khvassa tatheva pāpakammaṁ pavedenti:
segs.e: Rather, the kings are informed of someone’s bad deed:
‘This person had relations with women or maidens under someone else’s protection.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā kāmesumicchācārahetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karonti.
segs.e: The kings have them arrested for that …

segs.p: Api nu tumhehi evarūpaṁ diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā’”ti?
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard of such a case?”
“Sir, we have seen it and heard of it, and we will hear of it again.”
“What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu tumhehi diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā:
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard
of a person who has given up lying,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā musāvādā veramaṇihetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karontī’”ti?
segs.e: and the kings have them arrested for that …?”
“No, sir.”
“Good, mendicants!

segs.p: Mayāpi kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, neva diṭṭhaṁ na sutaṁ:
segs.e: I too have never seen or heard of such a thing.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā musāvādā veramaṇihetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karontī’ti.
Api ca khvassa tatheva pāpakammaṁ pavedenti:
segs.e: Rather, the kings are informed of someone’s bad deed:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ puriso gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā musāvādena atthaṁ pabhañjīti.
segs.e: ‘This person has ruined a householder or householder’s child by lying.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā musāvādahetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karonti.
segs.e: The kings have them arrested for that …

segs.p: Api nu tumhehi evarūpaṁ diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā’”ti?
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard of such a case?”
“Sir, we have seen it and heard of it, and we will hear of it again.”
“What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: api nu tumhehi diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā:
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard
of a person who has given up intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇihetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karontī’”ti?
segs.e: and the kings have them arrested for that, and execute, imprison, or banish them, or do what the case requires?”
“No, sir.”
“Good, mendicants!

segs.p: Mayāpi kho etaṁ, bhikkhave, neva diṭṭhaṁ na sutaṁ:
segs.e: I too have never seen or heard of such a thing.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇihetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karontī’ti.
Api ca khvassa tatheva pāpakammaṁ pavedenti:
segs.e: Rather, the kings are informed of someone’s bad deed:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ puriso surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānaṁ anuyutto itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā jīvitā voropesi;
segs.e: ‘While under the influence of intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor, this person murdered a woman or a man.

segs.p: ayaṁ puriso surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānaṁ anuyutto gāmā vā araññā vā adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādiyi;
segs.e: Or they stole something from a village or wilderness.

segs.p: ayaṁ puriso surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānaṁ anuyutto paritthīsu parakumārīsu cārittaṁ āpajji;
segs.e: Or they had relations with women or maidens under someone else’s protection.

segs.p: ayaṁ puriso surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānaṁ anuyutto gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā musāvādena atthaṁ pabhañjīti.
segs.e: Or they ruined a householder or householder’s child by lying.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rājāno gahetvā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānahetu hananti vā bandhanti vā pabbājenti vā yathāpaccayaṁ vā karonti.
segs.e: The kings have them arrested for being under the influence of intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor, and execute, imprison, or banish them, or do what the case requires.

segs.p: Api nu tumhehi evarūpaṁ diṭṭhaṁ vā sutaṁ vā’”ti?
segs.e: Have you ever seen or heard of such a case?”
“Sir, we have seen it and heard of it, and we will hear of it again.”
Numbered Discourses 5.179
18. A Lay Follower
A Layperson

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati pañcamattehi upāsakasatehi parivuto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, escorted by around five hundred lay followers, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Venerable Sāriputta:

segs.p: “yaṁ kañci, sāriputta, jāneyyātha gihiṁ odātavasanaṁ pañcasu sikkhāpadesu saṁvutakammantaṁ catunnaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhiṁ akicchalābhiṁ akasiralābhiṁ, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: “You should know this, Sāriputta, about those white-clothed laypeople whose actions are restrained in the five precepts, and who get four blissful meditations in this life belonging to the higher mind when they want, without trouble or difficulty. They may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’
And what are the five precepts in which their actions are restrained?

segs.p: Idha, sāriputta, ariyasāvako pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.
These are the five precepts in which their actions are restrained.

segs.p: Katamesaṁ catunnaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī?
segs.e: And what are the four blissful meditations in this life belonging to the higher mind that they get when they want, without trouble or difficulty?

segs.p: Idha, sāriputta, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi, satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Ayamassa paṭhamo ābhicetasiko diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro adhigato hoti avisuddhassa cittassa visuddhiyā apariyodātassa cittassa pariyodapanāya.
segs.e: This is the first blissful meditation in this life belonging to the higher mind, which they achieve in order to purify the unpurified mind and cleanse the unclean mind.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, sāriputta, ariyasāvako dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

segs.p: Ayamassa dutiyo ābhicetasiko diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro adhigato hoti avisuddhassa cittassa visuddhiyā apariyodātassa cittassa pariyodapanāya.
segs.e: This is the second blissful meditation …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, sāriputta, ariyasāvako saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: Ayamassa tatiyo ābhicetasiko diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro adhigato hoti avisuddhassa cittassa visuddhiyā apariyodātassa cittassa pariyodapanāya.
segs.e: This is the third blissful meditation …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, sāriputta, ariyasāvako ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segs.p: Ayamassa catuttho ābhicetasiko diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro adhigato hoti avisuddhassa cittassa visuddhiyā apariyodātassa cittassa pariyodapanāya.
segs.e: This is the fourth blissful meditation in this life belonging to the higher mind, which they achieve in order to purify the unpurified mind and cleanse the unclean mind.

segs.p: Imesaṁ catunnaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī.
segs.e: These are the four blissful meditations in this life belonging to the higher mind that they get when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: Yaṁ kañci, sāriputta, jāneyyātha gihiṁ odātavasanaṁ—imesu pañcasu sikkhāpadesu saṁvutakammantaṁ, imesañca catunnaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhiṁ akicchalābhiṁ akasiralābhiṁ, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: You should know this, Sāriputta, about those white-clothed laypeople whose actions are restrained in the five precepts, and who get four blissful meditations in this life belonging to the higher mind when they want, without trouble or difficulty. They may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’
Seeing the peril in the hells,
you should shun bad deeds.
Taking up the teaching of the noble ones,
an astute person should shun them.
You shouldn’t harm living beings,
so long as strength is found.
Nor should you knowingly speak falsehood,
or take what is not given.
Content with your own partners,
you should stay away from the partners of others.
A personage shouldn’t drink wine or toddy,
as they confuse the mind.
You should recollect the Buddha,
and reflect on the teaching.
You should develop a harmless mind of welfare,
which leads to the realms of gods.
When suitable gifts to give are available
to someone who seeks and needs merit,
a religious donation is abundant
if given first to the peaceful ones.
I will tell of the peaceful ones,
Sāriputta, listen to me.
Cows may be black or white,
red or tawny,
mottled or uniform,
or pigeon-colored.
But when one is born among them,
the bull that’s tamed—
a behemoth, powerful,
well-paced in pulling forward—
they yoke the load just to him,
regardless of his color.
So it is for humans,
wherever they may be born—
among aristocrats, brahmins, peasants,
menials, or corpse-workers and scavengers—
but when one is born among them,
tamed, true to their vows.
Firm in principle, accomplished in ethical conduct,
truthful, conscientious,
they’ve given up birth and death,
and have completed the spiritual journey.
With burden put down, detached,
they’ve completed the task <j>and are free of defilements.
Gone beyond all things,
they’re quenched by not grasping.
In that flawless field,
a religious donation is abundant.
Fools who don’t understand—
unlearned simpletons—
give their gifts to those outside,
and don’t attend the peaceful ones.
But those who do attend the peaceful ones—
wise, esteemed as attentive—
and whose faith in the Holy One
has roots planted deep,
they go to the realm of the gods,
or are born here in a good family.
Gradually those astute ones
reach extinguishment.”
Numbered Discourses 5.180
18. A Lay Follower
About Gavesī

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṁ carati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kosalans together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā addhānamaggappaṭipanno aññatarasmiṁ padese mahantaṁ sālavanaṁ;
segs.e: While traveling along a road the Buddha saw a large sal grove in a certain spot.

segs.p: disvāna maggā okkamma yena taṁ sālavanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ sālavanaṁ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṁ padese sitaṁ pātvākāsi.
segs.e: He left the road, went to the sal grove, and plunged deep into it. And at a certain spot he smiled.
Then Venerable Ānanda thought,

segs.p: “ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo bhagavato sitassa pātukammāya?
segs.e: “What is the cause, what is the reason why the Buddha smiled?
Realized Ones do not smile for no reason.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: So Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo bhagavato sitassa pātukammāya?
segs.e: “What is the cause, what is the reason why the Buddha smiled?
Realized Ones do not smile for no reason.”

segs.p: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, ānanda, imasmiṁ padese nagaraṁ ahosi iddhañceva phītañca bahujanaṁ ākiṇṇamanussaṁ.
segs.e: “Once upon a time, Ānanda, there was a city in this spot that was successful and prosperous, populous and full of people.

segs.p: Taṁ kho panānanda, nagaraṁ kassapo bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho upanissāya vihāsi.
segs.e: And Kassapa, a blessed one, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, lived supported by that city.

segs.p: Kassapassa kho panānanda, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa gavesī nāma upāsako ahosi sīlesu aparipūrakārī.
segs.e: He had a lay follower named Gavesī who had not fulfilled all the precepts.

segs.p: Gavesinā kho, ānanda, upāsakena pañcamattāni upāsakasatāni paṭidesitāni samādapitāni ahesuṁ sīlesu aparipūrakārino.
segs.e: And the five hundred lay followers who were taught and advised by Gavesī also had not fulfilled all the precepts.

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, gavesissa upāsakassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Gavesī thought:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upāsakasatānaṁ bahūpakāro pubbaṅgamo samādapetā, ahañcamhi sīlesu aparipūrakārī, imāni ca pañca upāsakasatāni sīlesu aparipūrakārino.
segs.e: ‘I’m the helper, leader, and adviser of these five hundred lay followers, yet neither I nor they have fulfilled the precepts.
We’re the same, I’m in no way better.
So let me do better.’

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, gavesī upāsako yena tāni pañca upāsakasatāni tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tāni pañca upāsakasatāni etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Gavesī went to those five hundred lay followers and said to them:
‘From this day forth may the venerables remember me as one who has fulfilled the precepts.’

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, tesaṁ pañcannaṁ upāsakasatānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then those five hundred lay followers thought:

segs.p: ‘ayyo kho gavesī amhākaṁ bahūpakāro pubbaṅgamo samādapetā.
segs.e: ‘Master Gavesī is our helper, leader, and adviser,

segs.p: Ayyo hi nāma gavesī sīlesu paripūrakārī bhavissati.
segs.e: and now he will fulfill the precepts.
Why don’t we do the same?’

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, tāni pañca upāsakasatāni yena gavesī upāsako tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā gavesiṁ upāsakaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then those five hundred lay followers went to Gavesī and said to him:

segs.p: ‘ajjatagge ayyo gavesī imānipi pañca upāsakasatāni sīlesu paripūrakārino dhāretū’ti.
segs.e: ‘From this day forth may Master Gavesī remember these five hundred lay followers as having fulfilled the precepts.’

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, gavesissa upāsakassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Gavesī thought:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upāsakasatānaṁ bahūpakāro pubbaṅgamo samādapetā, ahañcamhi sīlesu paripūrakārī, imānipi pañca upāsakasatāni sīlesu paripūrakārino.
segs.e: ‘I’m the helper, leader, and adviser of these five hundred lay followers, and both I and they have fulfilled the precepts.
We’re the same, I’m in no way better.
So let me do better.’

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, gavesī upāsako yena tāni pañca upāsakasatāni tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tāni pañca upāsakasatāni etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Gavesī went to those five hundred lay followers and said to them:

segs.p: ‘ajjatagge maṁ āyasmanto brahmacāriṁ dhāretha ārācāriṁ virataṁ methunā gāmadhammā’ti.
segs.e: ‘From this day forth may the venerables remember me as one who is chaste, set apart, refraining from the vulgar act of sex.’

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, tesaṁ pañcannaṁ upāsakasatānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then those five hundred lay followers did the same. …

segs.p: ‘ayyo kho gavesī amhākaṁ bahūpakāro pubbaṅgamo samādapetā.
Ayyo hi nāma gavesī brahmacārī bhavissati ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā.
Atha kho, ānanda, tāni pañca upāsakasatāni yena gavesī upāsako tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā gavesiṁ upāsakaṁ etadavocuṁ:
‘ajjatagge ayyo gavesī imānipi pañca upāsakasatāni brahmacārino dhāretu ārācārino viratā methunā gāmadhammā’ti.
Atha kho, ānanda, gavesissa upāsakassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Gavesī thought:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upāsakasatānaṁ bahūpakāro pubbaṅgamo samādapetā.
segs.e: ‘These five hundred lay followers …

segs.p: Ahañcamhi brahmacārī ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā.
Imānipi pañca upāsakasatāni brahmacārino ārācārino viratā methunā gāmadhammā.
segs.e: are chaste, set apart, refraining from the vulgar act of sex.
We’re the same, I’m in no way better.
So let me do better.’

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, gavesī upāsako yena tāni pañca upāsakasatāni tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tāni pañca upāsakasatāni etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Gavesī went to those five hundred lay followers and said to them:

segs.p: ‘ajjatagge maṁ āyasmanto ekabhattikaṁ dhāretha rattūparataṁ virataṁ vikālabhojanā’ti.
segs.e: ‘From this day forth may the venerables remember me as one who eats in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night, and from food at the wrong time.’

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, tesaṁ pañcannaṁ upāsakasatānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then those five hundred lay followers did the same. …

segs.p: Ayyo hi nāma gavesī ekabhattiko bhavissati rattūparato virato vikālabhojanā.
Atha kho, ānanda, tāni pañca upāsakasatāni yena gavesī upāsako tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā gavesiṁ upāsakaṁ etadavocuṁ:
‘ajjatagge ayyo gavesī imānipi pañca upāsakasatāni ekabhattike dhāretu rattūparate virate vikālabhojanā’ti.
Atha kho, ānanda, gavesissa upāsakassa etadahosi:
segs.e: Then Gavesī thought:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho imesaṁ pañcannaṁ upāsakasatānaṁ bahūpakāro pubbaṅgamo samādapetā.
segs.e: ‘These five hundred lay followers …

segs.p: Ahañcamhi brahmacārī ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā.
Imānipi pañca upāsakasatāni brahmacārino ārācārino viratā methunā gāmadhammā.
Imānipi pañca upāsakasatāni ekabhattikā rattūparatā viratā vikālabhojanā.
segs.e: eat in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night, and food at the wrong time.
We’re the same, I’m in no way better.
So let me do better.’

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, gavesī upāsako yena kassapo bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā kassapaṁ bhagavantaṁ arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the lay follower Gavesī went up to the blessed one Kassapa, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha and said to him:

segs.p: ‘labheyyāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṁ labheyyaṁ upasampadan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Sir, may I receive the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence?’

segs.p: Alattha kho, ānanda, gavesī upāsako kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike pabbajjaṁ, alattha upasampadaṁ.
segs.e: And he received the going forth, the ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

segs.p: Acirūpasampanno kho panānanda, gavesī bhikkhu eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Not long after his ordination, the mendicant Gavesī, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: ‘Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.’

segs.p: Aññataro ca panānanda, gavesī bhikkhu arahataṁ ahosi.
segs.e: And the mendicant Gavesī became one of the perfected.

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, tesaṁ pañcannaṁ upāsakasatānaṁ etadahosi:
segs.e: Then those five hundred lay followers thought:

segs.p: ‘ayyo kho gavesī amhākaṁ bahūpakāro pubbaṅgamo samādapetā.
segs.e: ‘Master Gavesī is our helper, leader, and adviser,

segs.p: Ayyo hi nāma gavesī kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajissati.
segs.e: He has shaved off his hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and gone forth from the lay life to homelessness.
Why don’t we do the same?’

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, tāni pañca upāsakasatāni yena kassapo bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā kassapaṁ bhagavantaṁ arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then those five hundred lay followers went up to the blessed one Kassapa, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha and said to him:

segs.p: ‘labheyyāma mayaṁ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṁ, labheyyāma upasampadan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Sir, may we receive the going forth and ordination in the Buddha’s presence?’

segs.p: Alabhiṁsu kho, ānanda, tāni pañca upāsakasatāni kassapassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike pabbajjaṁ, alabhiṁsu upasampadaṁ.
segs.e: And they did receive the going forth and ordination in the Buddha’s presence.

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, gavesissa bhikkhuno etadahosi:
segs.e: Then the mendicant Gavesī thought:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ kho imassa anuttarassa vimuttisukhassa nikāmalābhī homi akicchalābhī akasiralābhī.
segs.e: ‘I get the supreme bliss of freedom whenever I want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: Aho vatimānipi pañca bhikkhusatāni imassa anuttarassa vimuttisukhassa nikāmalābhino assu akicchalābhino akasiralābhino’ti.
segs.e: Oh, may these five hundred mendicants do the same!’

segs.p: Atha kho, ānanda, tāni pañca bhikkhusatāni vūpakaṭṭhā appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharantā nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—
segs.e: Then those five hundred mendicants, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. They lived having achieved with their own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihariṁsu.
‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti abbhaññiṁsu.
segs.e: They understood: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

segs.p: Iti kho, ānanda, tāni pañca bhikkhusatāni gavesīpamukhāni uttaruttari paṇītapaṇītaṁ vāyamamānā anuttaraṁ vimuttiṁ sacchākaṁsu.
segs.e: And so, Ānanda, those five hundred mendicants headed by Gavesī, trying to go higher and higher, better and better, realized the supreme bliss of freedom.
So you should train like this:
‘Trying to go higher and higher, better and better, we will realize the supreme bliss of freedom.’
That’s how you should train.”
Numbered Discourses 5.181
19. Wilderness Dwellers
Wilderness Dwellers
“Mendicants, there are these five kinds of wilderness dwellers.
What five?

segs.p: Mandattā momūhattā āraññiko hoti, pāpiccho icchāpakato āraññiko hoti, ummādā cittakkhepā āraññiko hoti, vaṇṇitaṁ buddhehi buddhasāvakehīti āraññiko hoti, appicchataṁyeva nissāya santuṭṭhiṁyeva nissāya sallekhaṁyeva nissāya pavivekaṁyeva nissāya idamatthitaṁyeva nissāya āraññiko hoti.
segs.e: One may be a wilderness dweller because of stupidity and folly. Or because of corrupt wishes, being of wishful temperament. Or because of madness and mental disorder. Or because it is praised by the Buddhas and their disciples. Or for the sake of having few wishes, for the sake of contentment, self-effacement, seclusion, and simplicity.
These are the five kinds of wilderness dwellers.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ āraññikānaṁ yvāyaṁ āraññiko appicchataṁyeva nissāya santuṭṭhiṁyeva nissāya sallekhaṁyeva nissāya pavivekaṁyeva nissāya idamatthitaṁyeva nissāya āraññiko hoti, ayaṁ imesaṁ pañcannaṁ āraññikānaṁ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca.
segs.e: But the one who dwells in the wilderness for the sake of having few wishes is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of the five.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṁ, khīramhā dadhi, dadhimhā navanītaṁ, navanītamhā sappi, sappimhā sappimaṇḍo, sappimaṇḍo tattha aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: From a cow comes milk, from milk comes curds, from curds come butter, from butter comes ghee, and from ghee comes cream of ghee. And the cream of ghee is said to be the best of these.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, imesaṁ pañcannaṁ āraññikānaṁ yvāyaṁ āraññiko appicchataṁyeva nissāya santuṭṭhiṁyeva nissāya sallekhaṁyeva nissāya pavivekaṁyeva nissāya idamatthitaṁyeva nissāya āraññiko hoti, ayaṁ imesaṁ pañcannaṁ āraññikānaṁ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, the one who dwells in the wilderness for the sake of having few wishes is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of the five.”
Numbered Discourses 5.182
19. Wilderness Dwellers
Robes
“Mendicants, these five wear rag robes.
What five?

segs.p: Mandattā momūhattā paṁsukūliko hoti …pe… idamatthitaṁyeva nissāya paṁsukūliko hoti.
segs.e: One may wear rag robes because of stupidity … corrupt wishes … madness … because it is praised by the Buddhas … or for the sake of having few wishes …
These are the five who wear rag robes.”

19. Wilderness Dwellers
Those Who Eat Only From the Almsbowl
“Mendicants, these five eat only from the almsbowl.
What five?

segs.p: Mandattā momūhattā pattapiṇḍiko hoti, pāpiccho icchāpakato pattapiṇḍiko hoti, ummādā cittakkhepā pattapiṇḍiko hoti, ‘vaṇṇitaṁ buddhehi buddhasāvakehī’ti pattapiṇḍiko hoti, appicchataṁyeva nissāya santuṭṭhiṁyeva nissāya sallekhaṁyeva nissāya pavivekaṁyeva nissāya idamatthitaṁyeva nissāya pattapiṇḍiko hoti.
segs.e: One may eat only from the almsbowl because of stupidity and folly. Or because of corrupt wishes, being of wishful temperament. Or because of madness and mental disorder. Or because it is praised by the Buddhas and their disciples. Or for the sake of having few wishes, for the sake of contentment, self-effacement, seclusion, and simplicity.
These are the five who eat only from the almsbowl.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ pattapiṇḍikānaṁ yvāyaṁ pattapiṇḍiko appicchataṁyeva nissāya santuṭṭhiṁyeva nissāya sallekhaṁyeva nissāya pavivekaṁyeva nissāya idamatthitaṁyeva nissāya pattapiṇḍiko hoti, ayaṁ imesaṁ pañcannaṁ pattapiṇḍikānaṁ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca.
segs.e: But the person who eats only from the almsbowl for the sake of having few wishes is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of the five.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṁ, khīramhā dadhi, dadhimhā navanītaṁ, navanītamhā sappi, sappimhā sappimaṇḍo, sappimaṇḍo tattha aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: From a cow comes milk, from milk comes curds, from curds come butter, from butter comes ghee, and from ghee comes cream of ghee. And the cream of ghee is said to be the best of these.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, imesaṁ pañcannaṁ pattapiṇḍikānaṁ yvāyaṁ pattapiṇḍiko appicchataṁyeva nissāya santuṭṭhiṁyeva nissāya sallekhaṁyeva nissāya pavivekaṁyeva nissāya idamatthitaṁyeva nissāya pattapiṇḍiko hoti, ayaṁ imesaṁ pañcannaṁ pattapiṇḍikānaṁ aggo ca seṭṭho ca mokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, the one who eats only from the almsbowl for the sake of having few wishes is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of the five.”
Numbered Discourses 5.191
20. Brahmins
Hounds

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, porāṇā brāhmaṇadhammā etarahi sunakhesu sandissanti, no brāhmaṇesu.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these five traditional principles of the brahmins are exhibited these days among hounds, but not among brahmins.
What five?

segs.p: Pubbe sudaṁ, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇiṁyeva gacchanti, no abrāhmaṇiṁ.
segs.e: In the past brahmins had sex only with brahmin women, not with others.

segs.p: Etarahi, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇimpi gacchanti, abrāhmaṇimpi gacchanti.
segs.e: These days brahmins have sex with both brahmin women and others.

segs.p: Etarahi, bhikkhave, sunakhā sunakhiṁyeva gacchanti, no asunakhiṁ.
segs.e: But these days hounds have sex only with female hounds, not with other species.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo porāṇo brāhmaṇadhammo etarahi sunakhesu sandissati, no brāhmaṇesu.
segs.e: This is the first ancient principle of the brahmins exhibited these days among hounds, but not among brahmins.

segs.p: Pubbe sudaṁ, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇiṁ utuniṁyeva gacchanti, no anutuniṁ.
segs.e: In the past brahmins had sex only with brahmin women in the fertile phase of the menstrual cycle, not at other times.

segs.p: Etarahi, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇiṁ utunimpi gacchanti, anutunimpi gacchanti.
segs.e: These days brahmins have sex with brahmin women both in the fertile phase of the menstrual cycle and at other times.

segs.p: Etarahi, bhikkhave, sunakhā sunakhiṁ utuniṁyeva gacchanti, no anutuniṁ.
segs.e: But these days hounds have sex only with female hounds when they are in heat, not at other times.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo porāṇo brāhmaṇadhammo etarahi sunakhesu sandissati, no brāhmaṇesu.
segs.e: This is the second ancient principle of the brahmins exhibited these days among hounds, but not among brahmins.

segs.p: Pubbe sudaṁ, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇiṁ neva kiṇanti no vikkiṇanti, sampiyeneva saṁvāsaṁ sambandhāya sampavattenti.
segs.e: In the past brahmins neither bought nor sold brahmin women. They lived together because they loved each other and wanted their family line to continue.

segs.p: Etarahi, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇiṁ kiṇantipi vikkiṇantipi, sampiyenapi saṁvāsaṁ sambandhāya sampavattenti.
segs.e: These days brahmins both buy and sell brahmin women. They live together whether they love each other or not and they want their family line to continue.

segs.p: Etarahi, bhikkhave, sunakhā sunakhiṁ neva kiṇanti no vikkiṇanti, sampiyeneva saṁvāsaṁ sambandhāya sampavattenti.
segs.e: But these days hounds neither buy nor sell female hounds. They live together because they’re attracted to each other and want their family line to continue.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo porāṇo brāhmaṇadhammo etarahi sunakhesu sandissati, no brāhmaṇesu.
segs.e: This is the third ancient principle of the brahmins exhibited these days among hounds, but not among brahmins.

segs.p: Pubbe sudaṁ, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇā na sannidhiṁ karonti dhanassapi dhaññassapi rajatassapi jātarūpassapi.
segs.e: In the past brahmins did not store up money, grain, silver, or gold.

segs.p: Etarahi, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇā sannidhiṁ karonti dhanassapi dhaññassapi rajatassapi jātarūpassapi.
segs.e: These days brahmins do store up money, grain, silver, and gold.

segs.p: Etarahi, bhikkhave, sunakhā na sannidhiṁ karonti dhanassapi dhaññassapi rajatassapi jātarūpassapi.
segs.e: But these days hounds don’t store up money, grain, silver, or gold.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho porāṇo brāhmaṇadhammo etarahi sunakhesu sandissati, no brāhmaṇesu.
segs.e: This is the fourth ancient principle of the brahmins exhibited these days among hounds, but not among brahmins.

segs.p: Pubbe sudaṁ, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇā sāyaṁ sāyamāsāya pāto pātarāsāya bhikkhaṁ pariyesanti.
segs.e: In the past brahmins went looking for almsfood for dinner at dusk, and for breakfast at daybreak.

segs.p: Etarahi, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇā yāvadatthaṁ udarāvadehakaṁ bhuñjitvā avasesaṁ ādāya pakkamanti.
segs.e: These days brahmins eat as much as they like until their bellies are full, then take away the leftovers.

segs.p: Etarahi, bhikkhave, sunakhā sāyaṁ sāyamāsāya pāto pātarāsāya bhikkhaṁ pariyesanti.
segs.e: But these days hounds go looking for dinner at dusk, and for breakfast at daybreak.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo porāṇo brāhmaṇadhammo etarahi sunakhesu sandissati, no brāhmaṇesu.
segs.e: This is the fifth ancient principle of the brahmins exhibited these days among hounds, but not among brahmins.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca porāṇā brāhmaṇadhammā etarahi sunakhesu sandissanti, no brāhmaṇesū”ti.
segs.e: These five ancient principles of the brahmins are exhibited these days among hounds, but not among brahmins.”
Numbered Discourses 5.192
20. Brahmins
With the Brahmin Doṇa

segs.p: Atha kho doṇo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Doṇa the brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho doṇo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, Doṇa sat down to one side, and said to the Buddha:
“Worthy Gotama, I have heard that

segs.p: ‘na samaṇo gotamo brāhmaṇe jiṇṇe vuḍḍhe mahallake addhagate vayoanuppatte abhivādeti vā paccuṭṭheti vā āsanena vā nimantetī’ti.
segs.e: the ascetic Gotama doesn’t bow to old brahmins, the elderly and senior, who are advanced in years and have reached the final stage of life; nor does he rise in their presence or offer them a seat.
And this is indeed the case,

segs.p: Na hi bhavaṁ gotamo brāhmaṇe jiṇṇe vuḍḍhe mahallake addhagate vayoanuppatte abhivādeti vā paccuṭṭheti vā āsanena vā nimanteti.
segs.e: for the worthy Gotama does not bow to old brahmins, elderly and senior, who are advanced in years and have reached the final stage of life; nor does he rise in their presence or offer them a seat.
This is not appropriate, worthy Gotama.”
“Doṇa, do you too claim to be a brahmin?”

segs.p: “Yañhi taṁ, bho gotama, sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, if anyone should be rightly called
a brahmin, it’s me.

segs.p: mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena, ajjhāyako mantadharo, tiṇṇaṁ vedānaṁ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṁ sākkharappabhedānaṁ itihāsapañcamānaṁ, padako veyyākaraṇo lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo’ti, mameva taṁ, bho gotama, sammā vadamāno vadeyya.
Ahañhi, bho gotama, brāhmaṇo ubhato sujāto—

mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena, ajjhāyako mantadharo, tiṇṇaṁ vedānaṁ pāragū sanighaṇḍukeṭubhānaṁ sākkharappabhedānaṁ itihāsapañcamānaṁ, padako veyyākaraṇo lokāyatamahāpurisalakkhaṇesu anavayo”ti.
segs.e: For I am well born on both my mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation. I recite and remember the hymns, and have mastered the three Vedas, together with their vocabularies and ritual performance, their phonology and word classification, and the testaments as fifth. I know them word-by-word, and their grammar. I am well versed in cosmology and the marks of a great man.”

segs.p: “Ye kho te, doṇa, brāhmaṇānaṁ pubbakā isayo mantānaṁ kattāro mantānaṁ pavattāro, yesamidaṁ etarahi brāhmaṇā porāṇaṁ mantapadaṁ gītaṁ pavuttaṁ samihitaṁ tadanugāyanti tadanubhāsanti bhāsitamanubhāsanti sajjhāyitamanusajjhāyanti vācitamanuvācenti, seyyathidaṁ—aṭṭhako, vāmako, vāmadevo, vessāmitto, yamadaggi, aṅgīraso, bhāradvājo, vāseṭṭho, kassapo, bhagu;
segs.e: “Doṇa, the ancient brahmin seers were Aṭṭhaka, Vāmaka, Vāmadeva, Vessāmitta, Yamadaggi, Aṅgīrasa, Bhāradvāja, Vāseṭṭha, Kassapa, and Bhagu. They were the authors and propagators of the hymns, whose hymnal was sung and propagated and compiled in ancient times. These days, brahmins continue to sing and chant it. They continue chanting what was chanted, rehearsing what was rehearsed, and teaching what was taught.
Those seers described five kinds of brahmins.

segs.p: brahmasamaṁ, devasamaṁ, mariyādaṁ, sambhinnamariyādaṁ, brāhmaṇacaṇḍālaṁyeva pañcamaṁ.
segs.e: A brahmin who is equal to the Divinity, one who is equal to a god, one who toes the line, one who crosses the line, and the fifth is a brahmin corpse-worker.
Which one of these are you, Doṇa?”

segs.p: “Na kho mayaṁ, bho gotama, pañca brāhmaṇe jānāma, atha kho mayaṁ brāhmaṇātveva jānāma.
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, we don’t know about these five kinds of brahmins. We just know the word ‘brahmin’.

segs.p: Sādhu me bhavaṁ gotamo tathā dhammaṁ desetu yathā ahaṁ ime pañca brāhmaṇe jāneyyan”ti.
segs.e: Worthy Gotama, please teach me this matter so I can learn about these five brahmins.”

segs.p: “Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, suṇohi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, brahmin, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”ti kho doṇo brāhmaṇo bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, worthy sir,” Doṇa replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Doṇa, how is a brahmin equal to the Divinity?

segs.p: Idha, doṇa, brāhmaṇo ubhato sujāto hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a brahmin is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

segs.p: mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena.
So aṭṭhacattālīsavassāni komārabrahmacariyaṁ carati mante adhīyamāno.
segs.e: For forty-eight years he leads the boy’s spiritual life studying the hymns.

segs.p: Aṭṭhacattālīsavassāni komārabrahmacariyaṁ caritvā mante adhīyitvā ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ pariyesati dhammeneva, no adhammena.
segs.e: Then he seeks a fee for his tutor, but only by legitimate means, not illegitimate.
In this context, Doṇa, what is legitimate?

segs.p: Neva kasiyā na vaṇijjāya na gorakkhena na issatthena na rājaporisena na sippaññatarena, kevalaṁ bhikkhācariyāya kapālaṁ anatimaññamāno.
segs.e: Not by farming, trade, raising cattle, archery, government service, or one of the professions, but solely by living on alms, not scorning the alms bowl.

segs.p: So ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ niyyādetvā kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajati.
segs.e: Having offered the fee to his tutor, he shaves off his hair and beard, dresses in ocher robes, and goes forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: So evaṁ pabbajito samāno mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ tathā tatiyaṁ tathā catutthaṁ, iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: Then they meditate spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.
They meditate spreading a heart full of compassion …
rejoicing …

segs.p: upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ tathā tatiyaṁ tathā catutthaṁ, iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: So ime cattāro brahmavihāre bhāvetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ brahmalokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: Having developed these four divine meditations, when the body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a realm of divinity.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, doṇa, brāhmaṇo brahmasamo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a brahmin is equal to the Divinity.
And how is a brahmin equal to a god?

segs.p: Idha, doṇa, brāhmaṇo ubhato sujāto hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a brahmin is well born on both the mother’s and the father’s sides …

segs.p: mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena.
So aṭṭhacattālīsavassāni komārabrahmacariyaṁ carati mante adhīyamāno.
Aṭṭhacattālīsavassāni komārabrahmacariyaṁ caritvā mante adhīyitvā ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ pariyesati dhammeneva, no adhammena.
Neva kasiyā na vaṇijjāya na gorakkhena na issatthena na rājaporisena na sippaññatarena, kevalaṁ bhikkhācariyāya kapālaṁ anatimaññamāno.
So ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ niyyādetvā dāraṁ pariyesati dhammeneva, no adhammena.
segs.e: Having offered the fee to his tutor, he seeks a wife, but only by legitimate means, not illegitimate.
In this context, Doṇa, what is legitimate?

segs.p: Neva kayena na vikkayena, brāhmaṇiṁyeva udakūpassaṭṭhaṁ.
segs.e: Not by buying or selling, he only accepts a brahmin woman by the pouring of water.

segs.p: So brāhmaṇiṁyeva gacchati, na khattiyiṁ na vessiṁ na suddiṁ na caṇḍāliṁ na nesādiṁ na veniṁ na rathakāriṁ na pukkusiṁ gacchati, na gabbhiniṁ gacchati, na pāyamānaṁ gacchati, na anutuniṁ gacchati.
segs.e: He has sex only with a brahmin woman. He does not have sex with a woman from a family of aristocrats, peasants, menials, corpse-workers, hunters, bamboo-workers, chariot-makers, or scavengers. Nor does he have sex with women who are pregnant, breastfeeding, or outside the fertile phase of the menstrual cycle.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, doṇa, brāhmaṇo na gabbhiniṁ gacchati?
segs.e: And why does the brahmin not have sex with a pregnant woman?

segs.p: Sace, doṇa, brāhmaṇo gabbhiniṁ gacchati, atimīḷhajo nāma so hoti māṇavako vā māṇavikā vā.
segs.e: If a brahmin had sex with a pregnant woman, the boy or girl would be born in too much filth.

segs.p: Tasmā, doṇa, brāhmaṇo na gabbhiniṁ gacchati.
segs.e: That’s why the brahmin doesn’t have sex with a pregnant woman.

segs.p: Kasmā ca, doṇa, brāhmaṇo na pāyamānaṁ gacchati?
segs.e: And why does the brahmin not have sex with a breastfeeding woman?

segs.p: Sace, doṇa, brāhmaṇo pāyamānaṁ gacchati, asucipaṭipīḷito nāma so hoti māṇavako vā māṇavikā vā.
segs.e: If a brahmin had sex with a breastfeeding woman, the boy or girl would drink back the semen.

segs.p: Tasmā, doṇa, brāhmaṇo na pāyamānaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: That’s why the brahmin doesn’t have sex with a breastfeeding woman.

segs.p: Tassa sā hoti brāhmaṇī neva kāmatthā na davatthā na ratatthā, pajatthāva brāhmaṇassa brāhmaṇī hoti.
segs.e: And why does the brahmin not have sex outside the fertile phase of the menstrual cycle? Because his brahmin wife is not there for sensual pleasure, fun, and enjoyment, but only for procreation.

segs.p: So methunaṁ uppādetvā kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajati.
segs.e: Having ensured his progeny through sex, he shaves off his hair and beard, dresses in ocher robes, and goes forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: So evaṁ pabbajito samāno vivicceva kāmehi …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: When he has gone forth, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, he enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.

segs.p: So ime cattāro jhāne bhāvetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: Having developed these four absorptions, when the body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, doṇa, brāhmaṇo devasamo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a brahmin is equal to god.
And how does a brahmin toe the line?

segs.p: Idha, doṇa, brāhmaṇo ubhato sujāto hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a brahmin is well born on both the mother’s and the father’s sides …

segs.p: mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena.
So aṭṭhacattālīsavassāni komārabrahmacariyaṁ carati mante adhīyamāno.
Aṭṭhacattālīsavassāni komārabrahmacariyaṁ caritvā mante adhīyitvā ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ pariyesati dhammeneva, no adhammena.
Neva kasiyā na vaṇijjāya na gorakkhena na issatthena na rājaporisena na sippaññatarena, kevalaṁ bhikkhācariyāya kapālaṁ anatimaññamāno.
So ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ niyyādetvā dāraṁ pariyesati dhammeneva, no adhammena.
Neva kayena na vikkayena, brāhmaṇiṁyeva udakūpassaṭṭhaṁ.
segs.e: Not by buying or selling, he only accepts a brahmin woman by the pouring of water.

segs.p: So brāhmaṇiṁyeva gacchati, na khattiyiṁ na vessiṁ na suddiṁ na caṇḍāliṁ na nesādiṁ na veniṁ na rathakāriṁ na pukkusiṁ gacchati, na gabbhiniṁ gacchati, na pāyamānaṁ gacchati, na anutuniṁ gacchati.
Kasmā ca, doṇa, brāhmaṇo na gabbhiniṁ gacchati?
Sace, doṇa, brāhmaṇo gabbhiniṁ gacchati, atimīḷhajo nāma so hoti māṇavako vā māṇavikā vā.
Tasmā, doṇa, brāhmaṇo na gabbhiniṁ gacchati.
Kasmā ca, doṇa, brāhmaṇo na pāyamānaṁ gacchati?
Sace, doṇa, brāhmaṇo pāyamānaṁ gacchati, asucipaṭipīḷito nāma so hoti māṇavako vā māṇavikā vā.
Tasmā, doṇa, brāhmaṇo na pāyamānaṁ gacchati.
Tassa sā hoti brāhmaṇī neva kāmatthā na davatthā na ratatthā, pajatthāva brāhmaṇassa brāhmaṇī hoti.
So methunaṁ uppādetvā tameva puttassādaṁ nikāmayamāno kuṭumbaṁ ajjhāvasati, na agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajati.
segs.e: Having ensured his progeny through sex, his child makes him happy. Because of this attachment he stays in his family property, and does not go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: Yāva porāṇānaṁ brāhmaṇānaṁ mariyādo tattha tiṭṭhati, taṁ na vītikkamati.
segs.e: As far as the line of the ancient brahmins extends, he doesn’t cross over it.

segs.p: ‘Yāva porāṇānaṁ brāhmaṇānaṁ mariyādo tattha brāhmaṇo ṭhito taṁ na vītikkamatī’ti, kho, doṇa, tasmā brāhmaṇo mariyādoti vuccati.
segs.e: That’s why he’s called a brahmin who toes the line.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, doṇa, brāhmaṇo mariyādo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a brahmin toes the line.
And how does a brahmin cross the line?

segs.p: Idha, doṇa, brāhmaṇo ubhato sujāto hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a brahmin is well born on both the mother’s and the father’s sides …

segs.p: mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena.
So aṭṭhacattālīsavassāni komārabrahmacariyaṁ carati mante adhīyamāno.
Aṭṭhacattālīsavassāni komārabrahmacariyaṁ caritvā mante adhīyitvā ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ pariyesati dhammeneva, no adhammena.
Neva kasiyā na vaṇijjāya na gorakkhena na issatthena na rājaporisena na sippaññatarena, kevalaṁ bhikkhācariyāya kapālaṁ anatimaññamāno.
So ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ niyyādetvā dāraṁ pariyesati dhammenapi adhammenapi kayenapi vikkayenapi brāhmaṇimpi udakūpassaṭṭhaṁ.
segs.e: Having offered a fee for his tutor, he seeks a wife by both legitimate and illegitimate means. That is, by buying or selling, as well as accepting a brahmin woman by the pouring of water.

segs.p: So brāhmaṇimpi gacchati khattiyimpi gacchati vessimpi gacchati suddimpi gacchati caṇḍālimpi gacchati nesādimpi gacchati venimpi gacchati rathakārimpi gacchati pukkusimpi gacchati gabbhinimpi gacchati pāyamānampi gacchati utunimpi gacchati anutunimpi gacchati.
segs.e: He has sex with a brahmin woman, as well as with a woman from a family of aristocrats, peasants, menials, corpse-workers, hunters, bamboo workers, chariot-makers, or scavengers. And he has sex with women who are pregnant, breastfeeding, or outside the fertile phase of the menstrual cycle.

segs.p: Tassa sā hoti brāhmaṇī kāmatthāpi davatthāpi ratatthāpi pajatthāpi brāhmaṇassa brāhmaṇī hoti.
segs.e: His brahmin wife is there for sensual pleasure, fun, and enjoyment, as well as for procreation.

segs.p: Yāva porāṇānaṁ brāhmaṇānaṁ mariyādo tattha na tiṭṭhati, taṁ vītikkamati.
segs.e: As far as the line of the ancient brahmins extends, he crosses over it.

segs.p: ‘Yāva porāṇānaṁ brāhmaṇānaṁ mariyādo tattha brāhmaṇo na ṭhito taṁ vītikkamatī’ti kho, doṇa, tasmā brāhmaṇo sambhinnamariyādoti vuccati.
segs.e: That’s why he’s called a brahmin who crosses the line.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, doṇa, brāhmaṇo sambhinnamariyādo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a brahmin crosses the line.
And how is a brahmin a brahmin corpse-worker?

segs.p: Idha, doṇa, brāhmaṇo ubhato sujāto hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a brahmin is well born on both his mother’s and father’s side, stemming from a clean vessel, with irrefutable and impeccable genealogy back to the seventh paternal generation.

segs.p: mātito ca pitito ca, saṁsuddhagahaṇiko, yāva sattamā pitāmahayugā akkhitto anupakkuṭṭho jātivādena.
So aṭṭhacattālīsavassāni komārabrahmacariyaṁ carati mante adhīyamāno.
segs.e: For forty-eight years he leads the virginal spiritual life studying the hymns.

segs.p: Aṭṭhacattālīsavassāni komārabrahmacariyaṁ caritvā mante adhīyitvā ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ pariyesati dhammenapi adhammenapi
segs.e: Then he seeks a fee for his tutor by legitimate means and illegitimate means.

segs.p: kasiyāpi vaṇijjāyapi gorakkhenapi issatthenapi rājaporisenapi sippaññatarenapi, kevalampi bhikkhācariyāya, kapālaṁ anatimaññamāno.
segs.e: By farming, trade, raising cattle, archery, government service, or one of the professions, not solely by living on alms, not scorning the alms bowl.

segs.p: So ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṁ niyyādetvā dāraṁ pariyesati dhammenapi adhammenapi kayenapi vikkayenapi brāhmaṇimpi udakūpassaṭṭhaṁ.
segs.e: Having offered a fee for his tutor, he seeks a wife by both legitimate and illegitimate means. That is, by buying or selling, as well as accepting a brahmin woman by the pouring of water.

segs.p: So brāhmaṇimpi gacchati khattiyimpi gacchati vessimpi gacchati suddimpi gacchati caṇḍālimpi gacchati nesādimpi gacchati venimpi gacchati rathakārimpi gacchati pukkusimpi gacchati gabbhinimpi gacchati pāyamānampi gacchati utunimpi gacchati anutunimpi gacchati.
segs.e: He has sex with a brahmin woman, as well as with a woman from a family of aristocrats, peasants, menials, corpse-workers, hunters, bamboo workers, chariot-makers, or scavengers. And he has sex with women who are pregnant, breastfeeding, or outside the fertile phase of the menstrual cycle.

segs.p: Tassa sā hoti brāhmaṇī kāmatthāpi davatthāpi ratatthāpi pajatthāpi brāhmaṇassa brāhmaṇī hoti.
segs.e: His brahmin wife is there for sensual pleasure, fun, and enjoyment, as well as for procreation.
He earns a living by any kind of work.
The brahmins say to him,

segs.p: ‘kasmā bhavaṁ brāhmaṇo paṭijānamāno sabbakammehi jīvikaṁ kappetī’ti?
segs.e: ‘Why is it that the worthy sir claims to be a brahmin, but you earn a living by any kind of work?’
He says,

segs.p: ‘seyyathāpi, bho, aggi sucimpi ḍahati asucimpi ḍahati, na ca tena aggi upalippati;
segs.e: ‘It’s like a fire that burns both pure and filthy things, but doesn’t become corrupted by them.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bho, sabbakammehi cepi brāhmaṇo jīvikaṁ kappeti, na ca tena brāhmaṇo upalippati.
segs.e: In the same way, worthy sir, if a brahmin earns a living by any kind of work, he is not corrupted by that.’

segs.p: Sabbakammehi jīvikaṁ kappetī’ti kho, doṇa, tasmā brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇacaṇḍāloti vuccati.
segs.e: A brahmin is called a brahmin corpse-worker because he earns a living by any kind of work.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, doṇa, brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇacaṇḍālo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a brahmin is a brahmin corpse-worker.

segs.p: Ye kho te, doṇa, brāhmaṇānaṁ pubbakā isayo mantānaṁ kattāro mantānaṁ pavattāro yesamidaṁ etarahi brāhmaṇā porāṇaṁ mantapadaṁ gītaṁ pavuttaṁ samīhitaṁ tadanugāyanti tadanubhāsanti bhāsitamanubhāsanti sajjhāyitamanusajjhāyanti vācitamanuvācenti, seyyathidaṁ—aṭṭhako, vāmako, vāmadevo, vessāmitto, yamadaggi, aṅgīraso, bhāradvājo, vāseṭṭho, kassapo, bhagu;
segs.e: Doṇa, the ancient brahmin seers were Aṭṭhaka, Vāmaka, Vāmadeva, Vessāmitta, Yamadaggi, Aṅgīrasa, Bhāradvāja, Vāseṭṭha, Kassapa, and Bhagu. They were the authors and propagators of the hymns, whose hymnal was sung and propagated and compiled in ancient times. These days, brahmins continue to sing and chant it. They continue chanting what was chanted, rehearsing what was rehearsed, and teaching what was taught.
Those seers described five kinds of brahmins.

segs.p: brahmasamaṁ, devasamaṁ, mariyādaṁ, sambhinnamariyādaṁ, brāhmaṇacaṇḍālaṁyeva pañcamaṁ.
segs.e: A brahmin who is equal to the Divinity, one who is equal to a god, one who toes the line, one who crosses the line, and the fifth is a brahmin corpse-worker.
Which one of these are you, Doṇa?”

segs.p: Evaṁ sante mayaṁ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇacaṇḍālampi na pūrema.
segs.e: “This being so, worthy Gotama, I don’t even qualify as a brahmin corpse-worker.

segs.p: Abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama …pe… upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: Excellent, worthy Gotama! … From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Numbered Discourses 5.193
20. Brahmins
With Saṅgārava

segs.p: Atha kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Saṅgārava the brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, Saṅgārava sat down to one side, and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo, yena kadāci dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā?
segs.e: “What is the cause, Worthy Gotama, what is the reason why sometimes even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed?

segs.p: Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo, yena kadāci dīgharattaṁ asajjhāyakatāpi mantā paṭibhanti, pageva sajjhāyakatā”ti?
segs.e: And why is it that sometimes even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed?”

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, brāhmaṇa, samaye kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, paratthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: “Brahmin, there’s a time when your heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire and you don’t truly understand the escape from sensual desire that has arisen. At that time you don’t truly know or see what is good for yourself, good for another, or good for both. Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto saṁsaṭṭho lākhāya vā haliddiyā vā nīliyā vā mañjiṭṭhāya vā.
segs.e: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was mixed with dye such as red lac, turmeric, indigo, or rose madder.

segs.p: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ nappajāneyya na passeyya.
segs.e: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in sensual desire … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati byāpādaparetena, uppannassa ca byāpādassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in ill will … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto agginā santatto ukkudhito ussadakajāto.
segs.e: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was heated by fire, boiling and bubbling.

segs.p: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ nappajāneyya na passeyya.
segs.e: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati byāpādaparetena, uppannassa ca byāpādassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in ill will … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
