segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati thinamiddhaparetena, uppannassa ca thinamiddhassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in dullness and drowsiness … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.
Suppose there was a bowl of water overgrown with moss and aquatic plants.

segs.p: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ nappajāneyya na passeyya.
segs.e: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati thinamiddhaparetena, uppannassa ca thinamiddhassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in dullness and drowsiness … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati uddhaccakukkuccaparetena, uppannassa ca uddhaccakukkuccassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in restlessness and remorse … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto vāterito calito bhanto ūmijāto.
segs.e: Suppose there was a bowl of water stirred by the wind, quivering, swirling, and rippling.

segs.p: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ nappajāneyya na passeyya.
segs.e: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati uddhaccakukkuccaparetena, uppannassa ca uddhaccakukkuccassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: In the same way, when your heart is overcome and mired in restlessness and remorse … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati vicikicchāparetena, uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: Furthermore, when your heart is overcome and mired in doubt … Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto āvilo luḷito kalalībhūto andhakāre nikkhitto.
segs.e: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was cloudy, murky, and muddy, hidden in the darkness.

segs.p: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ nappajāneyya na passeyya.
segs.e: Even a person with clear eyes checking their own reflection wouldn’t truly know it or see it.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati vicikicchāparetena, uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti na passati, dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: In the same way, there’s a time when your heart is overcome and mired in doubt and you don’t truly understand the escape from doubt that has arisen. At that time you don’t truly know or see what is good for yourself, good for another, or good for both. Even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

segs.p: Yasmiñca kho, brāhmaṇa, samaye na kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti passati, paratthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti passati, ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti passati, dīgharattaṁ asajjhāyakatāpi mantā paṭibhanti, pageva sajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: There’s a time when your heart is not overcome and mired in sensual desire and you truly understand the escape from sensual desire that has arisen. At that time you truly know and see what is good for yourself, good for another, and good for both. Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto asaṁsaṭṭho lākhāya vā haliddiyā vā nīliyā vā mañjiṭṭhāya vā.
segs.e: Suppose there was a bowl of water that was not mixed with dye such as red lac, turmeric, indigo, or rose madder.

segs.p: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ pajāneyya passeyya.
segs.e: A person with clear eyes checking their own reflection would truly know it and see it.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye na kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati …pe….
segs.e: In the same way, when your heart is not overcome and mired in sensual desire … Even hymns that are long-unpracticed spring to mind, let alone those that are practiced.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye na byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, when your heart is not overcome and mired in ill will … Even hymns that are long-unpracticed spring to mind, let alone those that are practiced.

segs.p: seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto agginā asantatto anukkudhito anussadakajāto.
segs.e: Suppose there was a bowl of water that’s not heated by a fire, boiling and bubbling.

segs.p: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ pajāneyya passeyya.
segs.e: A person with clear eyes checking their own reflection would truly know it and see it.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye na byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati …pe….
segs.e: In the same way, when your heart is not overcome and mired in ill will … Even hymns that are long-unpracticed spring to mind, let alone those that are practiced.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye na thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, when your heart is not overcome and mired in dullness and drowsiness … Even hymns that are long-unpracticed spring to mind, let alone those that are practiced.
Suppose there was a bowl of water that’s not overgrown with moss and aquatic plants.

segs.p: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ pajāneyya passeyya.
segs.e: A person with clear eyes checking their own reflection would truly know it and see it.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye na thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati …pe….
segs.e: In the same way, when your heart is not overcome and mired in dullness and drowsiness … Even hymns that are long-unpracticed spring to mind, let alone those that are practiced.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye na uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, when your heart is not overcome and mired in restlessness and remorse … Even hymns that are long-unpracticed spring to mind, let alone those that are practiced.

segs.p: seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto na vāterito na calito na bhanto na ūmijāto.
segs.e: Suppose there was a bowl of water that’s not stirred by the wind, quivering, swirling, and rippling.

segs.p: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ pajāneyya passeyya.
segs.e: A person with clear eyes checking their own reflection would truly know it and see it.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye na uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati …pe….
segs.e: In the same way, when your heart is not overcome and mired in restlessness and remorse … Even hymns that are long-unpracticed spring to mind, let alone those that are practiced.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye na vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na vicikicchāparetena, uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti passati, paratthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti passati, ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti passati, dīgharattaṁ asajjhāyakatāpi mantā paṭibhanti, pageva sajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: Furthermore, when your heart is not overcome and mired in doubt … Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto accho vippasanno anāvilo āloke nikkhitto.
segs.e: Suppose there was a bowl of water that’s transparent, clear, and unclouded, brought into the light.

segs.p: Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṁ pajāneyya passeyya.
segs.e: A person with clear eyes checking their own reflection would truly know it and see it.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṁ samaye na vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati na vicikicchāparetena, uppannāya ca vicikicchāya nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti passati, paratthampi …pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti passati, dīgharattaṁ asajjhāyakatāpi mantā paṭibhanti, pageva sajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: In the same way, there’s a time when your heart is not overcome and mired in doubt and you truly understand the escape from doubt that has arisen. At that time you truly know and see what is good for yourself, good for another, and good for both. Even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena kadāci dīgharattaṁ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.
segs.e: This is the cause, brahmin, this is the reason why sometimes even hymns that are long-rehearsed don’t spring to mind, let alone those that are not rehearsed.

segs.p: Ayaṁ pana, brāhmaṇa, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena kadāci dīgharattaṁ asajjhāyakatāpi mantā paṭibhanti, pageva sajjhāyakatā”ti.
segs.e: And this is why sometimes even hymns that are long-unrehearsed spring to mind, let alone those that are rehearsed.”

segs.p: “Abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama …pe… upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: “Excellent, worthy Gotama! … From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Numbered Discourses 5.194
20. Brahmins
With Kāraṇapālī

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena kāraṇapālī brāhmaṇo licchavīnaṁ kammantaṁ kāreti.
segs.e: Now at that time the brahmin Kāraṇapālī was working for the Licchavis.

segs.p: Addasā kho kāraṇapālī brāhmaṇo piṅgiyāniṁ brāhmaṇaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ;
segs.e: He saw the brahmin Piṅgiyānī coming off in the distance
and said to him,

segs.p: “Handa kuto nu bhavaṁ piṅgiyānī āgacchati divā divassā”ti?
segs.e: “So, Piṅgiyānī, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?”
“I’m coming, worthy sir, from the presence of the ascetic Gotama.”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññati bhavaṁ piṅgiyānī samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṁ? Paṇḍito maññe”ti?
segs.e: “What do you think of the ascetic Gotama’s lucidity of wisdom? Do you think he’s astute?”

segs.p: “Ko cāhaṁ, bho, ko ca samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṁ jānissāmi.
segs.e: Worthy sir, who am I to judge the ascetic Gotama’s lucidity of wisdom?

segs.p: Sopi nūnassa tādisova yo samaṇassa gotamassa paññāveyyattiyaṁ jāneyyā”ti.
segs.e: You’d really have to be on the same level to judge his lucidity of wisdom.”

segs.p: “Uḷārāya khalu bhavaṁ piṅgiyānī samaṇaṁ gotamaṁ pasaṁsāya pasaṁsatī”ti.
segs.e: Worthy Piṅgiyānī praises the ascetic Gotama with high praise indeed.”

segs.p: “Ko cāhaṁ, bho, ko ca samaṇaṁ gotamaṁ pasaṁsissāmi.
segs.e: “Who am I to praise the ascetic Gotama?

segs.p: Pasatthappasatthova so bhavaṁ gotamo seṭṭho devamanussānan”ti.
segs.e: He is praised by the praised as the first among gods and humans.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ pana bhavaṁ piṅgiyānī atthavasaṁ sampassamāno samaṇe gotame evaṁ abhippasanno”ti?
segs.e: “But for what reason are you so devoted to the ascetic Gotama?”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bho, puriso aggarasaparititto na aññesaṁ hīnānaṁ rasānaṁ piheti;
segs.e: “Suppose a person was completely satisfied by the best tasting food. They wouldn’t be attracted to anything that tasted inferior.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bho, yato yato tassa bhoto gotamassa dhammaṁ suṇāti—
segs.e: In the same way, when you hear the worthy Gotama’s teaching—

segs.p: yadi suttaso, yadi geyyaso, yadi veyyākaraṇaso, yadi abbhutadhammaso—
segs.e: whatever it may be, whether statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, or amazing stories—

segs.p: tato tato na aññesaṁ puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇappavādānaṁ piheti.
segs.e: then you’re not attracted to the doctrines of the various ascetics and brahmins.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho, puriso jighacchādubbalyapareto madhupiṇḍikaṁ adhigaccheyya.
segs.e: Suppose a person who was weak with hunger was to obtain a honey-cake.

segs.p: So yato yato sāyetha, labhateva sādurasaṁ asecanakaṁ;
segs.e: Wherever they taste it, they would enjoy a sweet, delectable flavor.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bho, yato yato tassa bhoto gotamassa dhammaṁ suṇāti—
segs.e: In the same way, when you hear the worthy Gotama’s teaching—

segs.p: yadi suttaso, yadi geyyaso, yadi veyyākaraṇaso, yadi abbhutadhammaso—
segs.e: whatever it may be, whether statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, or amazing stories—

segs.p: tato tato labhateva attamanataṁ, labhati cetaso pasādaṁ.
segs.e: then you get a sense of uplift, a confidence of the heart.
Suppose a person were to obtain a piece of sandalwood,
whether yellow or red.
Wherever they smelled it—

segs.p: yadi mūlato, yadi majjhato, yadi aggato—
segs.e: whether at the root, the middle, or the top—
they’d enjoy a delectable fragrance.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bho, yato yato tassa bhoto gotamassa dhammaṁ suṇāti—
segs.e: In the same way, when you hear the worthy Gotama’s teaching—

segs.p: yadi suttaso, yadi geyyaso, yadi veyyākaraṇaso, yadi abbhutadhammaso—
segs.e: whatever it may be, whether statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, or amazing stories—

segs.p: tato tato adhigacchati pāmojjaṁ adhigacchati somanassaṁ.
segs.e: then you become filled with joy and happiness.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho, puriso ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: Suppose there was a person who was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Tassa kusalo bhisakko ṭhānaso ābādhaṁ nīhareyya;
segs.e: A good doctor would cure them on the spot.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bho, yato yato tassa bhoto gotamassa dhammaṁ suṇāti—
segs.e: In the same way, when you hear the worthy Gotama’s teaching—

segs.p: yadi suttaso, yadi geyyaso, yadi veyyākaraṇaso, yadi abbhutadhammaso—
segs.e: whatever it may be, whether statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, or amazing stories—
then you make an end of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho, pokkharaṇī acchodakā sātodakā sītodakā setakā supatitthā ramaṇīyā.
segs.e: Suppose there was a lotus pond with clear, sweet, cool water, clean, with smooth banks, delightful.

segs.p: Atha puriso āgaccheyya ghammābhitatto ghammapareto kilanto tasito pipāsito.
segs.e: Then along comes a person struggling in the oppressive heat, weary, thirsty, and parched.

segs.p: So taṁ pokkharaṇiṁ ogāhetvā nhātvā ca pivitvā ca sabbadarathakilamathapariḷāhaṁ paṭippassambheyya.
segs.e: They’d plunge into the lotus pond to bathe and drink. And all their stress, weariness, and heat exhaustion would die down.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bho, yato yato tassa bhoto gotamassa dhammaṁ suṇāti—
segs.e: In the same way, when you hear the worthy Gotama’s teaching—

segs.p: yadi suttaso, yadi geyyaso, yadi veyyākaraṇaso, yadi abbhutadhammaso—
segs.e: whatever it may be, whether statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, or amazing stories—
then all your stress, weariness, and exhaustion die down.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, kāraṇapālī brāhmaṇo uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā dakkhiṇaṁ jāṇumaṇḍalaṁ pathaviyaṁ nihantvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṁ paṇāmetvā tikkhattuṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
segs.e: When this was said, the brahmin Kāraṇapālī rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, knelt on his right knee, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and expressed this heartfelt sentiment three times:
“Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!
Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!
Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!

segs.p: Abhikkantaṁ, bho piṅgiyāni, abhikkantaṁ, bho piṅgiyāni.
segs.e: Excellent, worthy Piṅgiyānī! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho piṅgiyāni, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhotā piṅgiyāninā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, the worthy Piṅgiyānī has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bho piṅgiyāni, taṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ piṅgiyānī dhāretu, ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Piṅgiyānī remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Numbered Discourses 5.195
20. Brahmins
Piṅgiyānī

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena pañcamattāni licchavisatāni bhagavantaṁ payirupāsanti.
segs.e: Now at that time around five hundred Licchavis were visiting the Buddha.

segs.p: Appekacce licchavī nīlā honti nīlavaṇṇā nīlavatthā nīlālaṅkārā, appekacce licchavī pītā honti pītavaṇṇā pītavatthā pītālaṅkārā, appekacce licchavī lohitakā honti lohitakavaṇṇā lohitakavatthā lohitakālaṅkārā, appekacce licchavī odātā honti odātavaṇṇā odātavatthā odātālaṅkārā.
segs.e: Some of the Licchavis were in blue, of blue color, clad in blue, adorned with blue. And some were similarly colored in yellow, red, or white.

segs.p: Tyassudaṁ bhagavā atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca.
segs.e: But the Buddha outshone them all in beauty and glory.

segs.p: Atha kho piṅgiyānī brāhmaṇo uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṁ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the brahmin Piṅgīyānī rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and said,
“I feel inspired to speak, Blessed One! I feel inspired to speak, Holy One!”
“Then speak as you feel inspired,” said the Buddha.

segs.p: Atha kho piṅgiyānī brāhmaṇo bhagavato sammukhā sāruppāya gāthāya abhitthavi:
segs.e: So the brahmin Piṅgīyānī extolled the Buddha in his presence with a fitting verse.
“Like a fragrant pink lotus
that blooms at daybreak, its fragrance unfaded—
see Aṅgīrasa dazzle,
bright as the sun in the sky!”

segs.p: Atha kho te licchavī pañcahi uttarāsaṅgasatehi piṅgiyāniṁ brāhmaṇaṁ acchādesuṁ.
segs.e: Then those Licchavis clothed Piṅgiyānī with five hundred upper robes.

segs.p: Atha kho piṅgiyānī brāhmaṇo tehi pañcahi uttarāsaṅgasatehi bhagavantaṁ acchādesi.
segs.e: And Piṅgiyānī clothed the Buddha with them.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā te licchavī etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to the Licchavis:
“Licchavis, the appearance of five treasures is rare in the world.
What five?

segs.p: Tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: A Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Tathāgatappaveditassa dhammavinayassa desetā puggalo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: A teacher of the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One.

segs.p: Tathāgatappaveditassa dhammavinayassa desitassa viññātā puggalo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: An individual who understands the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One.

segs.p: Tathāgatappaveditassa dhammavinayassa desitassa viññātā dhammānudhammappaṭipanno puggalo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: An individual who practices in line with the teaching.
An individual who is grateful and thankful.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, licchavī, pañcannaṁ ratanānaṁ pātubhāvo dullabho lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: The appearance of these five treasures is rare in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 5.196
20. Brahmins
The Great Dreams

segs.p: “Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato pañca mahāsupinā pāturahesuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, before his awakening five great dreams appeared to the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, when he was still not awake but intent on awakening.
What five?

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato ayaṁ mahāpathavī mahāsayanaṁ ahosi, himavā pabbatarājā bibbohanaṁ ahosi, puratthime samudde vāmo hattho ohito ahosi, pacchime samudde dakkhiṇo hattho ohito ahosi, dakkhiṇe samudde ubho pādā ohitā ahesuṁ.
segs.e: This great earth was his bed. Himalaya, king of mountains, was his pillow. His left hand was laid down in the eastern sea. His right hand was laid down in the western sea. And both his feet were laid down in the southern sea.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato ayaṁ paṭhamo mahāsupino pāturahosi.
segs.e: This is the first great dream that appeared to the Realized One before his awakening.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato tiriyā nāma tiṇajāti nābhiyā uggantvā nabhaṁ āhacca ṭhitā ahosi.
segs.e: Next, a kind of grass called ‘the crosser’ grew up from his navel and stood pressing against the cloudy sky.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato ayaṁ dutiyo mahāsupino pāturahosi.
segs.e: This is the second great dream that appeared to the Realized One before his awakening.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato setā kimī kaṇhasīsā pādehi ussakkitvā (…) yāva jāṇumaṇḍalā paṭicchādesuṁ.
segs.e: Next, white caterpillars with black heads crawled up from his feet and covered his knees.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato ayaṁ tatiyo mahāsupino pāturahosi.
segs.e: This is the third great dream that appeared to the Realized One before his awakening.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato cattāro sakuṇā nānāvaṇṇā catūhi disāhi āgantvā pādamūle nipatitvā sabbasetā sampajjiṁsu.
segs.e: Next, four birds of different colors came from the four quarters. They fell at his feet, turning pure white.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato ayaṁ catuttho mahāsupino pāturahosi.
segs.e: This is the fourth great dream that appeared to the Realized One before his awakening.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddho bodhisattova samāno mahato mīḷhapabbatassa uparūpari caṅkamati alippamāno mīḷhena.
segs.e: Next, he walked back and forth on top of a big mountain of filth while remaining unsoiled.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato ayaṁ pañcamo mahāsupino pāturahosi.
segs.e: This is the fifth great dream that appeared to the Realized One before his awakening.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato ayaṁ mahāpathavī mahāsayanaṁ ahosi, himavā pabbatarājā bibbohanaṁ ahosi, puratthime samudde vāmo hattho ohito ahosi, pacchime samudde dakkhiṇo hattho ohito ahosi, dakkhiṇe samudde ubho pādā ohitā ahesuṁ;
segs.e: Now, as to when, before his awakening, the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha was still not awake but intent on awakening. This great earth was his bed. Himalaya, king of mountains, was his pillow. His left hand was laid down in the eastern sea. His right hand was laid down in the western sea. And both his feet were laid down in the southern sea.

segs.p: tathāgatena, bhikkhave, arahatā sammāsambuddhena anuttarā sammāsambodhi abhisambuddhā.
segs.e: This was fulfilled when the Buddha awakened to the perfect awakening.

segs.p: Tassā abhisambodhāya ayaṁ paṭhamo mahāsupino pāturahosi.
segs.e: This was the first great dream that appeared to him while he was still not awakened.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato tiriyā nāma tiṇajāti nābhiyā uggantvā nabhaṁ āhacca ṭhitā ahosi;
segs.e: As to when a kind of grass called ‘the crosser’ grew up from his navel and stood pressing against the cloudy sky.

segs.p: tathāgatena, bhikkhave, arahatā sammāsambuddhena ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo abhisambujjhitvā yāva devamanussehi suppakāsito.
segs.e: This was fulfilled when, after the Buddha had awakened to the noble eightfold path, it was fully revealed among gods and humans.

segs.p: Tassa abhisambodhāya ayaṁ dutiyo mahāsupino pāturahosi.
segs.e: This was the second great dream that appeared to him while he was still not awakened.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato setā kimī kaṇhasīsā pādehi ussakkitvā yāva jāṇumaṇḍalā paṭicchādesuṁ;
segs.e: As to when white caterpillars with black heads crawled up from his feet and covered his knees.

segs.p: bahū, bhikkhave, gihī odātavasanā tathāgataṁ pāṇupetā saraṇaṁ gatā.
segs.e: This was fulfilled when many white-clothed laypeople went for refuge to him for life.

segs.p: Tassa abhisambodhāya ayaṁ tatiyo mahāsupino pāturahosi.
segs.e: This was the third great dream that appeared to him while he was still not awakened.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato cattāro sakuṇā nānāvaṇṇā catūhi disāhi āgantvā pādamūle nipatitvā sabbasetā sampajjiṁsu;
segs.e: As to when four birds of different colors came from the four quarters. They fell at his feet, turning pure white.

segs.p: cattārome, bhikkhave, vaṇṇā khattiyā brāhmaṇā vessā suddā te tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitvā anuttaraṁ vimuttiṁ sacchikaronti.
segs.e: This was fulfilled when members of the four classes—aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, and menials—went forth from the lay life to homelessness in the teaching and training proclaimed by the Realized One and realized supreme freedom.

segs.p: Tassa abhisambodhāya ayaṁ catuttho mahāsupino pāturahosi.
segs.e: This was the fourth great dream that appeared to him while he was still not awakened.

segs.p: Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddho bodhisattova samāno mahato mīḷhapabbatassa uparūpari caṅkamati alippamāno mīḷhena;
segs.e: As to when he walked back and forth on top of a big mountain of filth while remaining unsoiled.

segs.p: lābhī, bhikkhave, tathāgato cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ, taṁ tathāgato agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.
segs.e: This was fulfilled when the Realized One received robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. And he used them untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawbacks, and understanding the escape.

segs.p: Tassa abhisambodhāya ayaṁ pañcamo mahāsupino pāturahosi.
segs.e: This was the fifth great dream that appeared to him while he was still not awakened.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pubbeva sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato ime pañca mahāsupinā pāturahesun”ti.
segs.e: Before his awakening these five great dreams appeared to the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, when he was still not awake but intent on awakening.”
Numbered Discourses 5.197
20. Brahmins
Obstacles to Rain

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, vassassa antarāyā, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five obstacles to rain, which the forecasters don’t know, and which their vision does not traverse.
What five?
In the upper atmosphere the fire element flares up,
which disperses the clouds.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo vassassa antarāyo, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
segs.e: This is the first obstacle to rain, which the forecasters don’t know, and which their vision does not traverse.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, upari ākāse vāyodhātu pakuppati.
segs.e: Furthermore, in the upper atmosphere the air element flares up,
which disperses the clouds.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo vassassa antarāyo, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
segs.e: This is the second obstacle to rain …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, rāhu asurindo pāṇinā udakaṁ sampaṭicchitvā mahāsamudde chaḍḍeti.
segs.e: Furthermore, Rāhu, lord of titans, receives water in his hand and discards it in the ocean.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo vassassa antarāyo, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
segs.e: This is the third obstacle to rain …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, vassavalāhakā devā pamattā honti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the gods of the rain clouds become negligent.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho vassassa antarāyo, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
segs.e: This is the fourth obstacle to rain …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, manussā adhammikā honti.
segs.e: Furthermore, humans become unprincipled.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo vassassa antarāyo, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamati.
segs.e: This is the fifth obstacle to rain, which the forecasters don’t know, and which their vision does not traverse.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca vassassa antarāyā, yaṁ nemittā na jānanti, yattha nemittānaṁ cakkhu na kamatī”ti.
segs.e: These are the five obstacles to rain, which the forecasters don’t know, and which their vision does not traverse.”
Numbered Discourses 5.198
20. Brahmins
Well-Spoken Words

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatā vācā subhāsitā hoti, no dubbhāsitā, anavajjā ca ananuvajjā ca viññūnaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, speech that has five factors is well spoken, not poorly spoken. It’s blameless and is not criticized by sensible people.
What five?

segs.p: Kālena ca bhāsitā hoti, saccā ca bhāsitā hoti, saṇhā ca bhāsitā hoti, atthasaṁhitā ca bhāsitā hoti, mettacittena ca bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: It is speech that is timely, true, gentle, beneficial, and loving.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi aṅgehi samannāgatā vācā subhāsitā hoti, no dubbhāsitā, anavajjā ca ananuvajjā ca viññūnan”ti.
segs.e: Speech with these five factors is well spoken, not poorly spoken. It’s blameless and is not criticized by sensible people.”
Numbered Discourses 5.199
20. Brahmins
Families

segs.p: “Yaṁ, bhikkhave, sīlavanto pabbajitā kulaṁ upasaṅkamanti, tattha manussā pañcahi ṭhānehi bahuṁ puññaṁ pasavanti.
segs.e: “When ethical renunciates come to a family, the people brim with much merit for five reasons.
What five?

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye sīlavante pabbajite kulaṁ upasaṅkamante manussā disvā cittāni pasādenti, saggasaṁvattanikaṁ, bhikkhave, taṁ kulaṁ tasmiṁ samaye paṭipadaṁ paṭipannaṁ hoti.
segs.e: When they see ethical renunciates coming to their family, the people bring up confidence in their hearts. At that time the family is practicing a path leading to heaven.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye sīlavante pabbajite kulaṁ upasaṅkamante manussā paccuṭṭhenti abhivādenti āsanaṁ denti, uccākulīnasaṁvattanikaṁ, bhikkhave, taṁ kulaṁ tasmiṁ samaye paṭipadaṁ paṭipannaṁ hoti.
segs.e: When ethical renunciates come to their family, the people rise from their seats, bow down, and offer them a seat. At that time the family is practicing a path leading to a birth in an eminent family.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye sīlavante pabbajite kulaṁ upasaṅkamante manussā maccheramalaṁ paṭivinenti, mahesakkhasaṁvattanikaṁ, bhikkhave, taṁ kulaṁ tasmiṁ samaye paṭipadaṁ paṭipannaṁ hoti.
segs.e: When ethical renunciates come to their family, the people get rid of the stain of stinginess. At that time the family is practicing a path leading to being illustrious.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye sīlavante pabbajite kulaṁ upasaṅkamante manussā yathāsatti yathābalaṁ saṁvibhajanti, mahābhogasaṁvattanikaṁ, bhikkhave, taṁ kulaṁ tasmiṁ samaye paṭipadaṁ paṭipannaṁ hoti.
segs.e: When ethical renunciates come to their family, the people share what they have as best they can. At that time the family is practicing a path leading to great wealth.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye sīlavante pabbajite kulaṁ upasaṅkamante manussā paripucchanti paripañhanti dhammaṁ suṇanti, mahāpaññāsaṁvattanikaṁ, bhikkhave, taṁ kulaṁ tasmiṁ samaye paṭipadaṁ paṭipannaṁ hoti.
segs.e: When ethical renunciates come to their family, the people ask questions and listen to the teachings. At that time the family is practicing a path leading to great wisdom.

segs.p: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, sīlavanto pabbajitā kulaṁ upasaṅkamanti, tattha manussā imehi pañcahi ṭhānehi bahuṁ puññaṁ pasavantī”ti.
segs.e: When ethical renunciates come to a family, the people brim with much merit for these five reasons.”
Numbered Discourses 5.200
20. Brahmins
Elements of Escape
“Mendicants, there are these five elements of escape.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kāmaṁ manasikaroto kāmesu cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
segs.e: Take a case where a mendicant focuses on sensual pleasures, but on that their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

segs.p: Nekkhammaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto nekkhamme cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
segs.e: But when they focus on renunciation, on that their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ suvisaṁyuttaṁ kāmehi;
segs.e: Their mind is in a good state, well developed, well risen, well freed, and well detached from sensual pleasures.

segs.p: ye ca kāmapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vediyati.
segs.e: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of sensual pleasures, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.
This is how the escape from sensual pleasures is explained.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno byāpādaṁ manasikaroto byāpāde cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
segs.e: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on ill will, but their mind does not leap forth …

segs.p: Abyāpādaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto abyāpāde cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
segs.e: But when they focus on good will, their mind leaps forth …

segs.p: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ suvisaṁyuttaṁ byāpādena;
segs.e: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from ill will.

segs.p: ye ca byāpādapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vediyati.
segs.e: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of ill will, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.
This is how the escape from ill will is explained.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno vihesaṁ manasikaroto vihesāya cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
segs.e: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on harming, but their mind does not leap forth …

segs.p: Avihesaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto avihesāya cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
segs.e: But when they focus on compassion, their mind leaps forth …

segs.p: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ suvisaṁyuttaṁ vihesāya;
segs.e: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from harming.

segs.p: ye ca vihesāpaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vediyati.
segs.e: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of harming, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.
This is how the escape from harming is explained.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rūpaṁ manasikaroto rūpe cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
segs.e: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on form, but their mind does not leap forth …

segs.p: Arūpaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto arūpe cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
segs.e: But when they focus on the formless, their mind leaps forth …

segs.p: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ suvisaṁyuttaṁ rūpehi;
segs.e: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from forms.

segs.p: ye ca rūpapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vediyati.
segs.e: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of form, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.
This is how the escape from forms is explained.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sakkāyaṁ manasikaroto sakkāye cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
segs.e: Take a case where a mendicant focuses on substantial reality, but their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

segs.p: Sakkāyanirodhaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto sakkāyanirodhe cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
segs.e: But when they focus on the cessation of substantial reality, their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ suvisaṁyuttaṁ sakkāyena;
segs.e: Their mind is in a good state, well developed, well risen, well freed, and well detached from substantial reality.

segs.p: ye ca sakkāyapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vediyati.
segs.e: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of substantial reality, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.
This is how the escape from substantial reality is explained.

segs.p: Tassa kāmanandīpi nānuseti, byāpādanandīpi nānuseti, vihesānandīpi nānuseti, rūpanandīpi nānuseti, sakkāyanandīpi nānuseti so kāmanandiyāpi ananusayā, byāpādanandiyāpi ananusayā, vihesānandiyāpi ananusayā, rūpanandiyāpi ananusayā, sakkāyanandiyāpi ananusayā.
segs.e: Delight in sensual pleasures, ill will, harming, form, and substantial reality don’t linger within them.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu niranusayo, acchecchi taṇhaṁ, vivattayi saṁyojanaṁ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassa.
segs.e: That’s why they’re called a mendicant who is without underlying tendencies, who has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.

segs.p: Imā kho, bhikkhave, pañca nissāraṇīyā dhātuyo”ti.
segs.e: These are the five elements of escape.”
Numbered Discourses 5.201
21. With Kimbila
With Kimbila

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kimilāyaṁ viharati veḷuvane.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kimbilā in the Freshwater Mangrove Wood.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā kimilo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā kimilo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Kimbila went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo na ciraṭṭhitiko hotī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why the true teaching does not last long after the final quenching of the Realized One?”

segs.p: “Idha, kimila, tathāgate parinibbute bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo satthari agāravā viharanti appatissā, dhamme agāravā viharanti appatissā, saṅghe agāravā viharanti appatissā, sikkhāya agāravā viharanti appatissā, aññamaññaṁ agāravā viharanti appatissā.
segs.e: “Kimbila, it’s when the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen lack respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the training, and each other after the final quenching of the Realized One.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, kimila, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo na ciraṭṭhitiko hotī”ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why the true teaching does not last long after the final quenching of the Realized One.”

segs.p: “Ko pana, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo ciraṭṭhitiko hotī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why the true teaching does last long after the final quenching of the Realized One?”

segs.p: “Idha, kimila, tathāgate parinibbute bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo satthari sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, dhamme sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, saṅghe sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, sikkhāya sagāravā viharanti sappatissā, aññamaññaṁ sagāravā viharanti sappatissā.
segs.e: “Kimbila, it’s when the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen maintain respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the training, and each other after the final quenching of the Realized One.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, kimila, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo ciraṭṭhitiko hotī”ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why the true teaching does last long after the final quenching of the Realized One.”
Numbered Discourses 5.202
21. With Kimbila
Listening to the Teaching
“Mendicants, there are these five benefits of listening to the teaching.
What five?

segs.p: Assutaṁ suṇāti, sutaṁ pariyodāpeti, kaṅkhaṁ vitarati, diṭṭhiṁ ujuṁ karoti, cittamassa pasīdati.
segs.e: You learn new things, clarify what you’ve learned, get over uncertainty, correct your views, and inspire confidence in your mind.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā dhammassavane”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of listening to the teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 5.203
21. With Kimbila
A Thoroughbred

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño bhadro assājānīyo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅgantveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a fine royal thoroughbred with five factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.
What five?
Integrity, speed, tenderness, patience, and gentleness.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño bhadro assājānīyo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅgantveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: A fine royal thoroughbred with these five factors is worthy of a king. …

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with five qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What five?
Integrity, speed, tenderness, patience, and gentleness.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these five qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 5.204
21. With Kimbila
Powers
“Mendicants, there are these five powers.
What five?
Faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.
These are the five powers.”
Numbered Discourses 5.205
21. With Kimbila
Hard-heartedness
“Mendicants, there are these five kinds of hard-heartedness.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant has doubts about the Teacher. They’re uncertain, undecided, and lacking confidence.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
segs.e: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

segs.p: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ paṭhamo cetokhilo.
segs.e: This is the first kind of hard-heartedness.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhamme kaṅkhati …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant has doubts about the teaching …
the Saṅgha …
the training …

segs.p: sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto.
segs.e: A mendicant is angry and upset with their spiritual companions, resentful and closed off.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
segs.e: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

segs.p: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ pañcamo cetokhilo.
segs.e: This is the fifth kind of hard-heartedness.
These are the five kinds of hard-heartedness.”
Numbered Discourses 5.206
21. With Kimbila
Shackles
“Mendicants, there are these five shackles of the heart.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāmesu avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant isn’t free of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāmesu avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
segs.e: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

segs.p: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ paṭhamo cetasovinibandho.
segs.e: This is the first shackle of the heart.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye avītarāgo hoti …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, a mendicant isn’t free of greed for the body …
They’re not free of greed for form …

segs.p: yāvadatthaṁ udarāvadehakaṁ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṁ passasukhaṁ middhasukhaṁ anuyutto viharati …pe…
segs.e: They eat as much as they like until their belly is full, then indulge in the pleasures of sleeping, lying down, and drowsing …

segs.p: aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṁ carati: ‘imināhaṁ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti.
segs.e: They lead the spiritual life hoping to be reborn in one of the orders of gods, thinking: ‘By this precept or observance or fervent austerity or spiritual practice, may I become one of the gods!’

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṁ carati: ‘imināhaṁ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
segs.e: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

segs.p: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ pañcamo cetasovinibandho.
segs.e: This is the fifth shackle of the heart.
These are the five shackles of the heart.”
Numbered Discourses 5.207
21. With Kimbila
Porridge
“Mendicants, there are these five benefits of porridge.
What five?

segs.p: Khuddaṁ paṭihanati, pipāsaṁ paṭivineti, vātaṁ anulometi, vatthiṁ sodheti, āmāvasesaṁ pāceti.
segs.e: It wards off hunger, quenches thirst, settles the wind, cleans the bladder, and helps digestion.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā yāguyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of porridge.”
Numbered Discourses 5.208
21. With Kimbila
Chew Sticks
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of not using chew sticks.
What five?

segs.p: Acakkhussaṁ, mukhaṁ duggandhaṁ hoti, rasaharaṇiyo na visujjhanti, pittaṁ semhaṁ bhattaṁ pariyonandhati, bhattamassa nacchādeti.
segs.e: It’s not good for your eyes, you get bad breath, your taste-buds aren’t cleaned, bile and phlegm cover your food, and you lose your appetite.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā dantakaṭṭhassa akhādane.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of not using chew sticks.
There are these five benefits of using chew sticks.
What five?

segs.p: Cakkhussaṁ, mukhaṁ na duggandhaṁ hoti, rasaharaṇiyo visujjhanti, pittaṁ semhaṁ bhattaṁ na pariyonandhati, bhattamassa chādeti.
segs.e: It’s good for your eyes, you don’t get bad breath, your taste-buds are cleaned, bile and phlegm don’t cover your food, and food agrees with you.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā dantakaṭṭhassa khādane”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of using chew sticks.”
Numbered Discourses 5.209
21. With Kimbila
The Sound of Singing

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, ādīnavā āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṁ bhaṇantassa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks in reciting with a drawn-out singing voice.
What five?

segs.p: Attanāpi tasmiṁ sare sārajjati, parepi tasmiṁ sare sārajjanti, gahapatikāpi ujjhāyanti:
segs.e: You relish the sound of your own voice. Others relish the sound of your voice. Householders complain:

segs.p: ‘yatheva mayaṁ gāyāma, evamevaṁ kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā gāyantī’ti, sarakuttimpi nikāmayamānassa samādhissa bhaṅgo hoti, pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: ‘These ascetics who follow the Sakyan, sing just like us!’ When you’re enjoying the melody, your immersion breaks up. Those who come after follow your example.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā āyatakena gītassarena dhammaṁ bhaṇantassā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks in reciting with a drawn-out singing voice.”
Numbered Discourses 5.210
21. With Kimbila
Unmindful

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, ādīnavā muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa niddaṁ okkamayato.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of falling asleep unmindful and unaware.
What five?

segs.p: Dukkhaṁ supati, dukkhaṁ paṭibujjhati, pāpakaṁ supinaṁ passati, devatā na rakkhanti, asuci muccati.
segs.e: You sleep badly and wake miserably. You have bad dreams. The deities don’t protect you. And you emit semen.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa niddaṁ okkamayato.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of falling asleep unmindful and unaware.

segs.p: Pañcime, bhikkhave, ānisaṁsā upaṭṭhitassatissa sampajānassa niddaṁ okkamayato.
segs.e: There are these five benefits of falling asleep mindful and aware.
What five?

segs.p: Sukhaṁ supati, sukhaṁ paṭibujjhati, na pāpakaṁ supinaṁ passati, devatā rakkhanti, asuci na muccati.
segs.e: You sleep at ease and wake happily. You don’t have bad dreams. The deities protect you. And you don’t emit semen.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā upaṭṭhitassatissa sampajānassa niddaṁ okkamayato”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of falling asleep mindful and aware.”
Numbered Discourses 5.211
22. Abuse
An Abuser

segs.p: “Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkosakaparibhāsako ariyūpavādī sabrahmacārīnaṁ, tassa pañca ādīnavā pāṭikaṅkhā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant who abuses and insults their spiritual companions, denouncing the noble ones, can expect these five drawbacks.
What five?

segs.p: Pārājiko vā hoti chinnaparipantho, aññataraṁ vā saṅkiliṭṭhaṁ āpattiṁ āpajjati, bāḷhaṁ vā rogātaṅkaṁ phusati, sammūḷho kālaṁ karoti, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: They’re expelled, cut off, blocked out; or they commit a corrupt offense; or they contract a severe illness. They feel lost when they die. And when their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkosakaparibhāsako ariyūpavādī sabrahmacārīnaṁ, tassa ime pañca ādīnavā pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who abuses and insults their spiritual companions, denouncing the noble ones, can expect these five drawbacks.”
Numbered Discourses 5.212
22. Abuse
Starting Fights

segs.p: “Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako, tassa pañca ādīnavā pāṭikaṅkhā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant who starts fights, quarrels, disputes, debates, and disciplinary issues in the Saṅgha can expect five drawbacks.
What five?

segs.p: Anadhigataṁ nādhigacchati, adhigatā parihāyati, pāpako kittisaddo abbhuggacchati, sammūḷho kālaṁ karoti, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: They don’t achieve the unachieved. What they have achieved falls away. They get a bad reputation. They feel lost when they die. And when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako, tassa ime pañca ādīnavā pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who starts fights, quarrels, disputes, debates, and disciplinary issues in the Saṅgha can expect these five drawbacks.”
Numbered Discourses 5.213
22. Abuse
Ethics
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks for an unethical person because of their failure in ethics.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, dussīlo sīlavipanno pamādādhikaraṇaṁ mahatiṁ bhogajāniṁ nigacchati.
segs.e: Firstly, an unethical person loses great wealth on account of negligence.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.
segs.e: This is the first drawback.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa pāpako kittisaddo abbhuggacchati.
segs.e: Furthermore, an unethical person gets a bad reputation.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.
segs.e: This is the second drawback.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, dussīlo sīlavipanno yaññadeva parisaṁ upasaṅkamati—yadi khattiyaparisaṁ, yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṁ, yadi gahapatiparisaṁ, yadi samaṇaparisaṁ—avisārado upasaṅkamati maṅkubhūto.
segs.e: Furthermore, an unethical person enters any kind of assembly unconfident and embarrassed, whether it’s an assembly of aristocrats, brahmins, householders, or ascetics.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.
segs.e: This is the third drawback.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, dussīlo sīlavipanno sammūḷho kālaṁ karoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, an unethical person feels lost when they die.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.
segs.e: This is the fourth drawback.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, dussīlo sīlavipanno kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: Furthermore, an unethical person, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.
segs.e: This is the fifth drawback.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks for an unethical person because of their failure in ethics.
There are these five benefits for an ethical person because of their accomplishment in ethics.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, sīlavā sīlasampanno appamādādhikaraṇaṁ mahantaṁ bhogakkhandhaṁ adhigacchati.
segs.e: Firstly, an ethical person gains great wealth on account of diligence.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo ānisaṁso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.
segs.e: This is the first benefit.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sīlavato sīlasampannassa kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchati.
segs.e: Furthermore, an ethical person gets a good reputation.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo ānisaṁso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.
segs.e: This is the second benefit.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sīlavā sīlasampanno yaññadeva parisaṁ upasaṅkamati—yadi khattiyaparisaṁ, yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṁ, yadi gahapatiparisaṁ, yadi samaṇaparisaṁ—visārado upasaṅkamati amaṅkubhūto.
segs.e: Furthermore, an ethical person enters any kind of assembly bold and self-assured, whether it’s an assembly of aristocrats, brahmins, householders, or ascetics.

segs.p: Ayaṁ bhikkhave, tatiyo ānisaṁso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.
segs.e: This is the third benefit.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sīlavā sīlasampanno asammūḷho kālaṁ karoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, an ethical person dies not feeling lost.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho ānisaṁso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.
segs.e: This is the fourth benefit.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sīlavā sīlasampanno kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: Furthermore, when an ethical person’s body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, pañcamo ānisaṁso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.
segs.e: This is the fifth benefit.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā sīlavato sīlasampadāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits for an ethical person because of their accomplishment in ethics.”
Numbered Discourses 5.214
22. Abuse
Someone Who Talks a Lot
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks for an individual who talks a lot.
What five?

segs.p: Musā bhaṇati, pisuṇaṁ bhaṇati, pharusaṁ bhaṇati, samphappalāpaṁ bhaṇati, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, and nonsensical. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā bahubhāṇismiṁ puggale.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks for an individual who talks a lot.
There are these five benefits for an individual who talks thoughtfully.
What five?

segs.p: Na musā bhaṇati, na pisuṇaṁ bhaṇati, na pharusaṁ bhaṇati, na samphappalāpaṁ bhaṇati, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, and nonsensical. When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā mantabhāṇismiṁ puggale”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits for an individual who talks thoughtfully.”
Numbered Discourses 5.215
22. Abuse
Intolerance (1st)
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of intolerance.
What five?

segs.p: Bahuno janassa appiyo hoti amanāpo, verabahulo ca hoti, vajjabahulo ca, sammūḷho kālaṁ karoti, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: You are disliked and disagreeable to most people. You have lots of enmity and many faults. You feel lost when you die. And when your body breaks up, after death, you’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā akkhantiyā.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks to intolerance.
There are these five benefits of tolerance.
What five?

segs.p: Bahuno janassa piyo hoti manāpo, na verabahulo hoti, na vajjabahulo, asammūḷho kālaṁ karoti, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: You are liked and agreeable to most people. You have little enmity and few faults. You don’t feel lost when you die. And when your body breaks up, after death, you’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā khantiyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of tolerance.”
Numbered Discourses 5.216
22. Abuse
Intolerance (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of intolerance.
What five?

segs.p: Bahuno janassa appiyo hoti amanāpo, luddo ca hoti, vippaṭisārī ca, sammūḷho kālaṁ karoti, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: You are disliked and disagreeable to most people. You’re cruel and remorseful. You feel lost when you die. And when your body breaks up, after death, you’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā akkhantiyā.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks to intolerance.
There are these five benefits of tolerance.
What five?

segs.p: Bahuno janassa piyo hoti manāpo, aluddo ca hoti, avippaṭisārī ca, asammūḷho kālaṁ karoti, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: You are liked and agreeable to most people. You’re neither cruel nor remorseful. You don’t feel lost when you die. And when your body breaks up, after death, you’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā khantiyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of tolerance.”
Numbered Discourses 5.217
22. Abuse
Unimpressive Conduct (1st)
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of unimpressive conduct.
What five?
You blame yourself.
After examination, sensible people criticize you.
You get a bad reputation.
You feel lost when you die.

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: And when your body breaks up, after death, you’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā apāsādike.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of unimpressive conduct.
There are these five benefits of impressive conduct.
What five?
You don’t blame yourself.
After examination, sensible people praise you.
You get a good reputation.
You don’t feel lost when you die.

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: And when the body breaks up, after death, you’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā pāsādike”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of impressive conduct.”
Numbered Discourses 5.218
22. Abuse
Unimpressive Conduct (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of unimpressive conduct.
What five?

segs.p: Appasannā nappasīdanti, pasannānañca ekaccānaṁ aññathattaṁ hoti, satthusāsanaṁ akataṁ hoti, pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjati, cittamassa nappasīdati.
segs.e: You don’t inspire confidence in those without it. You cause some with confidence to change their minds. You don’t follow the Teacher’s instructions. Those who come after you follow your example. And your mind doesn’t become clear.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā apāsādike.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of unimpressive conduct.
There are these five benefits of impressive conduct.
What five?

segs.p: Appasannā pasīdanti, pasannānañca bhiyyobhāvo hoti, satthusāsanaṁ kataṁ hoti, pacchimā janatā diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjati, cittamassa pasīdati.
segs.e: You inspire confidence in those without it. You increase confidence in those who have it. You follow the Teacher’s instructions. Those who come after you follow your example. And your mind becomes clear.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā pāsādike”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of impressive conduct.”
Numbered Discourses 5.219
22. Abuse
Fire
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of a fire.
What five?

segs.p: Acakkhusso, dubbaṇṇakaraṇo, dubbalakaraṇo, saṅgaṇikāpavaḍḍhano, tiracchānakathāpavattaniko hoti.
segs.e: It’s bad for your eyes. It’s bad for your complexion. It makes you weak. It draws in groups. And it encourages low talk.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā aggismin”ti.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of a fire.”
Numbered Discourses 5.220
22. Abuse
About Madhurā
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of Madhurā.
What five?
The ground is uneven and dusty, the hounds are fierce, the native spirits are vicious, and it’s hard to get almsfood.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā madhurāyan”ti.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of Madhurā.”
Numbered Discourses 5.221
23. Long Wandering
Long Wandering (1st)

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, ādīnavā dīghacārikaṁ anavatthacārikaṁ anuyuttassa viharato.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks for someone who likes long and aimless wandering.
What five?

segs.p: Assutaṁ na suṇāti, sutaṁ na pariyodāpeti, sutenekaccena avisārado hoti, gāḷhaṁ rogātaṅkaṁ phusati, na ca mittavā hoti.
segs.e: You don’t learn new things. You don’t clarify what you’ve learned. You lack confidence in some things you have learned. You contract a severe illness. You don’t have any friends.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā dīghacārikaṁ anavatthacārikaṁ anuyuttassa viharato.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks for someone who likes long and aimless wandering.
There are these five benefits of a reasonable amount of wandering.
What five?

segs.p: Assutaṁ suṇāti, sutaṁ pariyodāpeti, sutenekaccena visārado hoti, na gāḷhaṁ rogātaṅkaṁ phusati, mittavā ca hoti.
segs.e: You learn new things. You clarify what you’ve learned. You have confidence in some things you have learned. You don’t contract severe illness. You have friends.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā samavatthacāre”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of a reasonable amount of wandering.”
Numbered Discourses 5.222
23. Long Wandering
Long Wandering (2nd)

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, ādīnavā dīghacārikaṁ anavatthacārikaṁ anuyuttassa viharato.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks for someone who likes long and aimless wandering.
What five?

segs.p: Anadhigataṁ nādhigacchati, adhigatā parihāyati, adhigatenekaccena avisārado hoti, gāḷhaṁ rogātaṅkaṁ phusati, na ca mittavā hoti.
segs.e: You don’t achieve the unachieved. What you have achieved falls away. You lose confidence in some things you’ve achieved. You contract a severe illness. You don’t have any friends.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā dīghacārikaṁ anavatthacārikaṁ anuyuttassa viharato.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks for someone who likes long and aimless wandering.
There are these five benefits of a reasonable amount of wandering.
What five?

segs.p: Anadhigataṁ adhigacchati, adhigatā na parihāyati, adhigatenekaccena visārado hoti, na gāḷhaṁ rogātaṅkaṁ phusati, mittavā ca hoti.
segs.e: You achieve the unachieved. What you have achieved doesn’t fall away. You’re confident in some things you’ve achieved. You don’t contract severe illness. You have friends.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā samavatthacāre”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of a reasonable amount of wandering.”
Numbered Discourses 5.223
23. Long Wandering
Overstaying
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of overstaying.
What five?

segs.p: Bahubhaṇḍo hoti bahubhaṇḍasannicayo, bahubhesajjo hoti bahubhesajjasannicayo, bahukicco hoti bahukaraṇīyo byatto kiṅkaraṇīyesu, saṁsaṭṭho viharati gahaṭṭhapabbajitehi ananulomikena gihisaṁsaggena, tamhā ca āvāsā pakkamanto sāpekkho pakkamati.
segs.e: You have a lot of stuff and store it up. You have a lot of medicine and store it up. You have a lot of duties and responsibilities, and become capable in whatever needs to be done. You mix closely with laypeople and renunciates, socializing inappropriately like a layperson. And when you leave that monastery, you miss it.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā atinivāse.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of overstaying.
There are these five benefits of staying for a reasonable length of time.
What five?

segs.p: Na bahubhaṇḍo hoti na bahubhaṇḍasannicayo, na bahubhesajjo hoti na bahubhesajjasannicayo, na bahukicco hoti na bahukaraṇīyo na byatto kiṅkaraṇīyesu, asaṁsaṭṭho viharati gahaṭṭhapabbajitehi ananulomikena gihisaṁsaggena, tamhā ca āvāsā pakkamanto anapekkho pakkamati.
segs.e: You don’t have a lot of stuff and store it up. You don’t have a lot of medicine and store it up. You don’t have a lot of duties and responsibilities, or become capable in whatever needs to be done. You don’t mix closely with laypeople and renunciates, socializing inappropriately like a layperson. And when you leave that monastery, you don’t miss it.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā samavatthavāse”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of staying for a reasonable length of time.”
Numbered Discourses 5.224
23. Long Wandering
Stingy
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of overstaying.
What five?

segs.p: Āvāsamaccharī hoti, kulamaccharī hoti, lābhamaccharī hoti, vaṇṇamaccharī hoti, dhammamaccharī hoti.
segs.e: You become stingy with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā atinivāse.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of overstaying.
There are these five benefits of staying for a reasonable length of time.
What five?

segs.p: Na āvāsamaccharī hoti, na kulamaccharī hoti, na lābhamaccharī hoti, na vaṇṇamaccharī hoti, na dhammamaccharī hoti.
segs.e: You’re not stingy with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā samavatthavāse”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of staying for a reasonable length of time.”
Numbered Discourses 5.225
23. Long Wandering
Visiting Families (1st)
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of visiting families.
What five?

segs.p: Anāmantacāre āpajjati, raho nisajjāya āpajjati, paṭicchanne āsane āpajjati, mātugāmassa uttari chappañcavācāhi dhammaṁ desento āpajjati, kāmasaṅkappabahulo viharati.
segs.e: You fall into an offense for wandering without leave. You fall into an offense for sitting in a private place with someone of the opposite sex. You fall into an offense for sitting in a hidden place with someone of the opposite sex. You fall into an offense for teaching more than five or six sentences to someone of the opposite sex. You have a lot of sensual thoughts.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā kulūpake”ti.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of visiting families.”
Numbered Discourses 5.226
23. Long Wandering
Visiting Families (2nd)

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, ādīnavā kulūpakassa bhikkhuno ativelaṁ kulesu saṁsaṭṭhassa viharato.
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks for a mendicant who visits families for too long, mixing closely with them.
What five?
You often see members of the opposite sex.
Seeing them, you become close.
Being so close, you become familiar.
Being familiar, lust overcomes you.

segs.p: otiṇṇacittassetaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ: ‘anabhirato vā brahmacariyaṁ carissati aññataraṁ vā saṅkiliṭṭhaṁ āpattiṁ āpajjissati sikkhaṁ vā paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissati’.
segs.e: When your mind is swamped by lust, you can expect that you will lead the spiritual life dissatisfied, or commit one of the corrupt offenses, or resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā kulūpakassa bhikkhuno ativelaṁ kulesu saṁsaṭṭhassa viharato”ti.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks for a mendicant who visits families for too long, mixing closely with them.”
Numbered Discourses 5.227
23. Long Wandering
Riches
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of riches.
What five?

segs.p: Aggisādhāraṇā bhogā, udakasādhāraṇā bhogā, rājasādhāraṇā bhogā, corasādhāraṇā bhogā, appiyehi dāyādehi sādhāraṇā bhogā.
segs.e: Fire, water, kings, thieves, and unloved heirs all take a share.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā bhogesu.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of riches.
There are these five benefits of riches.
What five?

segs.p: Bhoge nissāya attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti sammā sukhaṁ pariharati, mātāpitaro sukheti pīṇeti sammā sukhaṁ pariharati, puttadāradāsakammakaraporise sukheti pīṇeti sammā sukhaṁ pariharati, mittāmacce sukheti pīṇeti sammā sukhaṁ pariharati, samaṇabrāhmaṇesu uddhaggikaṁ dakkhiṇaṁ patiṭṭhāpeti sovaggikaṁ sukhavipākaṁ saggasaṁvattanikaṁ.
segs.e: Riches enable you to make yourself happy and pleased, to make your mother and father; your children, partners, bondservants, workers, and staff, and your friends and colleagues happy and pleased, and to keep them all happy. And they enable you to establish an uplifting religious donation for ascetics and brahmins that’s conducive to heaven, ripens in happiness, and leads to heaven.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā bhogesū”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of riches.”
Numbered Discourses 5.228
23. Long Wandering
Eating Late
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks for a family who takes their meals late in the day.
What five?

segs.p: Ye te atithī pāhunā, te na kālena paṭipūjenti;
segs.e: When guests visit, they are not served on time.

segs.p: yā tā balipaṭiggāhikā devatā, tā na kālena paṭipūjenti;
segs.e: The deities who accept spirit-offerings are not served on time.

segs.p: ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā ekabhattikā rattūparatā viratā vikālabhojanā, te na kālena paṭipūjenti;
segs.e: Ascetics and brahmins who eat in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night, and from food at the wrong time are not served on time.
Bondservants, workers, and staff do their duties neglectfully.
A meal eaten during the wrong period is not nutritious.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā ussūrabhatte kule.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks for a family who takes their meals late in the day.
There are these five benefits for a family who takes their meals at a proper time.
What five?

segs.p: Ye te atithī pāhunā, te kālena paṭipūjenti;
segs.e: When guests visit, they are served on time.

segs.p: yā tā balipaṭiggāhikā devatā, tā kālena paṭipūjenti;
segs.e: The deities who accept spirit-offerings are served on time.

segs.p: ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā ekabhattikā rattūparatā viratā vikālabhojanā, te kālena paṭipūjenti;
segs.e: Ascetics and brahmins who eat in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night, and from food at the wrong time are served on time.
Bondservants, workers, and staff do their duties attentively.
A meal eaten during the proper period is nutritious.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā samayabhatte kule”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits for a family who takes their meals at a proper time.”
Numbered Discourses 5.229
23. Long Wandering
Black Cobras (1st)
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of a black cobra.
What five?
It’s filthy, stinking, cowardly, frightening, and treacherous.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā kaṇhasappe.
segs.e: These are the five dangers of a black cobra.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcime ādīnavā mātugāme.
segs.e: In the same way there are these five drawbacks of a lady.
What five?
She’s filthy, stinking, cowardly, frightening, and treacherous.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā mātugāme”ti.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of a lady.”
Numbered Discourses 5.230
23. Long Wandering
Black Cobras (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of a black cobra.
What five?
It’s irritable, acrimonious, venomous, fork-tongued, and treacherous.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā kaṇhasappe.
segs.e: These are the five dangers of a black cobra.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcime ādīnavā mātugāme.
segs.e: In the same way there are these five drawbacks of a lady.
What five?
She’s irritable, acrimonious, venomous, fork-tongued, and treacherous.
This is a lady’s venom:
usually she’s very lustful.
This is a lady’s forked tongue:
usually she backbites.
This is a lady’s treachery:
usually she’s an adulteress.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā mātugāme”ti.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of a lady.”
Numbered Discourses 5.231
24. A Resident Mendicant
A Resident Mendicant

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu abhāvanīyo hoti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a resident mendicant with five qualities is not admirable.
What five?
They’re not accomplished in being well-mannered and doing their duties.
They’re not very learned and don’t remember what they’ve learned.
They’re not self-effacing and don’t enjoy self-effacement.
They’re not a good speaker and do not enunciate well.
They’re witless, dull, and idiotic.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu abhāvanīyo hoti.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with these five qualities is not admirable.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu bhāvanīyo hoti.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with these five qualities is admirable.
What five?
They’re accomplished in being well-mannered and doing their duties.
They’re very learned and remember what they’ve learned.
They’re self-effacing and enjoy self-effacement.
They’re a good speaker who enunciates well.
They’re wise, bright, and clever.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu bhāvanīyo hotī”ti.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with these five qualities is admirable.”
Numbered Discourses 5.232
24. A Resident Mendicant
Liked

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo ca.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a resident mendicant with five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.
What five?

segs.p: Sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu;
segs.e: They’re ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā;
segs.e: They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segs.p: kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā;
segs.e: They’re a good speaker who enunciates well, with a polished, clear, and articulate voice that expresses the meaning.

segs.p: catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī;
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.
