segs.p: āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṁ piyo ca hoti manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā”ti.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with these five qualities is dear and beloved to their spiritual companions, respected and admired.”
Numbered Discourses 5.233
24. A Resident Mendicant
Grace

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu āvāsaṁ sobheti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a resident mendicant with five qualities graces the monastery.
What five?
They’re ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s totally full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, reciting them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segs.p: kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā;
segs.e: They’re a good speaker who enunciates well, with a polished, clear, and articulate voice that expresses the meaning.

segs.p: paṭibalo hoti upasaṅkamante dhammiyā kathāya sandassetuṁ samādapetuṁ samuttejetuṁ sampahaṁsetuṁ;
segs.e: They’re able to educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire those who approach them with a Dhamma talk.

segs.p: catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī.
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu āvāsaṁ sobhetī”ti.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with these five qualities graces the monastery.”
Numbered Discourses 5.234
24. A Resident Mendicant
Very Helpful

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu āvāsassa bahūpakāro hoti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a resident mendicant with five qualities is very helpful to the monastery.
What five?
They’re ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

They’re very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s totally full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, reciting them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.
They repair what is decayed and damaged.

segs.p: mahā kho pana bhikkhusaṅgho abhikkanto nānāverajjakā bhikkhū gihīnaṁ upasaṅkamitvā āroceti:
segs.e: When a large mendicant Saṅgha is arriving with mendicants from abroad, they go to the lay people and announce:

segs.p: ‘mahā kho, āvuso, bhikkhusaṅgho abhikkanto nānāverajjakā bhikkhū, karotha puññāni, samayo puññāni kātun’ti;
segs.e: ‘A large mendicant Saṅgha is arriving with mendicants from abroad. Make merit! Now is the time to make merit!’

segs.p: catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī.
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu āvāsassa bahūpakāro hotī”ti.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with these five qualities is very helpful to the monastery.”
Numbered Discourses 5.235
24. A Resident Mendicant
A Sympathetic Mendicant

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu gihīnaṁ anukampati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a resident mendicant with five qualities shows sympathy to the lay people.
What five?
They encourage them in higher ethics.
They equip them to see the truth of the teachings.
When they are sick, they go to them and prompt their mindfulness, saying:
‘Establish your mindfulness, good fellows, in what is worthy.’

segs.p: mahā kho pana bhikkhusaṅgho abhikkanto nānāverajjakā bhikkhū gihīnaṁ upasaṅkamitvā āroceti:
segs.e: When a large mendicant Saṅgha is arriving with mendicants from abroad, they go to the lay people and announce:

segs.p: ‘mahā kho, āvuso, bhikkhusaṅgho abhikkanto nānāverajjakā bhikkhū, karotha puññāni, samayo puññāni kātun’ti;
segs.e: ‘A large mendicant Saṅgha is arriving with mendicants from abroad. Make merit! Now is the time to make merit!’

segs.p: yaṁ kho panassa bhojanaṁ denti lūkhaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā taṁ attanā paribhuñjati, saddhādeyyaṁ na vinipāteti.
segs.e: And they eat whatever food they give them, coarse or fine, not wasting a gift given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu gihīnaṁ anukampatī”ti.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with these five qualities shows sympathy to the lay people.”
Numbered Discourses 5.236
24. A Resident Mendicant
Deserving Criticism (1st)

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a resident mendicant with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?
Without examining or scrutinizing, they praise those deserving of criticism,
and they criticize those deserving of praise.

segs.p: ananuvicca apariyogāhetvā appasādanīye ṭhāne pasādaṁ upadaṁseti;
segs.e: Without examining or scrutinizing, they arouse faith in things that are dubious,

segs.p: ananuvicca apariyogāhetvā pasādanīye ṭhāne appasādaṁ upadaṁseti;
segs.e: and they don’t arouse faith in things that are inspiring.
And they waste a gift given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What five?
After examining and scrutinizing, they criticize those deserving of criticism,
and they praise those deserving of praise.

segs.p: anuvicca pariyogāhetvā appasādanīye ṭhāne appasādaṁ upadaṁseti;
segs.e: They don’t arouse faith in things that are dubious,

segs.p: anuvicca pariyogāhetvā pasādanīye ṭhāne pasādaṁ upadaṁseti;
segs.e: and they do arouse faith in things that are inspiring.
And they don’t waste a gift given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.237
24. A Resident Mendicant
Deserving Criticism (2nd)

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a resident mendicant with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?
Without examining or scrutinizing, they praise those deserving of criticism,
and they criticize those deserving of praise.
They’re stingy and avaricious regarding monasteries.
They’re stingy and avaricious regarding families.
And they waste a gift given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What five?
After examining and scrutinizing, they criticize those deserving of criticism,
and they praise those deserving of praise.
They’re not stingy and avaricious regarding monasteries.
They’re not stingy and avaricious regarding families.
And they don’t waste a gift given in faith.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato āvāsiko bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: A resident mendicant with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”

Numbered Discourses 5.241
25. Bad Conduct
Bad Conduct (1st)
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of bad conduct.
What five?
You blame yourself.
After examination, sensible people criticize you.
You get a bad reputation.
You feel lost when you die.

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: And when your body breaks up, after death, you’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā duccarite.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of bad conduct.
There are these five benefits of good conduct.
What five?
You don’t blame yourself.
After examination, sensible people praise you.
You get a good reputation.
You don’t feel lost when you die.

segs.p: kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When your body breaks up, after death, you’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā sucarite”ti.
segs.e: These are the five benefits of good conduct.”

25. Bad Conduct
A Charnel Ground
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks to a charnel ground.
What five?

segs.p: Asuci, duggandhā, sappaṭibhayā, vāḷānaṁ amanussānaṁ āvāso, bahuno janassa ārodanā—
segs.e: It’s filthy, stinking, frightening, a gathering place for savage monsters, and a weeping place for many people.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā sivathikāya.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of a charnel ground.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcime ādīnavā sivathikūpame puggale.
segs.e: In the same way there are five drawbacks of an individual like a charnel ground.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo asucinā kāyakammena samannāgato hoti;
segs.e: To start with, an individual has filthy conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.
This is how they’re filthy, I say.
That individual is just as filthy as a charnel ground.

segs.p: Tassa asucinā kāyakammena samannāgatassa, asucinā vacīkammena samannāgatassa, asucinā manokammena samannāgatassa pāpako kittisaddo abbhuggacchati.
segs.e: Because of their filthy conduct, they get a bad reputation.
This is how they’re stinky, I say.
That individual is just as stinky as a charnel ground.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ asucinā kāyakammena samannāgataṁ, asucinā vacīkammena samannāgataṁ, asucinā manokammena samannāgataṁ pesalā sabrahmacārī ārakā parivajjanti.
segs.e: Because of their filthy conduct, good-hearted spiritual companions avoid them from afar.
That’s how they’re frightening, I say.
That individual is just as frightening as a charnel ground.

segs.p: So asucinā kāyakammena samannāgato, asucinā vacīkammena samannāgato, asucinā manokammena samannāgato sabhāgehi puggalehi saddhiṁ saṁvasati.
segs.e: Because of their filthy conduct, they live together with individuals of a similar character.
This is how they gather with savage monsters, I say.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi sā, bhikkhave, sivathikā vāḷānaṁ amanussānaṁ āvāso;
segs.e: That individual is just as much a gathering place of savage monsters as a charnel ground.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ asucinā kāyakammena samannāgataṁ, asucinā vacīkammena samannāgataṁ, asucinā manokammena samannāgataṁ pesalā sabrahmacārī disvā khīyadhammaṁ āpajjanti:
segs.e: Because of their filthy conduct, when good-hearted spiritual companions see them they complain:

segs.p: ‘aho vata no dukkhaṁ ye mayaṁ evarūpehi puggalehi saddhiṁ saṁvasāmā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh, it’s so painful for us to have to live together with such as these.’
This is how there’s weeping, I say.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi sā, bhikkhave, sivathikā bahuno janassa ārodanā;
segs.e: This person is just as much a weeping place for many people as a charnel ground.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā sivathikūpame puggale”ti.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of an individual like a charnel ground.”
Numbered Discourses 5.250
25. Bad Conduct
Faith in Individuals
“Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks of placing faith in an individual.
What five?

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, puggale puggalo abhippasanno hoti, so tathārūpaṁ āpattiṁ āpanno hoti yathārūpāya āpattiyā saṅgho ukkhipati.
segs.e: The individual to whom an individual is devoted falls into an offense such that the Saṅgha suspends them.
It occurs to them:

segs.p: ‘yo kho myāyaṁ puggalo piyo manāpo so saṅghena ukkhitto’ti.
segs.e: ‘This individual dear and beloved to me has been suspended by the Saṅgha.’
They lose much of their faith in mendicants.

segs.p: Bhikkhūsu appasādabahulo samāno aññe bhikkhū na bhajati.
segs.e: So they don’t frequent other mendicants,

segs.p: Aññe bhikkhū abhajanto saddhammaṁ na suṇāti.
segs.e: they don’t hear the true teaching,
and they fall away from the true teaching.
This is the first drawback in placing faith in an individual.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ puggale puggalo abhippasanno hoti, so tathārūpaṁ āpattiṁ āpanno hoti yathārūpāya āpattiyā saṅgho ante nisīdāpeti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the individual to whom an individual is devoted falls into an offense such that the Saṅgha makes them sit at the end of the line. …

segs.p: ‘yo kho myāyaṁ puggalo piyo manāpo so saṅghena ante nisīdāpito’ti.
Bhikkhūsu appasādabahulo samāno aññe bhikkhū na bhajati.
Aññe bhikkhū abhajanto saddhammaṁ na suṇāti.

segs.e: This is the second drawback in placing faith in an individual.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ puggale puggalo abhippasanno hoti, so disāpakkanto hoti …pe… so vibbhanto hoti …pe… so kālaṅkato hoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the individual to whom an individual is devoted leaves for another region … disrobes … passes away.
It occurs to them:

segs.p: ‘yo kho myāyaṁ puggalo piyo manāpo so kālaṅkato’ti.
segs.e: ‘This individual dear and beloved to me has passed away.’
So they don’t frequent other mendicants,

segs.p: Aññe bhikkhū abhajanto saddhammaṁ na suṇāti.
segs.e: they don’t hear the true teaching,
and they fall away from the true teaching.
This is the fifth drawback in placing faith in an individual.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā puggalappasāde”ti.
segs.e: These are the five drawbacks of placing faith in an individual.”
Numbered Discourses 5.251
26. Ordination
Who Should Give Ordination
“Mendicants, ordination should be given by a mendicant with five qualities.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asekhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti;
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who has the entire spectrum of an adept’s ethics,
immersion,
wisdom,
freedom,
and the knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabban”ti.
segs.e: Ordination should be given by a mendicant with these five qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 5.252
26. Ordination
Who Should Give Dependence

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nissayo dātabbo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, dependence should be given by a mendicant with five qualities.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asekhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti …pe… asekhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who has the entire spectrum of an adept’s ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.
Dependence should be given by a mendicant with these five qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 5.253
26. Ordination
Who Should Have a Novice as Attendant

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a novice should attend on a mendicant with five qualities.
What five?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asekhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti; asekhena samādhikkhandhena … asekhena paññākkhandhena … asekhena vimuttikkhandhena … asekhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who has the entire spectrum of an adept’s ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and the knowledge and vision of freedom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo”ti.
segs.e: A novice should attend on a mendicant with these five qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 5.254
26. Ordination
Five Kinds of Stinginess
“Mendicants, there are these five kinds of stinginess.
What five?
Stinginess with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teachings.
These are the five kinds of stinginess.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ macchariyānaṁ etaṁ paṭikuṭṭhaṁ, yadidaṁ dhammamacchariyan”ti.
segs.e: The most contemptible of these five kinds of stinginess is stinginess with the teaching.”
Numbered Discourses 5.255
26. Ordination
Giving Up Stinginess

segs.p: “Pañcannaṁ, bhikkhave, macchariyānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the spiritual life is lived to give up and cut out these five kinds of stinginess.
What five?
Stinginess with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teachings.

segs.p: kulamacchariyassa … lābhamacchariyassa … vaṇṇamacchariyassa … dhammamacchariyassa pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussati.
Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṁ macchariyānaṁ pahānāya samucchedāya brahmacariyaṁ vussatī”ti.
segs.e: The spiritual life is lived to give up and cut out these five kinds of stinginess.”
Numbered Discourses 5.256
26. Ordination
The First Absorption

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up these five qualities you can’t enter and remain in the first absorption.
What five?
Stinginess with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teachings.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhamme appahāya abhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these five qualities you can’t enter and remain in the first absorption.

segs.p: Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: But after giving up these five qualities you can enter and remain in the first absorption.
What five?
Stinginess with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teachings.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhamme pahāya bhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharitun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these five qualities you can enter and remain in the first absorption.”
Numbered Discourses 5.257–263
26. Ordination
The Second Absorption, Etc.

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… abhabbo tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ … abhabbo catutthaṁ jhānaṁ … abhabbo sotāpattiphalaṁ … abhabbo sakadāgāmiphalaṁ … abhabbo anāgāmiphalaṁ … abhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up these five qualities you can’t enter and remain in the second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption … or realize the fruit of stream-entry … the fruit of once-return … the fruit of non-return … perfection.
What five?
Stinginess with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teachings.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhamme appahāya abhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: Without giving up these five qualities you can’t realize perfection.

segs.p: Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… bhabbo tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ … bhabbo catutthaṁ jhānaṁ … bhabbo sotāpattiphalaṁ … bhabbo sakadāgāmiphalaṁ … bhabbo anāgāmiphalaṁ … bhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātuṁ.
segs.e: But after giving up these five qualities you can enter and remain in the second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption … and realize the fruit of stream-entry … the fruit of once-return … the fruit of non-return … perfection.
What five?
Stinginess with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teachings.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhamme pahāya bhabbo arahattaṁ sacchikātun”ti.
segs.e: After giving up these five qualities you can realize perfection.”
Numbered Discourses 5.264
26. Ordination
Another Discourse on the First Absorption

segs.p: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, without giving up these five qualities you can’t enter and remain in the first absorption.
What five?

segs.p: Āvāsamacchariyaṁ, kulamacchariyaṁ, lābhamacchariyaṁ, vaṇṇamacchariyaṁ, akataññutaṁ akataveditaṁ.

Numbered Discourses 5.272
27. Abbreviated Texts on Appointments
A Meal Assigner

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhattuddesako na sammannitabbo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with five qualities should not be appointed as meal assigner.
What five?

segs.p: Chandāgatiṁ gacchati, dosāgatiṁ gacchati, mohāgatiṁ gacchati, bhayāgatiṁ gacchati, uddiṭṭhānuddiṭṭhaṁ na jānāti.
segs.e: They make decisions prejudiced by favoritism, hostility, stupidity, and cowardice. And they don’t know if a meal has been assigned or not.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhattuddesako na sammannitabbo.
segs.e: Someone with these five qualities should not be appointed as meal assigner.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhattuddesako sammannitabbo.
segs.e: Someone with five qualities should be appointed as meal assigner.
What five?

segs.p: Na chandāgatiṁ gacchati, na dosāgatiṁ gacchati, na mohāgatiṁ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṁ gacchati, uddiṭṭhānuddiṭṭhaṁ jānāti.
segs.e: They don’t make decisions prejudiced by favoritism, hostility, stupidity, and cowardice. And they know if a meal has been assigned or not.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhattuddesako sammannitabboti.
segs.e: Someone with these five qualities should be appointed as meal assigner.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhattuddesako sammato na pesetabbo …pe… sammato pesetabbo … bālo veditabbo … paṇḍito veditabbo … khataṁ upahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati … akkhataṁ anupahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati … yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye … yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with five qualities who has been appointed as meal assigner should not be called upon … should be called upon … should be known as a fool … should be known as astute … they keep themselves broken and damaged … they keep themselves unbroken and undamaged … is placed in hell as if delivered there … is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What five?

segs.p: Na chandāgatiṁ gacchati, na dosāgatiṁ gacchati, na mohāgatiṁ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṁ gacchati, uddiṭṭhānuddiṭṭhaṁ jānāti.
segs.e: They don’t make decisions prejudiced by favoritism, hostility, stupidity, and cowardice. And they know if a meal has been assigned or not.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhattuddesako yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: A meal assigner with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.273–285

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato senāsanapaññāpako na sammannitabbo …pe… paññattāpaññattaṁ na jānāti …pe… senāsanapaññāpako sammannitabbo …pe… paññattāpaññattaṁ jānāti …pe….
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with five qualities should not be appointed as lodgings allotter … they don’t know if a lodging has been allotted or not … Someone with five qualities should be appointed as lodgings allotter … they know if a lodging has been allotted or not …

segs.p: Senāsanagāhāpako na sammannitabbo …pe… gahitāgahitaṁ na jānāti …pe… senāsanagāhāpako sammannitabbo …pe… gahitāgahitaṁ jānāti …pe….
segs.e: A person should not be appointed as lodgings allocator … they don’t know if a lodging has been allocated or not … A person should be appointed as lodgings allocator … they know if a lodging has been allocated or not …

segs.p: Bhaṇḍāgāriko na sammannitabbo …pe… guttāguttaṁ na jānāti … bhaṇḍāgāriko sammannitabbo …pe… guttāguttaṁ jānāti ….
segs.e: A person should not be appointed as storeperson … they don’t know if stores are protected or not … A person should be appointed as storeperson … they know if stores are protected or not …

segs.p: Cīvarapaṭiggāhako na sammannitabbo …pe… gahitāgahitaṁ na jānāti … cīvarapaṭiggāhako sammannitabbo …pe… gahitāgahitaṁ jānāti ….
segs.e: … robe receiver …

segs.p: Cīvarabhājako na sammannitabbo …pe… bhājitābhājitaṁ na jānāti … cīvarabhājako sammannitabbo …pe… bhājitābhājitaṁ jānāti ….

… porridge distributor …
… fruit distributor …

segs.p: Khajjakabhājako na sammannitabbo …pe… bhājitābhājitaṁ na jānāti … khajjakabhājako sammannitabbo …pe… bhājitābhājitaṁ jānāti ….

segs.p: Appamattakavissajjako na sammannitabbo …pe… vissajjitāvissajjitaṁ na jānāti … appamattakavissajjako sammannitabbo …pe… vissajjitāvissajjitaṁ jānāti ….
segs.e: … dispenser of minor accessories …

segs.p: Sāṭiyaggāhāpako na sammannitabbo …pe… gahitāgahitaṁ na jānāti … sāṭiyaggāhāpako sammannitabbo …pe… gahitāgahitaṁ jānāti ….
segs.e: … allocator of bathing cloths …

segs.p: Pattaggāhāpako na sammannitabbo …pe… gahitāgahitaṁ na jānāti … pattaggāhāpako sammannitabbo …pe… gahitāgahitaṁ jānāti ….
segs.e: … bowl allocator …
… supervisor of monastery staff …
… supervisor of novices …

segs.p: Sāmaṇerapesako bālo veditabbo …pe… paṇḍito veditabbo … khataṁ upahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati … akkhataṁ anupahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati … yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye … yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.

segs.e: What five?

segs.p: Na chandāgatiṁ gacchati, na dosāgatiṁ gacchati, na mohāgatiṁ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṁ gacchati, pesitāpesitaṁ jānāti.
segs.e: They don’t make decisions prejudiced by favoritism, hostility, stupidity, and cowardice. And they know if a novice has been supervised or not.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato sāmaṇerapesako yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: A supervisor of novices with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.286
28. Abbreviated Texts on Training Rules
A Monk

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a monk with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, abrahmacārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī hoti.
segs.e: He kills living creatures, steals, has sex, lies, and consumes intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: A monk with these five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: A monk with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, abrahmacariyā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: He doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, have sex, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: A monk with these five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.287–292

A Nun

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā bhikkhunī …pe… sikkhamānā … sāmaṇero … sāmaṇerī … upāsako … upāsikā yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “A nun … trainee nun … novice monk … novice nun … layman … laywoman … with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātinī hoti, adinnādāyinī hoti, kāmesumicchācārinī hoti, musāvādinī hoti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyinī hoti.
segs.e: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, and consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatā upāsikā yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: With these five qualities they’re placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā upāsikā yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: A nun … trainee nun … novice monk … novice nun … layman … laywoman … with five qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā hoti, adinnādānā paṭiviratā hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā hoti, musāvādā paṭiviratā hoti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā hoti.
segs.e: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgatā upāsikā yathābhataṁ nikkhittā evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: With these five qualities they’re placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.293

28. Abbreviated Texts on Training Rules
A Jain Ascetic, Etc.

segs.p: “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato nigaṇṭho … muṇḍasāvako … jaṭilako … paribbājako … māgaṇḍiko … tedaṇḍiko … āruddhako … gotamako … devadhammiko yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “A Jain ascetic … disciple of the shavelings … a matted-hair ascetic … a wanderer … a follower of Māgaṇḍiya … a trident-bearing ascetic … a follower of the unobstructed … a follower of Gotama … a performer of rituals for the gods … with five qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What five?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī hoti.
segs.e: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, and consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahi dhammehi samannāgato devadhammiko yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye”ti.
segs.e: With these five qualities they’re placed in hell as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 5.303
29. Abbreviated Texts Beginning With Greed
Untitled Discourse on Greed (1st)
“For insight into greed, five things should be developed.
What five?

segs.p: Asubhasaññā, maraṇasaññā, ādīnavasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā—
segs.e: The perceptions of ugliness, death, drawbacks, repulsiveness of food, and dissatisfaction with the whole world.

segs.p: rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime pañca dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these five things should be developed.”
Numbered Discourses 5.304
29. Abbreviated Texts Beginning With Greed
Untitled Discourse on Greed (2nd)
“For insight into greed, five things should be developed.
What five?

segs.p: Aniccasaññā, anattasaññā, maraṇasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā—
segs.e: The perceptions of impermanence, not-self, death, repulsiveness of food, and dissatisfaction with the whole world.

segs.p: rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime pañca dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these five things should be developed.”
Numbered Discourses 5.305
29. Abbreviated Texts Beginning With Greed
Untitled Discourse on Greed (3rd)
“For insight into greed, five things should be developed.
What five?

segs.p: Aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā—
segs.e: The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of giving up, and the perception of fading away.

segs.p: rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime pañca dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these five things should be developed.”
Numbered Discourses 5.306
29. Abbreviated Texts Beginning With Greed
Untitled Discourse on Greed (4th)
“For insight into greed, five things should be developed.
What five?
The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime pañca dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these five things should be developed.”
Numbered Discourses 5.307
29. Abbreviated Texts Beginning With Greed
Untitled Discourse on Greed (5th)
“For insight into greed, five things should be developed.

The powers of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime pañca dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these five things should be developed.”
Numbered Discourses 5.308–1152
29. Abbreviated Texts Beginning With Greed
Untitled Discourses on Greed, Etc.

segs.p: “Rāgassa, bhikkhave, pariññāya … parikkhayāya … pahānāya … khayāya … vayāya … virāgāya … nirodhāya … cāgāya … paṭinissaggāya pañca dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: “For the complete understanding … finishing … giving up … ending … vanishing … fading away … cessation … giving away … letting go of greed, five things should be developed.”

segs.p: Dosassa … mohassa … kodhassa … upanāhassa … makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa abhiññāya … pariññāya … parikkhayāya … pahānāya … khayāya … vayāya … virāgāya … nirodhāya … cāgāya … paṭinissaggāya pañca dhammā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: “Of hate … delusion … anger … acrimony … disdain … contempt … jealousy … stinginess … deceit … deviousness … obstinacy … aggression … conceit … arrogance … vanity … negligence … for insight … complete understanding … finishing … giving up … ending … vanishing … fading away … cessation … giving away … letting go … five things should be developed.
What five?
The powers of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: pamādassa, bhikkhave, paṭinissaggāya ime pañca dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For the letting go of negligence, these five things should be developed.”
The Book of the Fives is finished.
